  ## (2) Issue body (verbatim)

  ```
  ### User Story

  Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of [#151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151) · Depends on S1, S3

  As a reviewer, I want to select a range of lines and suggest a replacement for all of them so that
  I can propose changes bigger than one line.

  ### User Scenario

  Ana shift-clicks lines 18 to 22 in the Files tab, clicks `+`, then "Suggest change". The block is
  pre-filled with those five lines. She rewrites them as three lines. Ben sees a five-red /
  three-green diff and applies it.

  ### Acceptance Criteria

  *    AC1: Given a reviewer shift-selects a contiguous range of new-side lines in one hunk, when
      they open the comment form, then the comment is anchored to the whole range and the header says
      "Lines 18–22".
  *    AC2: Given a multi-line suggestion, when rendered, then all lines in the range show as
      removed and the block's lines as added (S1 behaviour for a range).
  *    AC3: Given a multi-line suggestion, when applied, then exactly that range is replaced, and it
      is refused as outdated if any line in the range changed (S3 AC3 for a range).
  *    AC4: Given a selection that spans two hunks or both sides of the diff, when the reviewer tries
      to comment, then the selection is refused with a message.
  *    AC5: Given existing single-line comments after the upgrade, when shown and applied, then they
      behave exactly as before (range start = line).

  ### Out of Scope

  *   Ranges across files.

  ### Open Questions

  *   Maximum range length? (Proposed: the hunk's size; no separate cap.)

  ### Design Decision

  **Decision:** Add a `start_line` column to `comment` (0 = single-line, as today) and keep `Line` as
  the range end, so every existing comment is a valid single-line range.

  **Alternatives Considered:**

  *   _Store the range inside the comment body or a JSON column._ No schema change, but the range
      can't be queried or invalidated with the existing code.
  *   _Create one linked comment per line._ Breaks the "one comment, one suggestion" model from S4.

  **Rationale:** `Line` keeps its meaning, so `InvalidateCodeComments`, the API and old rows are
  untouched; only code that cares about ranges reads `start_line`.

  **Consequences:** Migration; `InvalidateCodeComments` should consider the whole range; S7's API
  gains a start-line field.

  ### Scope

  medium

  ### Scope Justification

  DB work
  ```

  *   AC4: two cases in one AC (spans two hunks, spans both sides), and "a message" has no text. Please give the message, or one AC per case.
  *   AC5: testable and good. It covers existing rows after the migration.

  **Cases considered:**

### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of [#151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151) · Depends on S1, S3

As a reviewer, I want to select a range of lines and suggest a replacement for all of them so that
I can propose changes bigger than one line.

### User Scenario

Ana shift-clicks lines 18 to 22 in the Files tab, clicks `+`, then "Suggest change". The block is
pre-filled with those five lines. She rewrites them as three lines. Ben sees a five-red /
three-green diff and applies it.

### Acceptance Criteria

*    AC1: Given a reviewer shift-selects a contiguous range of new-side lines in one hunk, when
    they open the comment form, then the comment is anchored to the whole range and the header says
    "Lines 18–22".
*    AC2: Given a multi-line suggestion, when rendered, then all lines in the range show as
    removed and the block's lines as added (S1 behaviour for a range).
*    AC3: Given a multi-line suggestion, when applied, then exactly that range is replaced, and it
    is refused as outdated if any line in the range changed (S3 AC3 for a range).
*    AC4: Given a selection that spans two hunks or both sides of the diff, when the reviewer tries
    to comment, then the selection is refused with a message.
*    AC5: Given existing single-line comments after the upgrade, when shown and applied, then they
    behave exactly as before (range start = line).

### Out of Scope

*   Ranges across files.

### Open Questions

*   Maximum range length? (Proposed: the hunk's size; no separate cap.)

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Add a `start_line` column to `comment` (0 = single-line, as today) and keep `Line` as
the range end, so every existing comment is a valid single-line range.

**Alternatives Considered:**

*   _Store the range inside the comment body or a JSON column._ No schema change, but the range
    can't be queried or invalidated with the existing code.
*   _Create one linked comment per line._ Breaks the "one comment, one suggestion" model from S4.

**Rationale:** `Line` keeps its meaning, so `InvalidateCodeComments`, the API and old rows are
untouched; only code that cares about ranges reads `start_line`.

**Consequences:** Migration; `InvalidateCodeComments` should consider the whole range; S7's API
gains a start-line field.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

DB work

## (2) Issue body (verbatim)

```
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of [#151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151) · Depends on S1, S3

As a reviewer, I want to select a range of lines and suggest a replacement for all of them so that
I can propose changes bigger than one line.

### User Scenario

Ana shift-clicks lines 18 to 22 in the Files tab, clicks `+`, then "Suggest change". The block is
pre-filled with those five lines. She rewrites them as three lines. Ben sees a five-red /
three-green diff and applies it.

### Acceptance Criteria

*    AC1: Given a reviewer shift-selects a contiguous range of new-side lines in one hunk, when
    they open the comment form, then the comment is anchored to the whole range and the header says
    "Lines 18–22".
*    AC2: Given a multi-line suggestion, when rendered, then all lines in the range show as
    removed and the block's lines as added (S1 behaviour for a range).
*    AC3: Given a multi-line suggestion, when applied, then exactly that range is replaced, and it
    is refused as outdated if any line in the range changed (S3 AC3 for a range).
*    AC4: Given a selection that spans two hunks or both sides of the diff, when the reviewer tries
    to comment, then the selection is refused with a message.
*    AC5: Given existing single-line comments after the upgrade, when shown and applied, then they
    behave exactly as before (range start = line).

### Out of Scope

*   Ranges across files.

### Open Questions

*   Maximum range length? (Proposed: the hunk's size; no separate cap.)

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Add a `start_line` column to `comment` (0 = single-line, as today) and keep `Line` as
the range end, so every existing comment is a valid single-line range.

**Alternatives Considered:**

*   _Store the range inside the comment body or a JSON column._ No schema change, but the range
    can't be queried or invalidated with the existing code.
*   _Create one linked comment per line._ Breaks the "one comment, one suggestion" model from S4.

**Rationale:** `Line` keeps its meaning, so `InvalidateCodeComments`, the API and old rows are
untouched; only code that cares about ranges reads `start_line`.

**Consequences:** Migration; `InvalidateCodeComments` should consider the whole range; S7's API
gains a start-line field.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

DB work
```

246
247	- **Design Decision (D3):** fill it in once you've picked an approach, before opening the PR. Put
248	  a second decision under another `### Decision 2` heading. If a PR changes the decision, update
249	  the issue body.
250	- **Spec review (D2):** before coding starts, a teammate posts a review comment **on the issue**.
251	  Start it with `Spec reviewed` so it is easy to find. The layout is the reviewer's choice, but the
252	  comment must say what was checked:
253	  1. each acceptance criterion: clear and testable, naming any that aren't;
254	  2. the cases considered (e.g. empty input, errors, permissions) and whether the ACs cover them;
255	  3. whether the scope fits the stated size;
256
257	  and end with an approval, or the problems for the author to fix in the spec. `Looks good!` with
258	  nothing about what was checked does not count. An optional layout:
259
260	  ```markdown
261	  Spec reviewed — @reviewer-username
262
263	  **Acceptance criteria:** <clear and testable? which aren't, and why>
264	  **Cases considered:** <which cases, and whether the ACs cover them>
265	  **Scope:** <does it fit the stated size?>
266	  **Verdict:** Approved | Changes needed: <list>
267	  ```
268
269	## Pull request format
270
271	Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
272	`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:
273
274	1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge. Every code PR links its issue, and
275	   the PR goes on the `Sprint 3` milestone too.
276	2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
277	3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
278	4. **Test Evidence:** required from Sprint 3. It replaces the old "How it was tested" section.
279	   Every behaviour change still needs a new or updated test.
280
281	   ```markdown
282	   ## Test Evidence
283
284	   | Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
285	   |---|---|---|---|
286	   | AC1: ... | ... | ... | ... |
287
288	   **Not tested automatically, and why:** [...]
289
290	   **AI-written tests:** [Which tests were written or modified by AI, and how you checked that their expected values are correct. If none, write "None."]
291	   ```
292
293	   - **One row per acceptance criterion** from the issue; for a bug report, the Expected Behavior.
294	     A PR that changes no product behaviour (e.g. a CI change) writes `N/A` and why.
295	   - **Test(s):** the test name, plus the file if not obvious. For a manual check, write `Manual:`
296	     followed by the steps and what you saw. An AC tested both ways lists both in the same row.
297	   - **Level:** `unit`, `integration`, `E2E` or `manual`.
298	   - **Source of expected value:** `AC`, `issue discussion`, `docs`, `upstream behavior`, or
299	     `other` (explain). **Never the current output of your own code:** a test whose expected value
300	     was copied from what the code returns cannot detect that the code is wrong.
301	   - **Not tested automatically, and why:** only for ACs checked manually only.
302	   - AI may draft this section; the author checks that it is accurate.
303
304	5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status. If CI doesn't run your tests, the commands you ran and
305	   a summary of the results (passed, failed, skipped).
306	6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
307	7. **Tech Debt:** required from Sprint 2. Both fields are required, and `None.` is a valid answer:
308
309	   ```markdown
310	   ## Tech Debt
311
312	   **Introduced:** <shortcuts, workarounds or design compromises this PR makes, and why>
313
314	   **Encountered:** <tech debt that was already there and that you ran into, and how you handled it>
315	   ```
316
317	8. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.
318
319	Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6; tests written or updated
320	appropriately, with the Test Evidence section complete, every AC covered and expected values
321	justified 6; description explains what and why, Tech Debt section present, issue linked 3; CI passes
322	or manual verification documented 3; reviewed with the rubric (including the test evidence row),
323	reviewer comment posted, merged only after an approval on the latest commit 2.
324
325	## Code review rubric
326
327	The reviewer posts this as a **PR comment**, as well as the GitHub review itself. A copy-paste copy
328	is in `.github/code-review-rubric.md`, so keep the two in sync. Pull the branch and test it when you
329	can, say what you checked, and mark each point as required or optional
330	(`docs/community-governance.md`). Score each row against the issue's acceptance criteria. Anything
331	below 7 needs a note saying what would raise it.
332
333	```markdown
334	### Code Review — @reviewer-username
335
336	**Checked:** <what you ran or tried>
337
338	| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
339	| --- | --- | --- |
340	| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
341	| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
342	| Test evidence — does every AC have a test? Are the expected values justified? Which tests did you run locally? | | |
343	| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
344	| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
345	| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
346	| Overall — merge as-is? | | |
347	```
348
349	## Mutation testing (D6)
350
351	A mutation testing tool makes small changes to the code (*mutants*), such as flipping a condition
352	or a boundary value, and runs the tests against each one. If a test fails, the mutant is
353	**killed**. If every test passes, it **survived**: the tests didn't notice the change, which points
354	to a weak or missing test. An **equivalent** mutant behaves exactly like the original code, so no
355	test can kill it. Definitions are in the course Glossary.
356
357	**Which issue:** one of your issues whose PR changes source code and tests (CSCI 535: two, and the
358	small issue may be one of them). A tool is required; mutating code by hand doesn't count.
359
360	| Code changed | Tool |
361	| --- | --- |
362	| Frontend TypeScript (Vitest) | StrykerJS with the Vitest runner |
363	| Go backend | Gremlins or go-mutesting |
364
365	1. Run the tool on the **source files changed by your PR(s)** for that issue, not the whole
366	   project.
367	2. Analyse every surviving mutant: equivalent, or a gap in your tests? If more than 10 survive,
368	   analyse at least 10, starting with lines your PR added or changed.
369	3. Add or strengthen **at least one test that kills a survivor** that revealed a gap, and re-run
370	   the tool to confirm it is killed. If no survivor reveals a gap (all killed or equivalent), say so
371	   and justify it in the surviving-mutants table; that completes this step.
372	4. Answer the three questions in the write-up.
373
374	Files:
375
376	- Write-up: `docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-<github-username>.md`, using the template below.
377	- Reports: machine-readable output of the first run and the re-run, as
378	  `docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<github-username>-before.json` and `-after.json` (`.txt`
379	  for go-mutesting). StrykerJS: add `"json"` to `reporters`. Gremlins: `--output=<file>.json`.
380	  go-mutesting: save the terminal output to a text file. The scores in the write-up must match the
381	  reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in the "after" report.
382	- The tool configuration you used, committed and linked from the write-up. Reusing a teammate's
383	  setup is encouraged, as long as you run the tool yourself and credit them. The team's shared
384	  setup (go-mutesting for Go), its commands and its pitfalls: `.claude-students/docs/mutation-testing.md`.
385
386	Common problems:
387
388	- **The tool stops before mutating.** It first runs the selected tests on unchanged code and stops
389	  if any fail. Fix or exclude them first; the D8 baseline shows which ones fail already.
390	- **Tests run against built code.** Mutants in the source are never seen by tests that run on
391	  compiled output. Configure a rebuild, or pick tests that run on source.
392	- **Tests need services.** Start the database or service first. How each test type runs is in
393	  `.claude-students/docs/testing.md`.
394	- **False survivors.** When limiting which tests run, include the tests that cover the mutated
395	  files. Otherwise mutants they would catch show as survived or not covered. Check that the
396	  relevant tests ran before writing a new test for a survivor.
397	- **Blocked?** Ask teammates first. Then tell the TA **as early as possible**, with the errors and
398	  the AI log of what you tried; the TA may approve a different issue or area. Problems reported at
399	  the end of the sprint don't excuse a missing D6.
400
401	Template, copied from the Sprint 3 page:
402
403	```markdown
404	# Mutation testing: Issue #<N> -- <issue title>
405
406	**PR(s):** #...  **Tool:** ...  **Config:** [link; credit the teammate if you reused their setup]  **Command:** `...`
407	**Reports:** [before](reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json) · [after](reports/<issue#>-<username>-after.json)
408	**Mutation score:** before ...% → after ...%
409
410	## Surviving mutants
411
412	| Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |
413	|---|---|---|---|
414	| | | | |
415
416	## New or strengthened test
417
418	Commit: [link] · Test: [file › test name] · Kills: [mutant location]
419
420	## Questions
421
422	1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?
423	2. Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain.
424	3. If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and what did you verify or correct? If AI was not used, write "N/A."
425	```
426
427	Grading (15 points): tool run on the files changed by the PR, with configuration, command, results
428	and reports committed 4; surviving mutants analysed correctly (equivalent or test gap, with an
429	explanation) 4; at least one new or strengthened test kills a survivor, confirmed by the re-run 4;
430	answers show understanding, not just description 3. CSCI 535: the average of the two write-ups.
431
432	## Sprint report (D8) sections
433
434	`docs/sprint<N>/report.md` (or `.pdf` or `.docx`), following `docs/sprint0/report.md`:
435
436	- Team: names, GitHub usernames, project name, repository link.
437	- Sprint overview.
438	- Backlog: milestone link, why the team chose these issues, plus a table of title, owner, points,
439	  scope and status.
440	- Requirements and design: when specs were done, what surprised you, design rationale.
441	- Completed issues: title, owner, PR link, author, reviewer, what changed.
442	- Test strategy, including untestable changes and why.
443	- AI tool usage per member: tools, session count, AI log folder link, and 2–3 sentences on lessons
444	  learned.
445	- Release: tag and release link.
446	- Risks and retrospective: what worked, what slowed the team down, next-sprint changes.
447	- Next sprint plan: initial ideas and carryover issues.
448	- New in Sprint 3:
449	  - **Suite health** (keep it short). A baseline table of the test suites relevant to the team (the
450	    packages or areas it works on, not the whole repository): for each suite, the command or CI
451	    workflow and the runner's summary line (passed, failed, skipped) at the Sprint 2 tag
452	    `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` and at the end of the sprint. Use CI results where available; locally, run
453	    only the packages you change. Failures are grouped by cause (e.g. environment-specific, already
454	    broken upstream, flaky, caused by our changes), each cause linking one issue that lists the
455	    affected tests. Any test the team's changes broke is fixed by the end of the sprint;
456	    pre-existing failures only need recording and grouping. Every skipped test and disabled CI
457	    check has a linked issue and a reason in a code comment.
458	  - **Mutation testing:** a link to each member's D6 write-up.
459	  - **Hardening issues:** which issues they are and where they came from.
460	  - **Carryovers:** the Sprint 2 issues carried over, and what changed.
461	- The report covers this sprint's work only. Write the Sprint 3 sections fresh rather than copying
462	  a previous report, and check that tables and links render on GitHub (no escaped `\|` or `\[`).

464	# AI assistance disclosure — required format
465
466	Course rule, not an upstream Gitea one. Every contributor discloses their own AI use per issue,
467	**even when no AI was used**. Source: the course AI Log Instructions page and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
468	(AI Contribution Policy). Two separate places, both required. The rest of the PR and issue
469	format is in `COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`.
470
471	## 1. A comment on the issue
472
473	Posted by each contributor on the **issue** they worked, once their work is done. One comment per
474	person — never edit someone else's. Add later sessions by editing your own table.
475
476	```markdown
477	### AI Assistance — @your-github-username
478
479	**Role in this issue:** Implementation
480
481	| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
482	|---|---|---|---|
483	| 1 | claude-code | [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md) | Confirmed the files found during concept location, drafted the template change and tests, ran them |
484
485	**Attachments:** [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl/](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/tree/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl)
486	```
487
488	- **Role** is one of Implementation, Code review, Testing, Other — pick the ones that apply and
489	  delete the rest, do not leave the slash list in place.
490	- **Tool** is the tool's name, e.g. `claude-code`, `claude-web`.
491	- **Log** is a full `https://github.com/...` link to the filed log. Relative paths break in issue
492	  comments. File naming is in `ai-logs/README.md`.
493	- **Attachments** only when the log has a companion folder; otherwise drop the line.
494	- **No AI used?** Keep the heading and role line and write `No AI used` in place of the table.
495
496	## 2. A short section in the pull request description — no log link
497
498	Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
499	used and how you verified it. It does **not** link or cite the AI log: from Sprint 1 on, the team
500	references logs in **issue comments only**, never in PR descriptions or PR comments (Sprint 1 page,
501	D5; later sprint pages also accept the PR, and the issue comment satisfies both).
502
503	```markdown
504	## AI assistance
505
506	Claude Code (claude-opus-5) drafted the handler and tests following the existing register/delete
507	code; I reviewed every line, ran the tests, checked the page by hand, and can explain each change.
508	AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on the linked issue.
509	```
510
511	Name the model, say what AI did and what you did, and point at the issue comment for the log. The
512	PR's Test Evidence section has its own **AI-written tests** line, which names the tests AI wrote or
513	changed and how you checked their expected values (`COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`, "Pull request format").
514
515	## Rules that make a disclosure wrong
516
517	- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
518	  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
519	- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.
520	- **A log link that 404s.** Until the log is merged to `main`, link the branch that holds it; switch
521	  to the `main` link once merged.
522	- **A log folder that is not your GitHub username** — `ai-logs/sprint1/jdonohue/` is wrong when the
523	  account is `Jack-Donohue`.
524	- **Claiming work AI did as your own, or the reverse.** The claim must match the log.
525	- **AI-written replies to reviewer questions on your own issue or PR.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` forbids it:
526	  the questions are for you.
527

529
530	Put section 2 in every PR description you draft, and draft the section 1 issue comment
531	separately, both filled in from the session you actually ran — never with placeholders. You may
532	draft the wording, but say plainly that the human must review and edit it before posting, and leave
533	the issue comment for them to post under their own account.

# models/issues — issues, pull requests, comments, reviews

**Read when:** querying or changing issue, PR, comment, label, milestone or review rows.
**Not here:** the business logic on top -> `services/issue` and `services/pull`; project boards -> `models/project`.

## Responsibilities

One package for the whole issue domain, because pull requests *are* issues in this schema.
`models/pull` is separate and tiny: automerge scheduling and per-user review state.

| Area | Files |
| --- | --- |
| Issue core | `issue.go`, `issue_list.go`, `issue_update.go`, `issue_search.go`, `issue_stats.go` |
| Pull requests | `pull.go`, `pull_list.go` |
| Comments | `comment.go`, `comment_list.go`, `comment_code.go`, `content_history.go` |
| Reviews | `review.go`, `review_list.go` |
| Labels / milestones | `issue_label.go`, `label.go`, `milestone.go`, `milestone_list.go` |
| People / time | `assignees.go`, `stopwatch.go`, `tracked_time.go` |
| Relations / state | `dependency.go`, `issue_xref.go`, `issue_watch.go`, `issue_pin.go`, `issue_lock.go`, `issue_user.go`, `issue_project.go`, `reaction.go` |

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `models/issues/issue.go` | `Issue`, `ErrIssueNotExist`, `LoadRepo`, `LoadPullRequest`, `LoadAttributes` |
| `models/issues/issue_list.go` | `IssueList` and its batching `LoadAttributes` |
| `models/issues/pull.go` | `PullRequest`, `PullRequestType`, `PullRequestStatus` |
| `models/issues/comment.go` | `Comment` and the `CommentType` enum |
| `models/issues/dependency.go` | `CreateIssueDependency` refuses a duplicate (`ErrDependencyExists`, unwraps to `util.ErrAlreadyExist`) and a dependency that would close a loop of any length (`ErrCircularDependency`, unwraps to `util.ErrUnprocessableContent`; an issue on itself is a loop of one); `dependencyLoopExists` follows the chain step by step, querying each step in batches of `db.DefaultMaxInSize` (`models/db/list.go`), and skips issues it has seen, so it still ends when it meets a loop saved before the check existed |
| `models/issues/issue_close_reason.go` | `CloseReason` and its names (`String`, `AsCloseReason`), `AllowedCloseReasons`, `BulkCloseReasons` (the list's bulk Close), `DefaultCloseReason`, `CloseReasonOptions.Validate` and its three errors, `CloseReasonOptions.DuplicateIssueID` (the duplicate lookup, shared with the API); stored in `Issue.CloseReason`, `CloseReasonText`, `CloseDuplicateIssueID` |
| `models/issues/issue_label.go` | `LoadLabels` — the idempotency pattern in miniature |
| `models/issues/issue_index.go` | `RecalculateIssueIndexForRepo` |
| `models/issues/issue_group.go` | `IssueLabelGroup`, `IssueList.GroupByExclusiveLabelScope` — the grouped list view |
| `models/issues/milestone_history.go` | `GetMilestoneScopeEvents`, `GetMilestoneStateEvents`, `GetMilestoneItems` — a milestone's past, read back from comments |

## Conventions & invariants

- **One `issue` table holds both issues and pull requests.** `Issue.IsPull` discriminates. The
  PR-only columns live in a separate `PullRequest` row linked by `IssueID` (recipe below). A query
  that forgets `IsPull` returns both kinds.
- `Issue.Index` is the **per-repository** number users see in URLs (`UNIQUE(repo_index)` with
  `RepoID`); `Issue.ID` is the global primary key. Look-ups by URL go through `RepoID` + `Index`.
- Never assign `Index` yourself: `issue_update.go` and `pull.go` take it from
  `db.GetNextResourceIndex(ctx, "issue_index", repo.ID)` inside the inserting transaction.
- Fields tagged `xorm:"-"` (`Repo`, `Poster`, `Labels`, `Milestone`, `Assignee`, `Attachments`,
  `Comments`, `PullRequest`, ...) are in-memory only, filled by the matching `LoadXxx(ctx)` method.
  `LoadAttributes(ctx)` loads the common set.
- `LoadXxx` methods are **idempotent and will not refresh**: each is guarded by an `isXxxLoaded`
  flag, so a second call is free — but a value that changed in the database after the first call
  stays stale on that struct. Re-fetch the issue rather than re-calling the loader.
- Error types come in the three-part shape: `ErrIssueNotExist` struct, `IsErrIssueNotExist(err)`,
  and `Unwrap() error` returning a `modules/util` sentinel such as `util.ErrNotExist`, so
  `errors.Is` works across layers.
- Comment kinds are the `CommentType` iota in `comment.go` (`CommentTypeComment` is a plain
  comment, `CommentTypeReview` a review, plus many state-change kinds). Rendering branches on it —
  adding a value means handling it in the templates too.
- New non-index data on a comment goes in the `Comment.CommentMetaData` JSON field, not a new
  column, as its code comment in `comment.go` says. It is written once at insert and never changed,
  and SQL cannot filter or index on it.
- A close reason leaves the server as its name, never its stored number: `CloseReason.String` and
  `AsCloseReason` (`models/issues/issue_close_reason.go`) convert both ways, as `CommentType.String`
  and `AsCommentType` do. Forms and pages send the name, so a name is as fixed as the number.
- A close comment snapshots the issue's reason in `CommentMetaData`. Read it with
  `Comment.MetaCloseReason()` (`models/issues/comment.go`), which returns no reason when the comment has no metadata, as every
  close comment written before the columns existed does.
- A close as duplicate takes the target's per-repository number; `SetIssueAsClosed` (`models/issues/issue_update.go`) resolves it
  with `GetIssueByIndex` in the issue's own repository and stores the global ID.
  `Comment.LoadCloseDuplicateIssue` loads the target with its repository; a deleted target returns
  `ErrIssueNotExist`. Reopening (`setIssueAsReopen`, the only code that reopens) clears the issue's
  reason, text and target; the close comment keeps its snapshot.

## Recipes

**Load a list of issues for display.** Fetch into an `IssueList`, then call
`issues.LoadAttributes(ctx)` once. Calling `issue.LoadAttributes(ctx)` in a loop is the N+1 this
type exists to prevent.

**Add a column to `Issue`.** Add the field with its xorm tag, add a migration
(`models-migrations.md`), and if it is denormalised from elsewhere, extend the consistency check in
`models/main_test.go` and the fixtures (`testing.md`).
Each new column also lowers `db.MaxBatchInsertSize` (`models/db/engine.go`, 999 divided by the column
count), which `services/migrations/migrate.go` uses as the issue page size. The recorded response in
`tests/integration/_mock_data/Test_MigrateFromGiteaToGitea/` is named after that `limit`, so rename it
to the new value or `Test_MigrateFromGiteaToGitea` fails with "missing fixture".

**Find a PR from an issue.** `issue.LoadPullRequest(ctx)`, then `issue.PullRequest`. From the other
direction, `pr.Issue` after the PR's own loader.

## Gotchas

- Counter columns on `Repository` (`NumIssues`, `NumClosedIssues`, `NumPulls`, ...) are
  denormalised. Changing issue state means keeping them in step, and fixture rows must match or
  `unittest.CheckConsistencyFor` fails.
- `Issue.Index` and `PullRequest.Index` are both present. They agree, but write through the issue.
- `Issue.Link()` dereferences `issue.Repo`, so an issue fetched with `GetIssueByID` panics there
  until `LoadRepo(ctx)` has run.
- A milestone's history exists only as `CommentTypeMilestone` comments (`OldMilestoneID` to
  `MilestoneID`): migrated issues have none and `DeleteMilestoneByRepoID` writes none. Those columns
  are unindexed and `comment` has no `repo_id`, so `milestone_history.go` joins `issue`. Milestone
  counters (`UpdateMilestoneCounters`) count pull requests as well as issues.
- `models/pull` holds no pull requests; they are in `models/issues/pull.go` (see Responsibilities).
- `GroupByExclusiveLabelScope` and `applyGroupByLabelScope` (`models/issues/issue_search.go`, driven
  by `IssuesOptions.GroupLabelScope`) derive the same groups twice — once in SQL to keep a page's
  rows contiguous, once in Go to split that page. Their ordering rules must stay identical, and
  both tie-break on `label.id`, never `label.name`: SQL collation does not match Go's string
  comparison, so a name tie-break silently disagrees across a page boundary.
- Lists filter through `applyConditions` (`models/issues/issue_search.go`), but `GetIssueStats` and
  `GetIssueTotalTrackedTime` use `applyIssuesOptions` (`models/issues/issue_stats.go`), so a new
  `IssuesOptions` filter goes in both or the Open/Closed counts ignore it. "No deadline" is
  `deadline_unix` 0 or NULL: the column has no default and fixture rows omit it.

## Related

- `models-db.md` — transactions and `GetNextResourceIndex`
- `models-repo-and-git.md` — the counter columns and repo units that gate issues

verified-at: 773c614f56

# models/migrations — versioned schema changes

**Read when:** you changed a persisted struct under `models/`, or a migration test fails.
**Not here:** the runtime engine -> `models-db.md`; running the suite -> `testing.md`.

## Responsibilities

An ordered, append-only list of schema migrations. Each has an integer id; the database records how
far it has got, and startup applies whatever is missing. `services/versioned_migration` is what
invokes this at boot.

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `models/migrations/migrations.go` | the ordered slice, `newMigration`, `minDBVersion`, `Migrate`, `EnsureUpToDate`, `GetCurrentDBVersion`, `ExpectedDBVersion` |
| `models/migrations/v1_27/v343.go` | a minimal add-columns migration — the shape to copy |
| `models/migrations/base/db.go` | `RecreateTable`, `RecreateTables`, `DropTableColumns`, `ModifyColumn` |
| `models/migrations/migrationtest/tests.go` | `PrepareTestEnv`, `MainTest` for migration tests |
| `models/migrations/fixtures/Test_<FuncName>/` | per-test fixture directory, named after the test |

## Conventions & invariants

- A migration is one `newMigration(<id>, "<description>", v1_27.FuncName)` entry **appended at the
  bottom** of the slice in `migrations.go`. Order is the schema history; never insert in the
  middle, never renumber.
- The implementation lives in the current version subpackage as `v<id>.go` — migration 342 is
  `models/migrations/v1_27/v342.go` — with the function exported and named for what it does.
- Signature is `func(x db.EngineMigration) error`, or with a leading `context.Context` when the
  migration needs one. `newMigration` accepts either.
- The database version is *the last migration's id + 1*. `minDBVersion` is 70 (Gitea 1.5.3):
  installs older than that must upgrade through an intermediate release first.
- **A migration declares its own local copy of every struct it touches, inside the function**, with
  only the columns it cares about. `v342.go` declares a local `ActionRun` holding just the three
  new columns. Never import the live model from `models/` — the model keeps evolving, and a
  migration must describe the schema *as of its own moment* forever.
- Partial table changes use `x.SyncWithOptions(xorm.SyncOptions{IgnoreDropIndices: true,
  IgnoreConstrains: true}, new(Foo))` rather than plain `Sync`, so unrelated indices and
  constraints survive (`docs/guidelines-backend.md`).
- A column added to an existing table takes `NOT NULL DEFAULT <value>`
  (`models/migrations/v1_27/v343.go`): the default fills existing rows in the same `ALTER TABLE`.
  Without it the column is nullable and old rows hold NULL (`models/migrations/v1_27/v332.go`),
  which `WHERE col = 0` does not match. `NOT NULL` with no default fails on a populated table.
- New `.go` files carry a copyright header with the current year (`AGENTS.md`).

## Recipes

**Add a migration.**

1. Change the real struct in its `models/<domain>/` package.
2. Create `models/migrations/v1_27/v<next id>.go` with an exported function and a local struct copy
   holding only the affected columns.
3. Append `newMigration(<next id>, "<description>", v1_27.FuncName)` to the bottom of the slice in
   `migrations.go`.
4. Add `v<next id>_test.go` beside it, using `migrationtest.PrepareTestEnv`; put any fixtures in
   `models/migrations/fixtures/Test_<FuncName>/`.
5. `make test-migration`.

**Change a column type or drop columns.** Use `base.ModifyColumn` or `base.DropTableColumns` rather
than raw SQL — they handle the per-driver differences. `base.RecreateTable` is the last resort for
changes some drivers cannot express.

## Gotchas

- **Never edit a migration that has shipped.** Installs that already ran it will not run it again,
  so the edit silently applies to new installs only and the two diverge. Add a new migration.
- Registering a model with `db.RegisterModel` creates the table on a *fresh* install only. Existing
  installs need the migration — this is the most common way a change works locally and breaks on
  upgrade.
- Migration tests use their own harness (`migrationtest`), not `models/unittest`. The fixture
  directory name must match the test function name exactly or no fixtures load.
- `migrationtest` loads fixtures through `models/unittest/fixtures_loader.go` → `NewFixturesLoader`,
  which skips, without an error, any table whose model is not registered. Blank-import the owning
  package and assert the row count, as `models/migrations/v1_27/v343_test.go` does.
- `make test-migration` is a separate target from `make test-backend`; a migration can be broken
  while the backend suite is green.
- `go test ./models/...` runs the migration packages in parallel, but they share one repository
  directory (`models/migrations/migrationtest/tests.go` → `PrepareTestEnv`), so old tests fail at
  random with missing-directory errors. `make migrations.individual.test` runs them with `-p 1`.

## Related

- `models-db.md` — `db.RegisterModel` and the engine
- `testing.md` — the other four test tiers

# services/pull and services/gitdiff — pull requests, review, diffs

**Read when:** touching PR creation, mergeability, merging, code review comments, or the diff
viewer.
**Not here:** the `PullRequest` row -> `models-issues.md`; issue-side logic -> `services-issue.md`.

## Responsibilities

| Package | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `services/pull` | PR lifecycle: create, mergeability checking, merge, review, code comments, branch protection enforcement |
| `services/gitdiff` | parsing a git patch into the structures the diff viewer renders |
| `services/automerge`, `services/automergequeue` | "merge when checks pass" |
| `services/agit` | AGit flow — creating a PR by pushing a magic ref |

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `services/pull/pull.go` | `NewPullRequest`, `ChangeTargetBranch`, `AddTestPullRequestTask`, `PushToBaseRepo`, `UpdateRef` |
| `services/pull/merge.go` | `Merge`, `SetMerged`, `MergedManually`, `IsUserAllowedToMerge`, `CheckPullBranchProtections`, `GetDefaultMergeMessage` |
| `services/pull/merge_merge.go`, `merge_squash.go`, `merge_rebase.go`, `merge_ff_only.go` | one file per merge style |
| `services/pull/check.go` | the mergeability queue: `AddPullRequestToCheckQueue`, `InitializePullRequests` |
| `services/pull/merge_tree.go` | conflict detection via `git merge-tree` |
| `services/pull/temp_repo.go` | `createTemporaryRepoForPR` — the scratch clone merges run in |
| `services/pull/patch.go` | `DownloadDiffOrPatch`, `AttemptThreeWayMerge`, `CheckFileProtection` |
| `services/pull/review.go` | `CreateCodeComment`, `SubmitReview`, `DismissReview`, `InvalidateCodeComments` |
| `services/pull/protected_branch.go` | `CreateOrUpdateProtectedBranch` |
| `services/gitdiff/gitdiff.go` | `Diff`, `DiffFile`, `DiffSection`, `DiffLine`, `ParsePatch`, `GetDiffForRender`, `GetDiffForAPI` |
| `services/gitdiff/gitdiff_excerpt.go` | expanding context lines in the viewer |
| `services/gitdiff/highlightdiff.go` | intra-line highlighting |

## Conventions & invariants

- **Mergeability is computed asynchronously.** Nothing recomputes it inline: a change pushes the PR
  id onto the worker queue in `check.go` via `AddPullRequestToCheckQueue`, and the result is
  written back to `PullRequest.Status`. The queue is unique-keyed, so pushing the same id twice is
  free. Code that needs a fresh answer must handle "not computed yet" rather than blocking.
- Merges do not run in the live repository. `createTemporaryRepoForPR` builds a scratch clone and
  the merge-style files operate there; only on success is the result pushed. A merge path that
  writes to the real repo directly is a bug.
- Merge styles are `repo_model.MergeStyle` values (`MergeStyleMerge`, `MergeStyleRebase`,
  `MergeStyleRebaseMerge`, `MergeStyleSquash`, `MergeStyleFastForwardOnly`) and each must be
  allowed by the repo's PR unit config — check with the unit accessors
  (`models-repo-and-git.md`), never by string comparison.
- `Merge` is not the permission check. `IsUserAllowedToMerge` and `CheckPullBranchProtections` sit
  beside it in `merge.go` but are separate calls the caller must make itself.
- **Merging and closing judge dependencies differently.** `CheckPullMergeable`
  (`services/pull/check.go`), which the web, API and automerge paths all call, returns
  `ErrDependenciesLeft` while `MergeBlockedByDependencies` (`models/issues/dependency.go`) finds an
  open issue or an unmerged pull request, and skips that check when `IsDependenciesEnabled` is off.
  `GetMergeBlockingDependencies` (`models/issues/dependency.go`) lists the same ones for the merge
  box (`routers/web/repo/pull_merge_box.go`): both use `mergeBlockingDependencyCond`, so the page and
  the check cannot disagree.
  Closing (`SetIssueAsClosed`, `models/issues/issue_update.go`) skips dependencies the same way and
  otherwise uses `IssueNoDependenciesLeft`, where a closed pull request counts as done. Changing one
  rule does not change the other.
- **Review comments are anchored to a commit, not to a line of the current head.** `CreateCodeComment`
  takes `latestCommitID` and a `treePath`; when the branch moves, `InvalidateCodeComments` marks
  the ones that no longer apply. A comment feature that stores only a line number will drift.
- `GetDiffForRender` and `GetDiffForAPI` are deliberately separate — the render path carries
  highlighting, escaping and a repo link for building URLs. Do not use the API one to build HTML.
- `notify_service.*` is called after the transaction, exactly as in `services-issue.md`.

## Recipes

**Add something to the diff viewer.** Extend `DiffFile`/`DiffSection`/`DiffLine` in
`services/gitdiff/gitdiff.go`, populate it in `ParsePatch` or `GetDiffForRender`, then render it in
the repo diff templates and wire the frontend behaviour (`frontend-js.md`).

**Add a merge style.** A `MergeStyle` constant and its unit-config flag in `models/repo`, a
`merge_<style>.go` implementation, a branch in `Merge`, the repo settings UI, and the locale keys.

**Change when a PR becomes mergeable.** The check itself is in `check.go` / `merge_tree.go`. Add
the trigger by calling `AddPullRequestToCheckQueue`, not by computing inline.

## Gotchas

- `services/pull` is the logic; the `PullRequest` *rows* are in `models/issues/pull.go`. The
  package named `models/pull` is only automerge and review state (`models-issues.md`).
- A PR's issue fields (title, labels, comments) go through `services/issue`. Only PR-specific
  behaviour lives here, so a "PR change" often touches both packages.
- `AddTestPullRequestTask` reads as a test helper. It is production code that queues PR rechecks
  after a push.
- Diff size is capped by the `maxLines` / `maxFiles` arguments to `ParsePatch`; a large diff is
  truncated rather than failing, so check the `Diff` flags before assuming completeness.

# web_src/js — page features and how they get wired up

**Read when:** adding or changing browser behaviour on a page.
**Not here:** Vue components -> `frontend-vue-components.md`; styling -> `frontend-css.md`; the HTML -> `templates.md`.

## Responsibilities

| Directory | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `features/` | one file per page or feature (`repo-issue.ts`, `repo-diff.ts`, `repo-code.ts`), plus `features/admin/` and `features/comp/` for shared widgets |
| `modules/` | cross-cutting infrastructure: `fetch.ts`, `init.ts`, `observer.ts`, `i18n.ts`, `toast.ts`, `tippy.ts`, `fomantic.ts`, `clipboard.ts`, `codeeditor/` |
| `utils/` | pure helpers with no DOM assumptions: `dom.ts`, `html.ts`, `url.ts`, `time.ts`, `color.ts`, `string.ts` |
| `markup/`, `render/` | enhancing already-rendered content (anchors, mermaid, math) |
| `webcomponents/` | custom elements such as `relative-time`, `overflow-menu`, `aria-menu` |

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `web_src/js/index.ts` | the entry point: imports fomantic and `../css/index.css`, then passes every `initXxx` to `callInitFunctions` |
| `web_src/js/modules/init.ts` | `callInitFunctions`, `InitPerformanceTracer` |
| `web_src/js/modules/observer.ts` | `registerGlobalInitFunc`, `registerGlobalEventFunc`, `registerGlobalSelectorFunc`, `initGlobalSelectorObserver` |
| `web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts` | `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` |
| `web_src/js/utils/dom.ts` | `showElem`, `hideElem`, `toggleElem`, `queryElems`, `createElementFromHTML` |
| `web_src/js/modules/i18n.ts` | `trN` — the frontend side of the locale system |
| `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts` | `registerShortcut` (keys like `'g c'`), `getShortcuts`, and the `<kbd data-shortcut-keys data-shortcut-section>` hints and `onShortcutLink` links that register themselves |

## Conventions & invariants

**Two ways to wire a feature, and new code should prefer the second.**

1. *Page-load init:* export `initFoo()` from a `features/` file and add it to the array in
   `index.ts`. Every function in that array runs on **every** page, so it must find its elements
   and return immediately when they are absent.
2. *Declarative:* `registerGlobalInitFunc('initFoo', (el) => {...})` in the module, and
   `data-global-init="initFoo"` on the element in the template. For clicks,
   `registerGlobalEventFunc('click', 'onFoo', ...)` with `data-global-click="onFoo"`. This covers
   elements added to the DOM later and runs once per element (guarded by an internal
   `_giteaGlobalInited` flag), so re-adding a node does not re-initialise it.

`registerGlobalSelectorFunc(selector, handler)` also exists, but `observer.ts` marks it as "less
efficient and less maintainable" — it is for element types already on many pages, not new work.

- **Ordering rule:** every `registerGlobalInitFunc` must run *before* `initGlobalSelectorObserver`,
  which `index.ts` deliberately calls last. Registering after it throws.
- **One function per element.** `callGlobalInitFunc` in `observer.ts` looks the attribute up as a
  whole string, so `data-global-init` names exactly one function — space-separating two is an open
  TODO there, not a feature. To add behaviour to an element that already has one (the new-issue
  title in `templates/repo/issue/new_form.tmpl` carries `autoFocusEnd`), put the attribute on a
  wrapper and query for the inner element.
- Data fetching goes through the `fetch.ts` wrappers, never a raw `fetch`.
- Show and hide with `.tw-hidden` plus `showElem` / `hideElem` / `toggleElem`. In Vue use
  `v-if`/`v-show` instead (`frontend-vue-components.md`).
- Use `node.getAttribute`, not `node.dataset` (camel-casing surprises), and never bind
  user-provided data onto a DOM node.
- Custom DOM events are prefixed `ce-`, declared as an exported constant next to their emitter —
  see `EventEditorContentChanged` in `features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`.
- TypeScript, per `docs/guidelines-frontend.md`: `import type` for type-only imports,
  `@ts-expect-error` over `@ts-ignore`, `!` rather than `?.`/`??` when a value always exists, and
  `async` only on a function that actually awaits.
- One feature per file or directory; ids and classes are kebab-case with 2-3 feature keywords.

## Recipes

**Add behaviour to an element.** Register a global init func in the owning `features/` module and
put `data-global-init="yourFuncName"` on the element in its template. No change to `index.ts`.

**Add a whole-page feature.** New `features/<name>.ts` exporting `initName()`, an early return when
its root element is missing, then add the import and the array entry in `index.ts`.

**Profile a slow page.** `?_ui_performance_trace=1` prints per-init timings; over 500ms is logged.

**Look up an issue by its number.** `matchIssue` (`utils/match.ts`) is the `#` list's search: a
number comes back first (`services/issue/suggestion.go` → `GetSuggestion`), and the current issue
is left out. Keyword matches are limited to the kinds the viewer may read
(`routers/web/repo/issue_suggestions.go`), but the match by number (`GetIssueByIndex`) is not, so a
viewer who can't read pull requests still gets one typed by its number. The duplicate close
reason's preview in `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` uses it.

**Add a keyboard shortcut.** Call `registerShortcut` (`modules/shortcut.ts`). One given an `element` exists while that element
is in the document, hidden or not; a clash with a live one throws. A link can declare one that follows it (`onShortcutLink`,
`templates/repo/header.tmpl`), live while it's rendered; markup rendered twice (navbar icons, `templates/base/head_navbar.tmpl`)
marks one copy. The `?` dialog (`templates/base/footer.tmpl`) can turn shortcuts off (WCAG 2.1.4); only `alwaysOn` ones still run.

**Run one test file.** `pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>` (`testing.md`).

## Gotchas

- A page-load init without its early return costs every page in Gitea; the 500ms warning catches it.
- Fomantic-UI (jQuery) is vendored and deprecated. Do not build new features on it, and do not mix
  it with Vue — Vue may use its CSS classes but not its JavaScript.
- Which menu to build on, Fomantic dropdown or `<aria-menu>` (`web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.ts`),
  is decided in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md`.
- `utils/` is for pure helpers. A function that reaches for `window` or a global selector belongs
  in `modules/` or `features/`.
- A feature can follow a comment box it did not create: the editor's change and upload events
  bubble (`features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`, `features/comp/EditorUpload.ts`), and
  `getComboMarkdownEditor` finds the editor, as `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` does. But
  the editor attaches itself before its async `init` finishes, and calling it before then throws;
  read its textarea until an event arrives.
- Enter on a Fomantic dropdown item only fires a `click` when the item is a link or carries
  `js-aria-clickable` (`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`), so a plain click listener on other
  items never hears a keyboard pick. The close reason menu in `templates/repo/issue/view_content.tmpl`
  marks its items; an `<aria-menu>` item needs no class, as Enter and Space call its `click()`.
- After a click on a Fomantic dropdown item, the dropdown keeps the focus, so focusing something
  else from your click handler needs `setTimeout(..., 0)`.
- `createTippy` (`modules/tippy.ts`) moves a popup to `document.body`, so inputs in it leave their
  `<form>` and are not sent. Keep their values in hidden fields inside the form, as the close reason
  popups in `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` do.

## Related

- `frontend-vue-components.md` — when a feature should be a Vue app instead
- `templates.md` — where `data-global-init` attributes and `pageData` come from
- `frontend-css.md` — `tw-hidden` and the class conventions

# templates — the Go HTML templates and their helpers

**Read when:** editing a page's markup, adding a template, or needing a template function.
**Not here:** the handler that renders it -> `routers-web.md`; classes -> `frontend-css.md`; behaviour -> `frontend-js.md`.

## Responsibilities

Server-rendered HTML, composed with Go's `html/template`. `modules/templates` owns the renderer and
every function templates can call.

| Directory | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `base/` | the page skeleton: `head.tmpl`, `head_script.tmpl`, `head_navbar.tmpl`, `footer.tmpl`, `paginate.tmpl`, `alert.tmpl` |
| `shared/` | reusable partials: `issuelist.tmpl` and its row partial `issuelist_items.tmpl`, `combomarkdowneditor.tmpl`, `actions/`, `secrets/`, `webhook/`, `user/` |
| `repo/`, `user/`, `org/`, `admin/`, `explore/`, `projects/`, `package/` | one directory per page area |
| `mail/` | email bodies |
| `status/` | error pages |
| `devtest/` | the `/devtest` component gallery, also driven by the e2e tests |
| `custom/` | site-admin override hooks — intentionally near-empty |
| `swagger/` | the generated API spec (`v1_json.tmpl`), see `routers-api-v1.md` |

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `modules/templates/helper.go` | `newFuncMapWebPage` — the whole set of page template functions, including `dict`, `Iif` and `Eval` |
| `modules/templates/util_render.go`, `util_render_comment.go` | markup and comment rendering helpers |
| `modules/templates/util_date.go`, `util_avatar.go`, `util_string.go`, `util_slice.go`, `util_dict.go` | the rest of the function set, grouped by kind |
| `modules/templates/htmlrenderer.go` | `TplName` and the renderer |
| `modules/templates/scopedtmpl/` | the scoped-template machinery behind partial rendering |
| `templates/base/head_script.tmpl` | emits `window.config`, including `pageData` |
| `templates/shared/close_reason_icon.tmpl` | a closed item's icon, state label and close-event badge by close reason, for `shared/issueicon.tmpl`, `repo/issue/view_title.tmpl` and `repo/issue/view_content/comments.tmpl` |

## Conventions & invariants

- A template is addressed by its path under `templates/` without the extension, as a
  `templates.TplName` constant in the handler — `"repo/issue/list"` is
  `templates/repo/issue/list.tmpl` (`routers-web.md`).
- **The handler's `ctx.Data` is the only data channel.** A template cannot reach anything the
  handler did not put there, and `ctx.RootData` inside a template context is that same data.
- Data destined for JavaScript goes through `ctx.PageData`, which `base/head_script.tmpl` emits as
  `window.config.pageData` — a separate channel from `ctx.Data`.
- **Every user-visible string is a locale key**, written `{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.issues.new"}}` or
  `ctx.Locale.TrN` for plurals. Never a literal. Keys are added only to
  `options/locale/locale_en-US.json`; the other locales come from Crowdin.
- Composition is `{{template "base/head" .}}` style includes. New shared markup goes in `shared/`,
  not copied between areas.
- `dict` is lowercase for historical reasons; new template functions get uppercase names
  (`helper.go` says so at the definition).
- `dict` treats the key `"."` specially: `dictMerge` in `modules/templates/util_dict.go` flattens
  that argument's map into the new one. So `dict "." $ "Issues" $subset` hands a partial the whole
  root context with one key replaced — but `"." $` **must come first**, or the merge overwrites the
  replacement instead. `templates/repo/issue/list_grouped.tmpl` renders each group this way.
- Mail templates use a different, smaller function set — `mailBodyFuncMap` and
  `mailSubjectTextFuncMap` in `modules/templates/mail.go`. A helper added for pages is not
  available in `templates/mail/`.
- Class attributes are written as one readable unit including their conditionals
  (`frontend-css.md`).
- Hook frontend behaviour up declaratively with `data-global-init` / `data-global-click`
  attributes rather than inline script (`frontend-js.md`).
- `.tmpl` files are tab-indented (`.editorconfig`).

## Recipes

**Add a page's template.** Create the `.tmpl` under the matching area directory, include
`base/head` and `base/footer`, declare the `TplName` constant in the handler, and add every string
as a locale key.

**Share markup between pages.** Put the partial in `templates/shared/` and include it from both
places. Two near-identical partials in two area directories is the thing to avoid.

**Add a template function.** Add it to the map returned by `newFuncMapWebPage` in
`modules/templates/helper.go` and implement it in the matching `util_*.go`. Prefer passing prepared data from the handler — a function that
does database work at render time is a performance bug.

**See a component in isolation.** Run Gitea in development mode and open `/devtest`.

## Gotchas

- A misspelled key in `ctx.Data` renders as empty, not as an error. Check the handler when
  something is silently blank.
- A missing locale key renders the key itself — visible, but easy to miss in a rarely-hit branch.
- `templates/swagger/v1_json.tmpl` is generated. Edit the swagger comments and run
  `make generate-swagger` instead (`routers-api-v1.md`).
- `templates/custom/` is for deployment overrides, not a place to put course code.

## Related

- `routers-web.md` — `TplName` and `ctx.Data`
- `frontend-css.md`, `frontend-js.md` — the classes and attributes used here

import {replaceTextareaSelection} from './comp/EditorMarkdown.ts';
import {showElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import type {ComboMarkdownEditor} from './comp/ComboMarkdownEditor.ts';

/** the backtick fence for a suggestion holding `line`: longer than any backtick run in it, at least 3 */
export function suggestionFence(line: string): string {
  let longest = 0;
  for (const run of line.match(/`+/g) ?? []) longest = Math.max(longest, run.length);
  return '`'.repeat(Math.max(3, longest + 1));
}

/** the text to insert after `textBefore` (the textarea text before the selection),
 *  and the offset in it where the cursor goes: the end of `line` inside the block */
export function buildSuggestionInsert(textBefore: string, line: string): {text: string, cursor: number} {
  const fence = suggestionFence(line);
  const prefix = textBefore && !textBefore.endsWith('\n') ? '\n' : ''; // the block starts on a line of its own
  const head = `${prefix}${fence}suggestion\n${line}`;
  return {text: `${head}\n${fence}\n`, cursor: head.length};
}

/** where to insert a block for a cursor at `pos`: after the fenced code block holding `pos`, if any, so a
 *  block is never nested in another (CommonMark: a closing fence uses the opening's character, is at least
 *  as long and has no info string; an unclosed block runs to the end) */
export function suggestionInsertPos(value: string, pos: number): number {
  let open: {char: string, len: number} | null = null;
  let lineStart = 0;
  while (true) {
    const newline = value.indexOf('\n', lineStart);
    const lineEnd = newline === -1 ? value.length : newline;
    const fence = /^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})(.*)$/.exec(value.slice(lineStart, lineEnd));
    if (!open) {
      if (pos <= lineStart) return pos;
      if (fence && !(fence[1][0] === '`' && fence[2].includes('`'))) {
        open = {char: fence[1][0], len: fence[1].length};
      } else if (pos <= lineEnd) {
        return pos;
      }
    } else if (fence?.[1][0] === open.char && fence[1].length >= open.len && !fence[2].trim()) {
      if (pos <= lineEnd) return newline === -1 ? value.length : newline + 1;
      open = null;
    }
    if (newline === -1) return open ? value.length : pos;
    lineStart = newline + 1;
  }
}

/** the range a block replaces for a selection from `start` to `end`: the selection itself (AC2), or, when
 *  either end is inside a fenced block, an empty range after that block, so no block is cut into */
export function suggestionInsertRange(value: string, start: number, end: number): [number, number] {
  const afterEnd = suggestionInsertPos(value, end);
  if (afterEnd !== end) return [afterEnd, afterEnd];
  const afterStart = suggestionInsertPos(value, start);
  if (afterStart !== start) return [afterStart, afterStart];
  return [start, end];
}

/** show the "Suggest change" button of a new code comment's editor, inserting a block with the text of `codeLine` */
export function initSuggestChangeButton(editor: ComboMarkdownEditor, codeLine: HTMLElement) {
  const button = editor.container.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.markdown-button-suggest-change');
  if (!button) return;
  showElem(button.closest('.markdown-toolbar-group')!);
  button.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    const textarea = editor.textarea;
    const [start, end] = suggestionInsertRange(textarea.value, textarea.selectionStart, textarea.selectionEnd);
    textarea.setSelectionRange(start, end);
    // textContent drops the highlighting spans and keeps leading whitespace; the diff cell also holds the line's own newline
    const line = codeLine.textContent.replace(/[\r\n]+$/, '');
    const {text, cursor} = buildSuggestionInsert(textarea.value.slice(0, start), line);
    replaceTextareaSelection(textarea, text);
    textarea.setSelectionRange(start + cursor, start + cursor);
  });
}
---
import {queryElems} from '../utils/dom.ts';

function makeLine(kind: 'removed' | 'added', text: string): HTMLElement {
  const row = document.createElement('div');
  row.className = `markup-suggestion-line ${kind}`;
  const marker = document.createElement('span');
  marker.className = 'markup-suggestion-marker';
  marker.textContent = kind === 'removed' ? '-' : '+';
  const code = document.createElement('code');
  code.textContent = text; // never innerHTML: suggestion text is user input
  row.append(marker, code);
  return row;
}

// Replaces ```suggestion blocks in a PR code comment with a diff against the commented line.
// The server only sets data-suggestion-original on new-side code comments, so plain comments keep a code block.
export function initMarkupCodeSuggestion(elMarkup: HTMLElement): void {
  const original = elMarkup.getAttribute('data-suggestion-original');
  if (original === null) return;
  const label = elMarkup.getAttribute('data-suggestion-label')!;
  queryElems(elMarkup, 'code.language-suggestion', (elCode) => {
    const block = elCode.closest('.code-block-container') ?? elCode.closest('pre')!;
    // an empty fence renders "" (delete the line); otherwise every line ends with "\n", so one blank line is "\n"
    const raw = elCode.textContent;
    const diff = document.createElement('div');
    diff.className = 'markup-suggestion';
    const header = document.createElement('div');
    header.className = 'markup-suggestion-header';
    header.textContent = label;
    diff.append(header, makeLine('removed', original));
    if (raw !== '') {
      for (const line of raw.replace(/\r?\n$/, '').split(/\r?\n/)) diff.append(makeLine('added', line));
    }
    block.replaceWith(diff);
  });
}

[![@musta55](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/48786719?u=872e537c6f8333143dd0cefc563a852d0f58f0f2&v=4&size=48)](https://github.com/musta55)

Issue body actions

### User Story

As a reviewer, I want to suggest an exact code change in a review comment, and as the PR author, I want to apply it with one click, so that small fixes don't need to be explained and retyped.

### User Scenario

A reviewer selects a few lines in a pull request diff and writes the code she would like to see instead. The PR author sees her suggestion as a diff in the conversation, clicks to apply it, and Gitea adds a commit with that change to the PR branch.

### Acceptance Criteria

The criteria below are a starting point and are incomplete. The open questions must be answered before implementation.

*    AC1: Given selected lines in a PR diff, when a reviewer adds a suggestion, then the comment shows the suggested change as a diff.
*    AC2: Given a suggestion, when the PR author applies it, then a commit with the change is added to the PR branch.
*    AC3: Given a user who can't push to the PR branch, when they try to apply a suggestion, then nothing is committed and they see why.
*    More criteria needed, based on the open questions below.

Acceptance criteria should also cover invalid input, failures, conflicts, and permissions, not only the main path.

### Out of Scope

*   Suggestions on commits outside a pull request
*   Suggestions that create, rename, or delete files

### Open Questions

*   What happens if the code changed after the suggestion was made?
*   Who besides the PR author may apply a suggestion? What about pull requests from forks?
*   What if the PR is closed or merged, or its branch was deleted?
*   Can several suggestions be applied at once? What if they touch the same lines?
*   Who appears as the author of the commit?
*   What happens if two people apply suggestions at the same time?
*   Can suggestions be applied through the API?
*   What happens to existing data and installations after upgrading?

### Design Decision

To be filled in before implementation.

**Decision:**
**Alternatives Considered:**
**Rationale:**
**Consequences:**

### Scope

large

### Scope Justification

Review comments and their markdown rendering, the PR diff UI, creating commits on the PR branch, permissions, and the API.

Description

[![@vvchopra](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/144284255?v=4&size=48)](https://github.com/vvchopra)

[vvchopra](https://github.com/vvchopra)

opened [on Nov 11, 2026](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/156#issue-6321994939)

Issue body actions

### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of [#151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151) · Depends on [#154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154) (S1, merged in [#168](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/pull/168))

User Story
----------

As a PR author, I want to apply a reviewer's suggestion with one click so that Gitea commits the
change to my branch and I don't retype it.

### User Scenario

Ben sees Ana's suggestion and clicks **Apply suggestion**. A small form shows a default commit
message, "Apply suggestion from [@ana](https://github.com/ana) on main.go", which he keeps. He confirms. The page reloads,
the PR has one more commit changing line 18, and the Files tab shows the new code.

### Acceptance Criteria

Errors from the Apply POST are returned the way Gitea's other web forms return them: HTTP 400 with
the message shown on the page, unless an AC says otherwise.

*    AC1: Given a suggestion on a single line, in a review comment or a reply in its thread, and
    a user who can push to the head branch, when they apply it, then exactly one commit is added to
    the head branch that replaces only that line, exactly as [S1. Render `suggestion` blocks in review comments as a diff #154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154)'s diff shows it (AC12). The form
    is prefilled with the default message "Apply suggestion from @ on " and can be
    edited: the commit uses the submitted message, or the default if the message is submitted
    empty.
*    AC2: Given a viewer who can't push to the head branch (read-only, or a fork PR without
    "Allow edits from maintainers"), when the PR is shown, then there is no Apply button, and a
    direct POST returns 403 and commits nothing ([Code suggestions in pull request reviews #151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151) AC3). A signed-out viewer sees no Apply
    button, and a direct POST redirects to sign-in and commits nothing. _Pending customer question 2
    on [Code suggestions in pull request reviews #151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151); see Open Questions for the default._
*    AC3: Given the commented line's text at the current head differs from the line the
    suggestion was written against, or the file was deleted or renamed at head, or the line number
    is now past the end of the file, when someone applies it, then nothing is committed and they see
    "This suggestion is outdated: the code changed since it was written."
*    AC4: Given the head branch moved between page load and Apply (someone pushed, or another
    suggestion was applied), when Apply is submitted with the old head SHA, then nothing is
    committed and they see "This branch has new commits since the page was loaded. Reload the page
    and try again." This holds whether or not the new commits touched the suggestion's file. The
    head SHA sent is the PR's head when the page loaded, even when the Files tab is showing a single
    earlier commit.
*    AC5: Given the PR is closed or merged, or its head branch was deleted, when the PR is shown,
    then there is no Apply button, and a direct POST commits nothing and returns 400 with
    "Suggestions can only be applied to an open pull request whose branch still exists."
*    AC6: Given the head branch is protected against this user's push, when they apply, then
    nothing is committed and they see Gitea's existing message `Cannot commit to protected branch "<branch>".` (the same check and text as the web editor), not the raw pre-receive output.
*    AC7: Given a comment with zero or several suggestion blocks, or a comment on an old-side
    (deleted) line, which [S1. Render `suggestion` blocks in review comments as a diff #154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154) AC7 renders as an ordinary code block, when shown, then there is no
    Apply button.
*    AC8: The commit's author and committer follow the customer's answer to question 1, and a
    test asserts them. _Pending customer question 1 on [Code suggestions in pull request reviews #151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151); see Open Questions for the default._
*    AC9: Given an outdated review comment (its code changed in a later push), when shown, then
    its suggestion has no Apply button. A POST from a page loaded before the change is handled by
    AC3/AC4.
*    AC10: Given a suggestion identical to the current line, when someone applies it, then no
    commit is made and they see "This suggestion makes no changes to the code."
*    AC11: Given a file with CRLF line endings or no final newline, when a suggestion on it is
    applied, then the changed line keeps the file's line ending and the file's final-newline state
    is unchanged; no other byte of the file changes.
*    AC12: Given the suggestion block is empty, has one blank line, or has several lines, when it
    is applied, then the commit deletes the line, replaces it with a blank line, or replaces it with
    those lines in order, matching [S1. Render `suggestion` blocks in review comments as a diff #154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154) AC2's diff. No line before or after it changes.

### Out of Scope

*   Several suggestions at once (S6); API (S7); recording "applied" state (S4).
*   Suggestions on old-side (deleted) lines (customer question 5): they render as plain code blocks
    in [S1. Render `suggestion` blocks in review comments as a diff #154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154), so there is nothing to apply. If the customer allows them, that's a follow-up issue.
*   Resolving the review conversation on apply (customer question 3).
*   Applying without JavaScript: like [S1. Render `suggestion` blocks in review comments as a diff #154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154)'s no-JavaScript fallback, the suggestion is then a plain
    code block with no Apply button.
*   Suggestions spanning several commented lines (S5). A one-line comment whose block has several
    lines is in scope (AC12).

### Open Questions

*   **Customer question 1 (commit author)**, for AC8: unanswered on [Code suggestions in pull request reviews #151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151). If there is no answer by
    Nov 16, the default is: the person who applied it is author and committer, with a
    `Co-authored-by:` trailer for the reviewer who wrote the suggestion.
*   **Customer question 2 (who may apply)**, for AC2: unanswered on [Code suggestions in pull request reviews #151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151). Default if no answer by
    Nov 16: anyone who can push to the head branch, including maintainers on a fork PR with "Allow
    edits from maintainers" on.
*   **Customer question 4 (applying your own suggestion):** unanswered on [Code suggestions in pull request reviews #151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151). Default if no answer
    by Nov 16: allowed; the permission rule in AC2 is the only check.
*   Should the Apply form allow editing the commit message? Resolved: editable, prefilled with
    the default (AC1).

### Design Decision

**Decision:** A new `services/pull` function (`ApplySuggestion(ctx, doer, comment, expectedHeadSHA, message)`) that first checks that `expectedHeadSHA` is still the head branch's commit (AC4) and
that the doer may commit to the branch, using the same check as the web editor (`CanCommitToBranch`;
AC6). It then reads the file at the current head, checks the target line still matches
`Comment.SuggestionOriginalLine()` from [#154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154) (ignoring a trailing `\r` on both sides, so CRLF files
compare correctly), replaces it with the block's lines, and commits through
`files_service.ChangeRepoFiles` with
`LastCommitID = expectedHeadSHA`. Permission is checked with the same head-branch write check the
web editor uses for PR branches, including `AllowMaintainerEdit`.

**Alternatives Considered:**

*   _Apply with `git apply` on a patch built from the suggestion, in a temporary clone._ Handles
    fuzz, but fuzzy application can land the change on the wrong line, and it duplicates what
    `ChangeRepoFiles` already does (temp repo, hooks, protection checks, push).
*   _Just replace line N without comparing contents._ Simple, but silently overwrites code if the
    file changed since the review (AC3).
*   _Rely on `ChangeRepoFiles`'s `LastCommitID` check alone for AC4._ That check only fails when the
    same file changed since `LastCommitID` (`services/repository/files/update.go:393`). If another
    file changed, it commits on the stale parent and the push is rejected as out of date, which the
    web editor reports with its generic "file contents have changed" message, not AC4's.

**Rationale:** `ChangeRepoFiles` already runs hooks, re-checks branch protection on push and
handles the temp repo, so only the suggestion-specific checks are new. Checking the head SHA and
`CanCommitToBranch` up front gives AC4 and AC6 their own messages instead of whatever the push
returns. Comparing line contents makes outdated suggestions fail safe.

**Consequences:** Applying a suggestion triggers the normal push path (CI, PR recheck,
`InvalidateCodeComments`). A suggestion whose line moved but didn't change is refused rather than
re-located; a later issue could add re-anchoring. Any push to the branch, even one unrelated to
the suggestion's file, makes an open page's Apply fail with AC4 until it is reloaded.

### Decision 2: reading suggestion blocks on the server

**Decision:** Add `Comment.SuggestionBlocks()` in `models/issues/comment_suggestion.go`, next to
[#154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154)'s `SuggestionOriginalLine()`. It parses `Comment.Content` with Gitea's own goldmark markdown
parser and returns the text of each fenced code block whose first info word is exactly
`suggestion`. The Apply POST reads the suggested text from it (the client never sends the text),
and AC7's "exactly one block" rule counts with it. S4 and S6 can reuse it.

**Alternatives Considered:**

*   _A line scanner or regex over the raw markdown._ Simpler and faster, but it can disagree with
    the rendered page on fences inside lists or blockquotes, `~~~` fences, longer fences and info
    strings ([S1. Render `suggestion` blocks in review comments as a diff #154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154) AC9), so Apply could commit something other than the diff on screen.
*   _Have the browser send the suggestion text with the POST._ No parser needed, but the commit would
    hold whatever the request says rather than what the comment says.

**Rationale:** Only goldmark is guaranteed to find the same blocks the page renders, so what the
reader sees is what gets committed.

**Consequences:** Parsing the comment costs a markdown parse per Apply and per comment shown with
an Apply button. The parser lives in the model package and must be kept in step with any future
change to how [#154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154) recognises suggestion blocks.

### Decision 3: where the Apply button comes from

**Decision:** The server adds a `data-suggestion-apply-url` attribute and the PR's head SHA next to
[#154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154)'s `data-suggestion-original` on the comment body, only when this viewer may apply (AC2, AC5,
AC9; old-side comments already get no attribute, AC7). [#154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154)'s `web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts`
then adds the Apply button and commit-message form to the diff header when the comment has
exactly one suggestion block. The server re-checks every condition on POST.

**Alternatives Considered:**

*   _Render the button in `repo/diff/comments.tmpl` and `conversation.tmpl`, outside the markup._
    Works without JavaScript, but the server would need to parse every comment at render time to
    count blocks, and the button would sit apart from the diff it applies, laid out twice.
*   _A separate frontend handler that finds [S1. Render `suggestion` blocks in review comments as a diff #154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154)'s rendered diffs._ Keeps [S1. Render `suggestion` blocks in review comments as a diff #154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154)'s file untouched, but
    depends on its generated markup and runs as a second pass over the same comments.

**Rationale:** It follows [#154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154)'s own design (the server supplies data attributes, the browser
draws the suggestion), covers both tabs with one code path, and re-renders after a comment is
edited ([#154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154) AC8).

**Consequences:** No JavaScript means no button (Out of Scope). Changes to `suggestion.ts` must
keep [#154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154)'s tests passing, and S4's "applied" marker will probably go in the same header.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

One new service function in `services/pull` and a goldmark-based `Comment.SuggestionBlocks()` in
`models/issues`, both with unit tests; one web route and handler with the permission and PR-state
checks; two data attributes in [#154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154)'s two comment templates; the Apply button and commit-message
form in [#154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154)'s `suggestion.ts` with Vitest tests; a few locale strings; and integration tests for
the permission and error cases (AC2, AC4–AC6) sharing one PR setup to keep them fast. No schema
change. Recording the applied state is S4.

* * *

[![@vvchopra](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/144284255?v=4&size=48)](https://github.com/vvchopra)
