Issue body actions

### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of [#151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151)

User Story
----------

As a PR author, I want a reviewer's suggested code to show as a before/after diff in the review
comment so that I can see exactly what would change without comparing it to the file myself.

### User Scenario

User Scenario
-------------

Ana reviews PR [#42](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/pull/42). On line 18 of `main.go` she writes a code comment containing

\`\`\`suggestion
	return fmt.Errorf("open %s: %w", name, err)
\`\`\`

and submits the review. Ben, the author, opens the Conversation tab. Under Ana's comment he sees
a small diff: line 18 as it is now in red, her replacement in green, labelled "Suggested change".
The same rendering appears on the Files changed tab. Text outside the block renders as normal
markdown.

### Acceptance Criteria

*    AC1: Given a code comment on a new-side line whose body has one ` ```suggestion ` block,
    when the comment is shown in the Conversation or Files changed tab, then the block renders as a
    diff headed "Suggested change": the commented line as removed (red) and each line of the block
    as added (green), with indentation kept.
*    AC2: Given an empty ` ```suggestion ` block, when rendered, then it shows the commented
    line as removed and nothing added (a "delete this line" suggestion).
*    AC3: Given a ` ```suggestion ` block in a plain issue or PR comment (not a code
    comment), when rendered, then it shows as an ordinary code block, not a diff.
*    AC4: Given a code comment with two or more suggestion blocks, when rendered, then each block
    renders as its own diff against the same commented line. (S3 decides whether to offer Apply.)
*    AC5: Given suggestion content containing HTML such as `<script>alert(1)</script>`, when
    rendered, then it is shown as literal text and nothing is executed.
*    AC6: Given an outdated code comment (the branch moved and the comment is `Invalidated`), when
    rendered, then the diff is still shown against the line the reviewer originally commented on,
    next to the existing "Outdated" label.
*    AC7: Given a code comment on an old-side (deleted) line, or one whose stored diff context is
    missing, when rendered, then the suggestion block shows as an ordinary code block and the page
    has no errors.
*    AC8: Given a code comment with a suggestion is edited, when the edit is saved, then the
    updated block renders as a diff without reloading the page.

### Out of Scope

*   Applying the suggestion (S3); multi-line ranges (S5); the editor button (S2).
*   Suggestions in commit comments outside a PR ([Code suggestions in pull request reviews #151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151) out of scope).
*   Suggestions on old-side (deleted) lines, until the customer answers question 5 on [Code suggestions in pull request reviews #151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151).
*   Syntax highlighting inside the suggestion diff.

### Open Questions

*   Should the old side of the diff come from the comment's stored diff context (what the reviewer
    saw) or from the file at the current head? (Decided: stored context, so the diff never changes
    under the reader; S3 does the "has it changed since" check.)
*   Old-side suggestions: waiting on customer question 5 on [Code suggestions in pull request reviews #151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151).

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Render the diff in the browser, the same way Gitea already renders `mermaid` and
`math` code blocks. The server takes the commented line from the comment's stored diff context
(`Comment.Patch`, whose last line is always the commented line) through a new
`Comment.SuggestionOriginalLine()` method, and puts it in a `data-suggestion-original` attribute
on the body of new-side code comments only. A new `web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts`, registered
beside the mermaid and math handlers, replaces each `code.language-suggestion` block inside such a
body with a diff, building it with `textContent` only.

**Alternatives Considered:**

*   _Post-process the rendered HTML on the server._ After markdown renders a code comment, Go would
    find the `<pre><code class="language-suggestion">` and swap in a template-rendered diff. It works
    without JavaScript, but it rewrites already-sanitised HTML and has to be repeated in both places
    that render code comments (the page load and the edit-comment save).
*   _A markdown renderer extension in `modules/markup`._ The renderer would emit the diff directly,
    but it would need to know which file and line a comment belongs to, which it doesn't carry for
    any other content, and the sanitiser's allowlist would need new classes.

**Rationale:** It follows an existing pattern (mermaid, math), leaves the markdown renderer and
sanitiser untouched, and the attribute on new-side code comments only is what keeps plain comments
as plain code blocks (AC3). Editing a comment re-runs the same frontend hook, so AC8 needs no
extra server code.

**Consequences:** Without JavaScript a suggestion shows as a plain code block. S3 and S7 must find
suggestion blocks in Go themselves (using goldmark's parser, so they agree with what the page
shows); S1 gives them `SuggestionOriginalLine()` to compare against.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

Medium scope because it touches a good amount of components in the code

    Spec reviewed — [@CarsonRackley](https://github.com/CarsonRackley)

    **Acceptance criteria:** All 8 are Given/When/Then with a clear pass/fail, and the failure cases
    (XSS, outdated, missing context) are good. AC2 should say whether a fence with one blank line
    counts as "empty" (delete the line) or replaces the line with a blank. AC7's "no errors" should
    be observable, e.g. "no console errors".

    **Cases considered:** Main path, empty block, several blocks, plain comment, XSS, outdated,
    old-side line and edit-without-reload are all covered. Missing:

    *   replies in a code-comment thread (add to AC1)
    *   the review summary body, which should behave like AC3
    *   which fence variants count (`~~~suggestion`, `Suggestion`), so S3/S7 parse the same blocks

    **Scope:** Medium fits (a model method, a template attribute, a new frontend handler, tests). But
    the justification needs to name the components and the expected size of change, not just "a
    good amount of components".

    **Verdict:** Changes needed:

    1.  Clarify AC2 and AC7.
    2.  Add the missing cases above.
    3.  Rewrite the Scope Justification.

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issues

import (
	"strings"

	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"
)

// SuggestionOriginalLine returns the commented line as the reviewer saw it: the last line of the
// stored patch, since CutDiffAroundLine stops right after the commented line.
// Old-side comments return None until #151 decides whether they may carry suggestions.
func (c *Comment) SuggestionOriginalLine() optional.Option[string] {
	if c.Type != CommentTypeCode || c.Line <= 0 {
		return optional.None[string]()
	}
	patch := strings.TrimRight(c.Patch, "\n")
	last := patch[strings.LastIndexByte(patch, '\n')+1:]
	if last == "" || (last[0] != '+' && last[0] != ' ') {
		return optional.None[string]() // "-" is the other side; "@", "d", "\\" mean no code line
	}
	return optional.Some(last[1:])
}

// Copyright 2025 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.

package issue

import (
	"context"
	"strconv"

	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	repo_model "gitea.dev/models/repo"
	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"
	"gitea.dev/modules/structs"
)

func GetSuggestion(ctx context.Context, repo *repo_model.Repository, isPull optional.Option[bool], keyword string) ([]*structs.Issue, error) {
	var issues issues_model.IssueList
	var err error
	pageSize := 5
	if keyword == "" {
		issues, err = issues_model.FindLatestUpdatedIssues(ctx, repo.ID, isPull, pageSize)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	} else {
		indexKeyword, _ := strconv.ParseInt(keyword, 10, 64)
		var issueByIndex *issues_model.Issue
		var excludedID int64
		if indexKeyword > 0 {
			issueByIndex, err = issues_model.GetIssueByIndex(ctx, repo.ID, indexKeyword)
			if err != nil && !issues_model.IsErrIssueNotExist(err) {
				return nil, err
			}
			if issueByIndex != nil {
				excludedID = issueByIndex.ID
				pageSize--
			}
		}

		issues, err = issues_model.FindIssuesSuggestionByKeyword(ctx, repo.ID, keyword, isPull, excludedID, pageSize)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}

		if issueByIndex != nil {
			issues = append([]*issues_model.Issue{issueByIndex}, issues...)
		}
	}

	if err := issues.LoadPullRequests(ctx); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	suggestions := make([]*structs.Issue, 0, len(issues))
	for _, issue := range issues {
		suggestion := &structs.Issue{
			ID:          issue.ID,
			Index:       issue.Index,
			Title:       issue.Title,
			State:       issue.State(),
			CloseReason: issue.CloseReason.String(),
		}

		if issue.IsPull && issue.PullRequest != nil {
			suggestion.PullRequest = &structs.PullRequestMeta{
				HasMerged:        issue.PullRequest.HasMerged,
				IsWorkInProgress: issue.PullRequest.IsWorkInProgress(ctx),
			}
		}
		suggestions = append(suggestions, suggestion)
	}

	return suggestions, nil
}

func Test_AddReasonToNotification(t *testing.T) {
	x, deferable := migrationtest.PrepareTestEnv(t, 0, new(notificationBeforeReason))
	defer deferable()

	var before []notificationBeforeReason
	require.NoError(t, x.Table("notification").Asc("id").Find(&before))
	require.Len(t, before, 4) // guards against the fixtures silently not loading

	require.NoError(t, AddReasonToNotification(x))

	var after []notificationBeforeReason
	require.NoError(t, x.Table("notification").Asc("id").Find(&after))
	assert.Equal(t, before, after) // #52 AC3 nothing else changes

	var reasons []int
	require.NoError(t, x.Table("notification").Asc("id").Cols("reason").Find(&reasons))
	assert.Equal(t, []int{0, 0, 0, 0}, reasons) // #52 AC3 every existing notification is "Other"
}

// DiffSide returns "previous" if Comment.Line is a LOC of the previous changes and "proposed" if it is a LOC of the proposed changes.
func (c *Comment) DiffSide() string {
	if c.Line < 0 {
		return "previous"
	}
	return "proposed"
}

// UnsignedLine returns the LOC of the code comment without + or -
func (c *Comment) UnsignedLine() uint64 {
	if c.Line < 0 {
		return uint64(c.Line * -1)
	}
	return uint64(c.Line)
}

// CodeCommentLink returns the url to a comment in code
func (c *Comment) CodeCommentLink(ctx context.Context) string {
	err := c.LoadIssue(ctx)
	if err != nil { // Silently dropping errors :unamused:
		log.Error("LoadIssue(%d): %v", c.IssueID, err)
		return ""
	}
	err = c.Issue.LoadRepo(ctx)
	if err != nil { // Silently dropping errors :unamused:
		log.Error("loadRepo(%d): %v", c.Issue.RepoID, err)
		return ""
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s/files#%s", c.Issue.Link(), c.HashTag())
}

// MetaCloseReason returns the reason recorded on a close comment; comments without metadata have none.
// The duplicate target is not included: load it with LoadCloseDuplicateIssue.
func (c *Comment) MetaCloseReason() CloseReasonOptions {
	if c.CommentMetaData == nil {
		return CloseReasonOptions{}
	}
	return CloseReasonOptions{Reason: c.CommentMetaData.CloseReason, Text: c.CommentMetaData.CloseReasonText}
}

// LoadCloseDuplicateIssue loads the issue a close comment names as the duplicate target,
// with its repository so that Link works. A deleted target returns ErrIssueNotExist.
func (c *Comment) LoadCloseDuplicateIssue(ctx context.Context) error {
	if c.CloseDuplicateIssue != nil || c.CommentMetaData == nil || c.CommentMetaData.CloseDuplicateIssueID <= 0 {
		return nil
	}
	issue, err := GetIssueByID(ctx, c.CommentMetaData.CloseDuplicateIssueID)
	if err != nil {

func (c *Comment) MetaSpecialDoerTr(locale translation.Locale) template.HTML {
	if c.CommentMetaData == nil {
		return ""
	}
	if c.CommentMetaData.SpecialDoerName == SpecialDoerNameCodeOwners {
		return locale.Tr("repo.issues.review.codeowners_rules")
	}
	return htmlutil.HTMLFormat("%s", c.CommentMetaData.SpecialDoerName)
}

func (c *Comment) TimelineRequestedReviewTr(locale translation.Locale, createdStr template.HTML) template.HTML {
	if c.Assignee != nil {
		if c.RemovedAssignee {
			if c.PosterID == c.AssigneeID {
				return locale.Tr("repo.issues.review.remove_review_request_self", createdStr)
			}
			return locale.Tr("repo.issues.review.remove_review_request", c.Assignee.GetDisplayName(), createdStr)
		}
		return locale.Tr("repo.issues.review.add_review_request", c.Assignee.GetDisplayName(), createdStr)
	}
	if c.AssigneeTeam != nil {
		if c.RemovedAssignee {
			return locale.Tr("repo.issues.review.remove_review_request", c.AssigneeTeam.Name, createdStr)
		}
		return locale.Tr("repo.issues.review.add_review_request", c.AssigneeTeam.Name, createdStr)
	}

	// impossible fallback
	assigneePrompt := fmt.Sprintf("(AssigneeID=%d, AssigneeTeamID=%d)", c.AssigneeID, c.AssigneeTeam.ID)
	setting.PanicInDevOrTesting("unknown timeline pull request review event comment: id=%d, %s", c.ID, assigneePrompt)
	if c.RemovedAssignee {
		return locale.Tr("repo.issues.review.remove_review_request", assigneePrompt, createdStr)
	}
	return locale.Tr("repo.issues.review.add_review_request", assigneePrompt, createdStr)
}

   111	export function initRepoCodeView() {
   112	  // When viewing a file or blame, there is always a ".file-view" element,
   113	  // but the ".code-view" class is only present when viewing the "code" of a file; it is not present when viewing a PDF file.
   114	  // Since the ".file-view" will be dynamically reloaded when navigating via the left file tree (eg: view a PDF file, then view a source code file, etc.)
   115	  // the "code-view" related event listeners should always be added when the current page contains ".file-view" element.
   116	  if (!document.querySelector('.repo-view-container .file-view')) return;
   117
   118	  // "file code view" and "blame" pages need this "line number button" feature
   119	  let selRangeStart: string | undefined;
   120	  addDelegatedEventListener(document, 'click', '.code-view .lines-num span', (el: HTMLElement, e: KeyboardEvent) => {
   121	    if (!selRangeStart || !e.shiftKey) {
   122	      selRangeStart = el.getAttribute('id')!;
   123	      selectRange(selRangeStart);
   124	    } else {
   125	      const selRangeStop = el.getAttribute('id');
   126	      selectRange(`${selRangeStart}-${selRangeStop}`);
   127	    }
   128	    window.getSelection()!.removeAllRanges();
   129	    showLineButton();
   130	  });
   131
   132	  // apply the selected range from the URL hash
   133	  const onHashChange = () => {
   134	    if (!window.location.hash) return;
   135	    if (!document.querySelector('.code-view .lines-num')) return;
   136	    const range = window.location.hash.substring(1);
   137	    const first = selectRange(range);
   138	    if (first) {
   139	      // set scrollRestoration to 'manual' when there is a hash in the URL, so that the scroll position will not be remembered after refreshing
   140	      if (window.history.scrollRestoration !== 'manual') window.history.scrollRestoration = 'manual';
   141	      first.scrollIntoView({block: 'start'});
   142	      showLineButton();
   143	    }
   144	  };
   145	  onHashChange();
   146	  window.addEventListener('hashchange', onHashChange);
   147	}

    12	// SuggestionOriginalLine returns the commented line as the reviewer saw it: the last line of the
    13	// stored patch, since CutDiffAroundLine stops right after the commented line.
    14	// Old-side comments return None until #151 decides whether they may carry suggestions.
    15	func (c *Comment) SuggestionOriginalLine() optional.Option[string] {
    16		if c.Type != CommentTypeCode || c.Line <= 0 {
    17			return optional.None[string]()
    18		}
    19		patch := strings.TrimRight(c.Patch, "\n")
    20		last := patch[strings.LastIndexByte(patch, '\n')+1:]
    21		if last == "" || (last[0] != '+' && last[0] != ' ') {
    22			return optional.None[string]() // "-" is the other side; "@", "d", "\\" mean no code line
    23		}
    24		return optional.Some(last[1:])
    25	}

// RenderNewCodeCommentForm will render the form for creating a new review comment
func RenderNewCodeCommentForm(ctx *context.Context) {
	issue := GetActionIssue(ctx)
	if ctx.Written() {
		return
	}
	if !issue.IsPull {
		return
	}
	currentReview, err := issues_model.GetCurrentReview(ctx, ctx.Doer, issue)
	if err != nil && !issues_model.IsErrReviewNotExist(err) {
		ctx.ServerError("GetCurrentReview", err)
		return
	}
	ctx.Data["PageIsPullFiles"] = true
	ctx.Data["Issue"] = issue
	ctx.Data["CurrentReview"] = currentReview
	pullHeadCommitID, err := ctx.Repo.GitRepo.GetRefCommitID(issue.PullRequest.GetGitHeadRefName())
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("GetRefCommitID", err)
		return
	}
	ctx.Data["AfterCommitID"] = pullHeadCommitID
	ctx.Data["IsAttachmentEnabled"] = setting.Attachment.Enabled
	upload.AddUploadContext(ctx, "comment")
	ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplNewComment)
}

5:/** the backtick fence for a suggestion holding `line`: longer than any backtick run in it, at least 3 */
6:export function suggestionFence(line: string): string {
7:  let longest = 0;
8:  for (const run of line.match(/`+/g) ?? []) longest = Math.max(longest, run.length);
9:  return '`'.repeat(Math.max(3, longest + 1));
10:}
11:
12:/** the text to insert after `textBefore` (the textarea text before the selection),
13: *  and the offset in it where the cursor goes: the end of `line` inside the block */
14:export function buildSuggestionInsert(textBefore: string, line: string): {text: string, cursor: number} {
15:  const fence = suggestionFence(line);
16:  const prefix = textBefore && !textBefore.endsWith('\n') ? '\n' : ''; // the block starts on a line of its own
17:  const head = `${prefix}${fence}suggestion\n${line}`;
18:  return {text: `${head}\n${fence}\n`, cursor: head.length};
19:}
20:
21:/** where to insert a block for a cursor at `pos`: after the fenced code block holding `pos`, if any, so a
22: *  block is never nested in another (CommonMark: a closing fence uses the opening's character, is at least
23: *  as long and has no info string; an unclosed block runs to the end) */
24:export function suggestionInsertPos(value: string, pos: number): number {
25:  let open: {char: string, len: number} | null = null;
26:  let lineStart = 0;
27:  while (true) {
28:    const newline = value.indexOf('\n', lineStart);
29:    const lineEnd = newline === -1 ? value.length : newline;
30:    const fence = /^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})(.*)$/.exec(value.slice(lineStart, lineEnd));
31:    if (!open) {
32:      if (pos <= lineStart) return pos;
33:      if (fence && !(fence[1][0] === '`' && fence[2].includes('`'))) {
34:        open = {char: fence[1][0], len: fence[1].length};
35:      } else if (pos <= lineEnd) {
36:        return pos;
37:      }
38:    } else if (fence?.[1][0] === open.char && fence[1].length >= open.len && !fence[2].trim()) {
39:      if (pos <= lineEnd) return newline === -1 ? value.length : newline + 1;
40:      open = null;
41:    }
42:    if (newline === -1) return open ? value.length : pos;
43:    lineStart = newline + 1;
44:  }
45:}
46:
47:/** the range a block replaces for a selection from `start` to `end`: the selection itself (AC2), or, when
48: *  either end is inside a fenced block, an empty range after that block, so no block is cut into */
49:export function suggestionInsertRange(value: string, start: number, end: number): [number, number] {
50:  const afterEnd = suggestionInsertPos(value, end);
51:  if (afterEnd !== end) return [afterEnd, afterEnd];
52:  const afterStart = suggestionInsertPos(value, start);
53:  if (afterStart !== start) return [afterStart, afterStart];
54:  return [start, end];
55:}
56:
57:/** show the "Suggest change" button of a new code comment's editor, inserting a block with the text of `codeLine` */
58:export function initSuggestChangeButton(editor: ComboMarkdownEditor, codeLine: HTMLElement) {
59:  const button = editor.container.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.markdown-button-suggest-change');
60:  if (!button) return;
61:  showElem(button.closest('.markdown-toolbar-group')!);
62:  button.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
63:    e.preventDefault();
64:    const textarea = editor.textarea;
65:    const [start, end] = suggestionInsertRange(textarea.value, textarea.selectionStart, textarea.selectionEnd);
66:    textarea.setSelectionRange(start, end);
67:    // textContent drops the highlighting spans and keeps leading whitespace; the diff cell also holds the line's own newline
68:    const line = codeLine.textContent.replace(/[\r\n]+$/, '');
69:    const {text, cursor} = buildSuggestionInsert(textarea.value.slice(0, start), line);
70:    replaceTextareaSelection(textarea, text);
71:    textarea.setSelectionRange(start + cursor, start + cursor);
72:  });
73:}

58	// LineBlame returns the latest commit at the given line
59	func lineBlame(ctx context.Context, repo *repo_model.Repository, gitRepo *git.Repository, branch, file string, line uint) (*git.Commit, error) {
60		sha, err := gitrepo.LineBlame(ctx, repo, branch, file, line)
61		if err != nil {
62			return nil, err
63		}
64		if len(sha) < 40 {
65			return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid result of blame: %s", sha)
66		}
67
68		objectFormat := git.ObjectFormatFromName(repo.ObjectFormatName)
69		return gitRepo.GetCommit(sha[:objectFormat.FullLength()])
70	}
71
72	// checkInvalidation checks if the line of code comment got changed by another commit.
73	// If the line got changed the comment is going to be invalidated.
74	func checkInvalidation(ctx context.Context, c *issues_model.Comment, repo *repo_model.Repository, gitRepo *git.Repository, branch string) error {
75		// FIXME differentiate between previous and proposed line
76		commit, err := lineBlame(ctx, repo, gitRepo, branch, c.TreePath, uint(c.UnsignedLine()))
77		if isErrBlameNotFoundOrNotEnoughLines(err) {
78			c.Invalidated = true
79			return issues_model.UpdateCommentInvalidate(ctx, c)
80		}
81		if err != nil {
82			return err
83		}
84		if c.CommitSHA != "" && c.CommitSHA != commit.ID.String() {
85			c.Invalidated = true
86			return issues_model.UpdateCommentInvalidate(ctx, c)
87		}
88		return nil
89	}

117		var (

125		// - Comments that reply to an existing review
126
127		if !pendingReview && replyReviewID != 0 {

130			if existsReview, err = issues_model.ReviewExists(ctx, issue, treePath, line); err != nil {

136		if !pendingReview && existsReview {

138				return nil, err

142				doer,
143				issue.Repo,
144				issue,
145				content,
146				treePath,
147				line,

153			}
154

156			if err != nil {
157				return nil, err
158			}
159

161
162			return comment, nil
163		}
164
165		review, err := issues_model.GetCurrentReview(ctx, doer, issue)
166		if err != nil {
167			if !issues_model.IsErrReviewNotExist(err) {
168				return nil, err
169			}
170
171			if review, err = issues_model.CreateReview(ctx, issues_model.CreateReviewOptions{
172				Type:     issues_model.ReviewTypePending,
173				Reviewer: doer,
174				Issue:    issue,
175				Official: false,
176				CommitID: latestCommitID,
177			}); err != nil {
178				return nil, err
179			}
180		}
181
182		comment, err := createCodeComment(ctx,
183			doer,
184			issue.Repo,
185			issue,
186			content,
187			treePath,
188			line,
189			review.ID,
190			attachments,
191		)
192		if err != nil {
193			return nil, err
194		}

196		if !pendingReview && !existsReview {

198			if _, _, err = SubmitReview(ctx, doer, gitRepo, issue, issues_model.ReviewTypeComment, "", latestCommitID, nil); err != nil {

208	// createCodeComment creates a plain code comment at the specified line / path
209	func createCodeComment(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, repo *repo_model.Repository, issue *issues_model.Issue, content, treePath string, line, reviewID int64, attachments []string) (*issues_model.Comment, error) {
210		var commitID, patch string
211		if err := issue.LoadPullRequest(ctx); err != nil {
212			return nil, fmt.Errorf("LoadPullRequest: %w", err)
213		}
214		pr := issue.PullRequest
215		if err := pr.LoadBaseRepo(ctx); err != nil {
216			return nil, fmt.Errorf("LoadBaseRepo: %w", err)
217		}
218		gitRepo, closer, err := gitrepo.RepositoryFromContextOrOpen(ctx, pr.BaseRepo)
219		if err != nil {
220			return nil, fmt.Errorf("RepositoryFromContextOrOpen: %w", err)
221		}
222		defer closer.Close()
223
224		invalidated := false
225		head := pr.GetGitHeadRefName()
226		if line > 0 {
227			if reviewID != 0 {
228				first, err := issues_model.FindComments(ctx, &issues_model.FindCommentsOptions{
229					ReviewID: reviewID,
230					Line:     line,
231					TreePath: treePath,
232					Type:     issues_model.CommentTypeCode,
233					ListOptions: db.ListOptions{
234						PageSize: 1,
235						Page:     1,
236					},
237				})
238				if err == nil && len(first) > 0 {
239					commitID = first[0].CommitSHA
240					invalidated = first[0].Invalidated
241					patch = first[0].Patch
242				} else if err != nil && !issues_model.IsErrCommentNotExist(err) {
243					return nil, fmt.Errorf("Find first comment for %d line %d path %s. Error: %w", reviewID, line, treePath, err)
244				} else {
245					review, err := issues_model.GetReviewByID(ctx, reviewID)
246					if err == nil && len(review.CommitID) > 0 {
247						head = review.CommitID
248					} else if err != nil && !issues_model.IsErrReviewNotExist(err) {
249						return nil, fmt.Errorf("GetReviewByID %d. Error: %w", reviewID, err)
250					}
251				}
252			}
253
254			if len(commitID) == 0 {
255				// FIXME validate treePath
256				// Get latest commit referencing the commented line
257				// No need for get commit for base branch changes
258				commit, err := lineBlame(ctx, pr.BaseRepo, gitRepo, head, treePath, uint(line))
259				if err == nil {
260					commitID = commit.ID.String()
261				} else if !isErrBlameNotFoundOrNotEnoughLines(err) {
262					return nil, fmt.Errorf("LineBlame[%s, %s, %s, %d]: %w", pr.GetGitHeadRefName(), gitRepo.Path, treePath, line, err)
263				}
264			}
265		}
266
267		// Only fetch diff if comment is review comment
268		if len(patch) == 0 && reviewID != 0 {
269			headCommitID, err := gitRepo.GetRefCommitID(pr.GetGitHeadRefName())
270			if err != nil {
271				return nil, fmt.Errorf("GetRefCommitID[%s]: %w", pr.GetGitHeadRefName(), err)
272			}
273			if len(commitID) == 0 {
274				commitID = headCommitID
275			}
276
277			patch, err = git.GetFileDiffCutAroundLine(
278				gitRepo, pr.MergeBase, headCommitID, treePath,
279				int64((&issues_model.Comment{Line: line}).UnsignedLine()), line < 0, setting.UI.CodeCommentLines,
280			)
281			if err != nil {
282				return nil, err
283			}
284
285			// If patch is still empty (unchanged line), generate code context
286			if patch == "" && commitID != "" {
287				patch, err = gitdiff.GeneratePatchForUnchangedLine(gitRepo, commitID, treePath, line, setting.UI.CodeCommentLines)
288				if err != nil {
289					// Log the error but don't fail comment creation
290					log.Debug("Unable to generate patch for unchanged line (file=%s, line=%d, commit=%s): %v", treePath, line, commitID, err)
291				}
292			}
293		}
294		return issues_model.CreateComment(ctx, &issues_model.CreateCommentOptions{
295			Type:        issues_model.CommentTypeCode,
296			Doer:        doer,
297			Repo:        repo,
298			Issue:       issue,
299			Content:     content,

Issue body actions

### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: small` · Type: Feature · Part of [#151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151)

As a reviewer, I want a button that fills in a suggestion block with the current line so that I
only edit the code instead of copying it and remembering the syntax.

### User Scenario

Ana opens the Files tab of an open PR and clicks the `+` next to new-side line 18. The code
comment form that opens has a "Suggest change" button in its toolbar. She clicks it and the
textarea gets a ` ```suggestion ` block holding line 18's current text, with the cursor at the
end of that line inside the block. She edits the line and clicks "Add single comment". The comment
is saved with the block as she typed it; showing it as a diff is S1's job.

### Acceptance Criteria

*    AC1: Given the code comment form opened on a new-side line (an added line, or an unchanged
    context line, including lines revealed by "expand"), in split or unified view, when the reviewer
    clicks "Suggest change", then the textarea contains a block made of a fence line
    ` ```suggestion `, the line's exact text (leading tabs and spaces kept, no `+` or space
    diff marker, no highlighting markup), and a closing fence.
*    AC2: Given the textarea already has text, when the reviewer clicks "Suggest change", then the
    block is inserted at the cursor (replacing any selected text), starts on a line of its own and is
    followed by a newline, and the text before and after it is kept.
*    AC3: Given the code comment form, when the reviewer clicks "Suggest change", then the
    textarea has focus and the cursor sits at the end of the line's text inside the block.
*    AC4: Given the line's text contains a run of N backticks with N ≥ 3 (for example
    ` ```js `), when the block is inserted, then both fences use N+1 backticks, so the block
    is not closed early. With fewer than 3 backticks in a row, the fences stay at 3.
*    AC5: Given an empty or whitespace-only line, when the block is inserted, then the block
    holds that line as is (an empty line or the same whitespace) between the fences.
*    AC6: Given the form opened on an old-side line (a deleted line, or the left column of a
    changed line in split view), when the form is shown, then the "Suggest change" button is not
    shown. If the customer's answer to question 5 on [Code suggestions in pull request reviews #151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151) allows old-side suggestions, this AC is
    updated before coding starts.
*    AC7: Given any markdown editor other than the code comment form (issue or PR conversation
    comment, review summary, editing an existing comment, a reply in an existing conversation), when
    it is shown, then it has no "Suggest change" button.
*    AC8: Given a visitor who is not signed in, or a repository that is archived, when the Files
    tab is shown, then there is no code comment form and so no button (behaviour unchanged,
    regression test).
*    AC9: Given a merged or closed PR, when the reviewer opens the code comment form, then the
    button is shown and works as in AC1 (Gitea still allows code comments there). If the customer
    answers that suggestions on closed PRs should be blocked, this AC is updated before coding.
*    AC10: The button is a keyboard-focusable `<button>` with an accessible name and tooltip
    from a new locale key `repo.diff.comment.suggest_change` (English "Suggest change", added to
    `locale_en-US.json` only).
*    AC11: Given a comment with a suggestion block, when it is submitted, then the stored comment
    content is exactly the textarea text (no server-side change to comment content).
*    AC12: Given a block was already inserted, when the reviewer clicks "Suggest change" again,
    then a second block is inserted at the cursor and the first block is left as is.

### Out of Scope

*   Selecting several lines (S5).
*   Rendering the block as a diff (S1) and applying it (S3).
*   The button in reply forms of an existing conversation. A line that already has a conversation
    has no `+`, so suggestions there wait for a later issue.
*   The legacy EasyMDE editor: switching to it hides the button, and switching back shows it again.
*   Server-side checks on suggestion blocks. The server stores them as plain markdown.

### Open Questions

*   Customer question 5 on [Code suggestions in pull request reviews #151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151): are suggestions on the old (deleted) side allowed? AC6 assumes no.
*   New question for the customer: should a reviewer be able to write a suggestion on a merged or
    closed PR, where it can never be applied? AC9 assumes yes, since the form is already there.

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Read the line text from the diff row already in the DOM (the `.code-inner` cell of
the row the form belongs to, as `textContent`) and insert it with the existing
`replaceTextareaSelection` helper from `EditorMarkdown.ts`; no server call. The button is added to
the shared markdown toolbar only when the editor sits inside a code comment form for the right
side.

**Alternatives Considered:**

*   _Fetch the raw line from the server._ Exact, but a round trip for text already on the page, and a
    new endpoint with its own permission checks.
*   _Server-render the block into the form's initial value._ Forces a suggestion on every comment and
    the reviewer has to delete it for a plain comment.

**Rationale:** The diff row holds the exact text the reviewer is looking at, which is what the
suggestion is anchored to.

**Consequences:** Depends on the diff row markup; highlighted spans must be read as plain text
(`textContent`), and an e2e test guards it. If the markup changes upstream, the e2e test fails
instead of the button inserting the wrong text.

### Decision 2

**Decision:** Build the fences from backticks, one longer than the longest backtick run in the line
and never shorter than 3. The text-building function is pure and unit-tested in Vitest.

**Alternatives Considered:**

*   _Always use 3 backticks._ Breaks on any line holding ` ``` `, such as markdown files or
    code that embeds fenced blocks.
*   _Use a tilde fence (`~~~suggestion`)._ Fails the same way on lines holding `~~~`, and S1's
    renderer would need to accept both fence styles.

**Rationale:** CommonMark closes a fence only on a run at least as long as the opening one, so a
longer opening fence always holds the line, whatever it contains.

**Consequences:** S1 ([#154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154)) reads the rendered `code.language-suggestion` block, and the markdown
renderer gives a longer fence the same element, so longer fences already work there; S1 should
still test one.

### Scope

small

### Scope Justification

Frontend only: one toolbar button in the shared markdown editor template shown for code comment
forms, a small TypeScript module with a pure text builder (Vitest) and the click handler, one
locale key, and one Playwright e2e test. No Go, database, API or permission changes.

Description

[![@vvchopra](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/144284255?v=4&size=48)](https://github.com/vvchopra)

[vvchopra](https://github.com/vvchopra)

opened [on Nov 11, 2026](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/157#issue-6322052718)

Issue body actions

### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of [#151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151) · Depends on S3

As a reviewer, I want to see which of my suggestions were applied, by whom and in which commit,
so that I don't re-check feedback that is already handled.

### User Scenario

After Ben applies Ana's suggestion, her comment shows "Applied by [@ben](https://github.com/ben) in `a1b2c3d`" with a link to
the commit, and the Apply button is gone. A timeline entry "ben applied a suggestion from ana"
appears in the conversation. Ana gets the usual push notification.

### Acceptance Criteria

*    AC1: Given a suggestion is applied, when the comment is shown, then it shows "Applied by
    [@user](https://github.com/user) in " linking to the commit, and no Apply button.
*    AC2: Given an applied suggestion, when anyone POSTs Apply again, then nothing is committed and
    "already applied" is returned.
*    AC3: Given an instance upgraded from a version without this feature, when existing review
    comments are shown, then they render as before and none is marked applied (migration test).
*    AC4: Given the applying commit is later removed by a force-push, when the comment is shown,
    then it still shows "Applied" with the SHA, and the SHA is not a broken link (shown unlinked).
*    AC5: Given the comment is deleted after being applied, when the PR is viewed, then the commit
    remains and no error occurs.
*    AC6: If the customer answers yes to question 3, then applying resolves the conversation.

### Out of Scope

*   Undoing an applied suggestion (revert it like any other commit).

### Open Questions

*   Customer question 3.

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Add nullable columns to `comment`: `suggestion_applied_by` (user ID),
`suggestion_applied_commit` (SHA) and `suggestion_applied_unix`, set in the same transaction as the
timeline entry, with a migration.

**Alternatives Considered:**

*   _A separate `review_suggestion` table, one row per suggestion._ Cleaner once S6 batches several
    per comment, but S1 allows one applyable suggestion per comment, so it is a join for nothing now.
*   _Store nothing; detect "applied" by comparing the current file to the suggestion._ No migration,
    but wrong when the same text arrives another way, and can't say who applied it.

**Rationale:** One applyable suggestion per comment makes the columns a direct fit, and the
migration is additive with safe zero values for old rows (AC3).

**Consequences:** A schema migration (`docs/models-migrations.md`). If multiple applyable
suggestions per comment are ever allowed, these columns must move to their own table.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

Some DB work

Description

[![@vvchopra](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/144284255?v=4&size=48)](https://github.com/vvchopra)

[vvchopra](https://github.com/vvchopra)

opened [on Nov 11, 2026](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/158#issue-6322067443)

Issue body actions

### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of [#151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151) · Depends on S1, S3

As a reviewer, I want to select a range of lines and suggest a replacement for all of them so that
I can propose changes bigger than one line.

### User Scenario

Ana shift-clicks lines 18 to 22 in the Files tab, clicks `+`, then "Suggest change". The block is
pre-filled with those five lines. She rewrites them as three lines. Ben sees a five-red /
three-green diff and applies it.

### Acceptance Criteria

*    AC1: Given a reviewer shift-selects a contiguous range of new-side lines in one hunk, when
    they open the comment form, then the comment is anchored to the whole range and the header says
    "Lines 18–22".
*    AC2: Given a multi-line suggestion, when rendered, then all lines in the range show as
    removed and the block's lines as added (S1 behaviour for a range).
*    AC3: Given a multi-line suggestion, when applied, then exactly that range is replaced, and it
    is refused as outdated if any line in the range changed (S3 AC3 for a range).
*    AC4: Given a selection that spans two hunks or both sides of the diff, when the reviewer tries
    to comment, then the selection is refused with a message.
*    AC5: Given existing single-line comments after the upgrade, when shown and applied, then they
    behave exactly as before (range start = line).

### Out of Scope

*   Ranges across files.

### Open Questions

*   Maximum range length? (Proposed: the hunk's size; no separate cap.)

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Add a `start_line` column to `comment` (0 = single-line, as today) and keep `Line` as
the range end, so every existing comment is a valid single-line range.

**Alternatives Considered:**

*   _Store the range inside the comment body or a JSON column._ No schema change, but the range
    can't be queried or invalidated with the existing code.
*   _Create one linked comment per line._ Breaks the "one comment, one suggestion" model from S4.

**Rationale:** `Line` keeps its meaning, so `InvalidateCodeComments`, the API and old rows are
untouched; only code that cares about ranges reads `start_line`.

**Consequences:** Migration; `InvalidateCodeComments` should consider the whole range; S7's API
gains a start-line field.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

DB work

    Spec reviewed — [@controlled-opposition](https://github.com/controlled-opposition)

    **Acceptance criteria:**

    *   AC1: testable. The selection rule (contiguous, new side, one hunk) and the "Lines 18–22" header are concrete.
    *   AC2: testable once it stands on its own. "S1 behaviour for a range" sends the reader to another issue. Please state it: all N selected lines show as removed and the block's lines as added.
    *   AC3: two behaviours in one AC (the exact range is replaced; the suggestion is refused if any line in the range changed), and "S3 AC3 for a range" has the same cross-reference problem. Suggest splitting into AC3a and AC3b and spelling both out.
    *   AC4: two cases in one AC (spans two hunks, spans both sides), and "a message" has no text. Please give the message, or one AC per case.
    *   AC5: testable and good. It covers existing rows after the migration.

    **Cases considered:**

    *   Covered: multi-line range, cross-hunk and cross-side selection, existing single-line comments, a changed line inside the range.
    *   Not covered by any AC: a selection made upward (shift-click above the start), a one-line "range" (start equals end), an empty replacement block (deleting the lines), a replacement with a different line count than the range (the scenario shows 5 to 3, but no AC checks it), and a range reaching the end of the file.
    *   Please add the ones you intend to handle or list the rest under Out of Scope.

    **Scope:**

    *   The justification ("DB work") is a fragment. Please give the one or two sentences of why: migration, selection UI, rendering, apply and invalidation all change.
    *   Medium is plausible but at the top of the range. Say what is cut if it runs long.
    *   Name the dependencies by number: S1 ([S1. Render `suggestion` blocks in review comments as a diff #154](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/154)), S3 ([S3. Apply a single suggestion as a commit on the PR branch #156](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/156)).

    **Other:**

    *   The Open Question (maximum range length) proposes an answer. Please resolve it and add an AC if a cap stays.
    *   The Design Decision names two alternatives and a reason, which meets D3.
    *   The issue was not on the `Sprint 3` milestone; I have added it.

    **Verdict:** Changes needed: split AC3 and AC4, make AC2 and AC3 self-contained, add or scope out the missing cases, fix the scope justification.

Description
-----------

[![@vvchopra](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/144284255?v=4&size=48)](https://github.com/vvchopra)

[vvchopra](https://github.com/vvchopra)

opened [on Nov 11, 2026](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/159#issue-6322179744)

Issue body actions

### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of [#151](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/151) · Depends on S3, S4

As a PR author, I want to pick several suggestions and apply them together so that my branch gets
one commit instead of one per suggestion.

### User Scenario

Ana leaves four suggestions on two files. Ben clicks **Add to batch** on three of them; a bar at the
bottom shows "3 suggestions selected · Apply". He applies them and the PR gets one commit changing
both files, and all three comments are marked applied.

### Acceptance Criteria

*    AC1: Given several selected suggestions, when applied, then one commit containing all of
    them is added and each is marked applied (S4) with that commit.
*    AC2: Given two selected suggestions whose lines overlap, when the user tries to add the second
    to the batch, then it is refused with "overlaps another suggestion in this batch".
*    AC3: Given one suggestion in the batch is outdated, when applied, then nothing is committed
    and the outdated one is named (all or nothing).
*    AC4: Given the batch is left unapplied and the page is reloaded, then the batch is empty (it
    is not stored server-side).
*    AC5: Permission, closed/merged PR and stale head rules are the same as S3.

### Out of Scope

*   Batches across PRs; saving a batch for later.

### Open Questions

*   Is there a maximum batch size? (Proposed: 50.)

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Generalise S3's service to take a list of comment IDs and build one
`ChangeRepoFiles` call with one entry per file, applying edits in a file bottom-up so earlier
replacements don't shift later line numbers.

**Alternatives Considered:**

*   _Apply each suggestion as its own commit in a loop._ Easy, but not atomic: a failure halfway
    leaves a partial result, and it is not what the user asked for.
*   _Store pending batches server-side._ Survives reloads, but needs a table and cleanup for
    something the user does in one sitting.

**Rationale:** One `ChangeRepoFiles` call is a single atomic commit, and bottom-up edits are a
simple, testable way to avoid line drift.

**Consequences:** S3's function signature changes; S7's batch endpoint reuses it.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

Touches a few different components

    [![@controlled-opposition](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/207494180?u=d0e136f74fc01c784c5f25251f31e67ff56a9068&v=4&size=48)](/controlled-opposition)

    Collaborator

    More actions

    Spec reviewed — [@controlled-opposition](https://github.com/controlled-opposition)

    **Acceptance criteria:**

    *   AC1: testable. One commit, all suggestions marked applied with that commit.
    *   AC2: testable. The refusal message is exact.
    *   AC3: testable. All or nothing, and the outdated one is named.
    *   AC4: testable by reloading the page, but state how the test checks it (a UI or E2E check, since there is no server state to assert).
    *   AC5: "same as S3" sends the reader to another issue and bundles three rules (permission, closed or merged PR, stale head). Please state each, ideally one AC per rule with its expected response.

    **Cases considered:**

    *   Covered: several suggestions, overlap, one outdated suggestion, reload.
    *   Not covered by any AC: two suggestions in one file that change line counts differently (the design relies on bottom-up edits to avoid line drift, but no AC tests it), a suggestion that was already applied, a batch of one, an empty batch (is Apply hidden or disabled?), the same suggestion added twice, and a batch larger than the maximum (the Open Question proposes 50 but no AC enforces it).
    *   The overlap check (AC2) needs ranges, so the issue depends on S5 ([S5. Suggest a change across several lines #158](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/158)) as well as S3 and S4.

    **Scope:**

    *   The justification ("Touches a few different components") is a fragment. Please name the components and give the one or two sentences of why.
    *   Medium fits: one service change, one UI bar, one commit.
    *   Name the dependencies by number: S3 ([S3. Apply a single suggestion as a commit on the PR branch #156](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/156)), S4 ([S4. Record and show that a suggestion was applied #157](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/157)), S5 ([S5. Suggest a change across several lines #158](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/158)).

    **Other:**

    *   The Design Decision names two alternatives and a reason, which meets D3.
    *   The issue was not on the `Sprint 3` milestone; I have added it.

    **Verdict:** Changes needed: make AC5 explicit, add the line-drift and already-applied cases, resolve the batch-size question, add the S5 dependency, fix the scope justification.

opened [on Nov 11, 2026](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/160#issue-6322249655)

Issue body actions

### User Story

As a bot or tool author, I want to create suggestions and apply them through `/api/v1` so that
automated reviewers (linters, formatters) can propose fixes that the author applies in Gitea.

### User Scenario

A lint bot posts a review via `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{index}/reviews` with a comment
whose body has a suggestion block. Ben applies it in the UI. A release script calls
`POST .../pulls/comments/{id}/suggestion/apply` to apply another one.

### Acceptance Criteria

*    AC1: Given a review created through the existing API with a suggestion block in a code
    comment, when viewed in the UI, then it renders as a suggestion and can be applied (no API
    change needed; integration test proves it).
*    AC2: Given a token with `write:repository` and push access to the head branch, when it POSTs
    the apply endpoint, then the commit is created and the response contains the commit SHA.
*    AC3: Given missing permission, an outdated suggestion, an already applied one, or a stale
    `head_sha`, when the endpoint is called, then it returns 403 / 409 / 409 / 409 with a message and
    commits nothing.
*    AC4: Given `GET` on a review comment, when the suggestion was applied, then the response
    includes `suggestion_applied_by` and `suggestion_applied_commit`.
*    AC5: Swagger is regenerated and the swagger check passes.

### Out of Scope

*   A batch apply endpoint, unless S6 has landed (then add `comment_ids[]`).

### Open Questions

*   Should the API also accept a structured `suggestion` field instead of only markdown in `body`?

### Design Decision

**Decision:** No new create endpoint: suggestions stay markdown in the comment body. Add one apply
endpoint that takes `head_sha` and an optional `message` and calls S3's service.

**Alternatives Considered:**

*   _A structured create endpoint (`path`, `lines`, `replacement`)._ Easier for bots, but two ways to
    author the same thing that must render identically.
*   _Mirror GitHub's API shape exactly._ GitHub has no apply endpoint to mirror.

**Rationale:** Bots already post review comments through the existing API, so they get
suggestions for free, and the service layer is shared with the UI.

**Consequences:** New route and swagger entry (`docs/routers-api-v1.md`), new fields on the comment
API struct (`docs/modules-structs.md`).

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

Touches multiple components. Builds off S3

    Spec reviewed — [@controlled-opposition](https://github.com/controlled-opposition)

    **Acceptance criteria:**

    *   AC1: testable. The setup is concrete (a review posted through the existing API with a suggestion block) and the outcome is observable (renders and can be applied). PR [test(api): prove suggestions posted through the reviews API render as suggestions (#160) #164](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/pull/164) already proves the "renders" half. The "can be applied" half waits on the apply endpoint.
    *   AC2: testable. The token scope, the head-branch push access and the expected result (commit SHA in the response) are all stated.
    *   AC3: clear but too big for one criterion. It packs four failure cases (403 / 409 / 409 / 409) into one AC, so one test row can't show which case failed. Suggest splitting into AC3a to AC3d, or one AC per status code.
    *   AC4: testable. The two field names are given. It depends on S4 ([S4. Record and show that a suggestion was applied #157](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/157)) recording the applied state, which should be said in the AC.
    *   AC5: testable. The swagger check passing is binary.

    **Cases considered:**

    *   Covered: missing permission, outdated suggestion, already-applied suggestion, stale `head_sha`.
    *   Not covered by any AC: unauthenticated request (401), comment ID that doesn't exist or isn't on a PR in this repo (404), a comment with no suggestion block, a closed or merged PR, and an omitted `message` (what is the default commit message?).
    *   Please add the ones you intend to handle, or list the rest under Out of Scope.

    **Scope:**

    *   Medium fits: one endpoint, two new response fields and swagger.
    *   The scope justification ("Touches multiple components. Builds off S3") is a fragment. Please spell out the "why" in one or two sentences.
    *   The dependency on S3 ([S3. Apply a single suggestion as a commit on the PR branch #156](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/156)) and S4 ([S4. Record and show that a suggestion was applied #157](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/157)) should be named with issue numbers.

    **Other:**

    *   The Open Question about a structured `suggestion` field is already answered by the Design Decision (not adding one). Please remove it or mark it resolved.
    *   The Design Decision names two alternatives and picks one with a reason, which meets D3.

    **Verdict:** Changes needed: split AC3, add or scope out the missing cases, fix the scope justification and the stale open question.

func GetRawDiff(repo *Repository, commitID string, diffType RawDiffType, writer io.Writer) (retErr error) {
	cmd, err := getRepoRawDiffForFileCmd(repo.Ctx, repo, "", commitID, diffType, "")
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("getRepoRawDiffForFileCmd: %w", err)
	}
	return cmd.WithStdoutCopy(writer).RunWithStderr(repo.Ctx)
}

// GetFileDiffCutAroundLine cuts the old or new part of the diff of a file around a specific line number
func GetFileDiffCutAroundLine(
	repo *Repository, startCommit, endCommit, treePath string,
	line int64, old bool, numbersOfLine int,
) (ret string, retErr error) {
	cmd, err := getRepoRawDiffForFileCmd(repo.Ctx, repo, startCommit, endCommit, RawDiffNormal, treePath)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("getRepoRawDiffForFileCmd: %w", err)
	}
	stdoutReader, stdoutClose := cmd.MakeStdoutPipe()
	defer stdoutClose()
	cmd.WithPipelineFunc(func(ctx gitcmd.Context) error {
		ret, err = CutDiffAroundLine(stdoutReader, line, old, numbersOfLine)
		return err
	})
	return ret, cmd.RunWithStderr(repo.Ctx)
}

// CutDiffAroundLine cuts a diff of a file in way that only the given line + numberOfLine above it will be shown
// it also recalculates hunks and adds the appropriate headers to the new diff.
// Warning: Only one-file diffs are allowed.
func CutDiffAroundLine(originalDiff io.Reader, line int64, old bool, numbersOfLine int) (string, error) {
	if line == 0 || numbersOfLine == 0 {
		// no line or num of lines => no diff
		return "", nil
	}

	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(originalDiff)
	hunk := make([]string, 0)

	// begin is the start of the hunk containing searched line
	// end is the end of the hunk ...
	// currentLine is the line number on the side of the searched line (differentiated by old)
	// otherLine is the line number on the opposite side of the searched line (differentiated by old)
	var begin, end, currentLine, otherLine int64
	var headerLines int

	inHunk := false

	for scanner.Scan() {
		lof := scanner.Text()
		// Add header to enable parsing

		if isHeader(lof, inHunk) {
			if strings.HasPrefix(lof, cmdDiffHead) {
				inHunk = false
			}
			hunk = append(hunk, lof)
			headerLines++
		}
		if currentLine > line {
			break
		}
		// Detect "hunk" with contains commented lof
		if strings.HasPrefix(lof, "@@") {
			inHunk = true
			// Already got our hunk. End of hunk detected!
			if len(hunk) > headerLines {
				break
			}
			// A map with named groups of our regex to recognize them later more easily
			submatches := hunkRegex.FindStringSubmatch(lof)
			groups := make(map[string]string)
			for i, name := range hunkRegex.SubexpNames() {
				if i != 0 && name != "" {
					groups[name] = submatches[i]
				}
			}
			if old {
				begin, _ = strconv.ParseInt(groups["beginOld"], 10, 64)
				end, _ = strconv.ParseInt(groups["endOld"], 10, 64)
				// init otherLine with begin of opposite side
				otherLine, _ = strconv.ParseInt(groups["beginNew"], 10, 64)
			} else {
				begin, _ = strconv.ParseInt(groups["beginNew"], 10, 64)
				if groups["endNew"] != "" {
					end, _ = strconv.ParseInt(groups["endNew"], 10, 64)
				} else {
					end = 0
				}
				// init otherLine with begin of opposite side
				otherLine, _ = strconv.ParseInt(groups["beginOld"], 10, 64)
			}
			end += begin // end is for real only the number of lines in hunk
			// lof is between begin and end
			if begin <= line && end >= line {
				hunk = append(hunk, lof)
				currentLine = begin
				continue
			}
		} else if len(hunk) > headerLines {
			hunk = append(hunk, lof)
			// Count lines in context
			switch lof[0] {
			case '+':
				if !old {
					currentLine++
				} else {
					otherLine++
				}
			case '-':
				if old {
					currentLine++
				} else {
					otherLine++
				}

// CodeComments represents comments on code by using this structure: FILENAME -> LINE (+ == proposed; - == previous) -> COMMENTS
type CodeComments map[string]map[int64][]*Comment

// FetchCodeComments will return a 2d-map: ["Path"]["Line"] = Comments at line
func FetchCodeComments(ctx context.Context, issue *Issue, currentUser *user_model.User, showOutdatedComments bool) (CodeComments, error) {
	return fetchCodeCommentsByReview(ctx, issue, currentUser, nil, showOutdatedComments)
}

func fetchCodeCommentsByReview(ctx context.Context, issue *Issue, currentUser *user_model.User, review *Review, showOutdatedComments bool) (CodeComments, error) {
	pathToLineToComment := make(CodeComments)
	if review == nil {
		review = &Review{ID: 0}
	}
	opts := FindCommentsOptions{
		Type:     CommentTypeCode,
		IssueID:  issue.ID,
		ReviewID: review.ID,
	}

	comments, err := findCodeComments(ctx, opts, issue, currentUser, review, showOutdatedComments)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	for _, comment := range comments {
		if pathToLineToComment[comment.TreePath] == nil {
			pathToLineToComment[comment.TreePath] = make(map[int64][]*Comment)
		}
		pathToLineToComment[comment.TreePath][comment.Line] = append(pathToLineToComment[comment.TreePath][comment.Line], comment)
	}
	return pathToLineToComment, nil
}

func findCodeComments(ctx context.Context, opts FindCommentsOptions, issue *Issue, currentUser *user_model.User, review *Review, showOutdatedComments bool) ([]*Comment, error) {
	var comments CommentList
	if review == nil {
		review = &Review{ID: 0}
	}
	conds := opts.ToConds()

	if !showOutdatedComments && review.ID == 0 {
		conds = conds.And(builder.Eq{"invalidated": false})
	}

	e := db.GetEngine(ctx)
	if err := e.Where(conds).
		Asc("comment.created_unix").
		Asc("comment.id").
		Find(&comments); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	if err := issue.LoadRepo(ctx); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	if err := comments.LoadPosters(ctx); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	if err := comments.LoadAttachments(ctx); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	if err := comments.loadResolveDoers(ctx); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	if err := comments.loadReactions(ctx, issue.Repo); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	// Find all reviews by ReviewID
	reviews := make(map[int64]*Review)
	ids := make([]int64, 0, len(comments))
	for _, comment := range comments {
		if comment.ReviewID != 0 {
			ids = append(ids, comment.ReviewID)
		}
	}
	if len(ids) > 0 {
		if err := e.In("id", ids).Find(&reviews); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}

	n := 0
	for _, comment := range comments {
		if re, ok := reviews[comment.ReviewID]; ok && re != nil {
			// If the review is pending only the author can see the comments (except if the review is set)
			if review.ID == 0 && re.Type == ReviewTypePending &&
				(currentUser == nil || currentUser.ID != re.ReviewerID) {
				continue
			}
			comment.Review = re
			comment.Issue = issue
		}
		comments[n] = comment
		n++

		var err error
		rctx := renderhelper.NewRenderContextRepoComment(ctx, issue.Repo, renderhelper.RepoCommentOptions{
			FootnoteContextID: strconv.FormatInt(comment.ID, 10),
		})
		if comment.RenderedContent, err = markdown.RenderString(rctx, comment.Content); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}
	return comments[:n], nil
}

		IssueID:  issue.ID,
		TreePath: treePath,
		Line:     line,
	}
	return findCodeComments(ctx, opts, issue, currentUser, nil, showOutdatedComments)

// LoadComments loads comments into each line
func (diff *Diff) LoadComments(ctx context.Context, issue *issues_model.Issue, currentUser *user_model.User, showOutdatedComments bool) error {
	allComments, err := issues_model.FetchCodeComments(ctx, issue, currentUser, showOutdatedComments)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	for _, file := range diff.Files {
		if lineCommits, ok := allComments[file.Name]; ok {
			for _, section := range file.Sections {
				for _, line := range section.Lines {
					if comments, ok := lineCommits[int64(line.LeftIdx*-1)]; ok {
						line.Comments = append(line.Comments, comments...)
					}
					if comments, ok := lineCommits[int64(line.RightIdx)]; ok {
						line.Comments = append(line.Comments, comments...)
					}
					sort.SliceStable(line.Comments, func(i, j int) bool {
						return line.Comments[i].CreatedUnix < line.Comments[j].CreatedUnix
					})
					// Mark expand buttons that have comments in hidden lines
					FillHiddenCommentIDsForDiffLine(line, lineCommits)
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// GeneratePatchForUnchangedLine creates a patch showing code context for an unchanged line
func GeneratePatchForUnchangedLine(gitRepo *git.Repository, commitID, treePath string, line int64, contextLines int) (string, error) {
	commit, err := gitRepo.GetCommit(commitID)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("GetCommit: %w", err)
	}

	entry, err := commit.GetTreeEntryByPath(treePath)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("GetTreeEntryByPath: %w", err)
	}

	blob := entry.Blob()
	dataRc, err := blob.DataAsync()
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("DataAsync: %w", err)
	}
	defer dataRc.Close()

	return generatePatchForUnchangedLineFromReader(dataRc, treePath, line, contextLines)
}

// generatePatchForUnchangedLineFromReader is the testable core logic that generates a patch from a reader
func generatePatchForUnchangedLineFromReader(reader io.Reader, treePath string, line int64, contextLines int) (string, error) {
	// Calculate line range (commented line + lines above it)
	commentLine := int(line)
	if line < 0 {
		commentLine = int(-line)
	}
	startLine := max(commentLine-contextLines, 1)
	endLine := commentLine

	// Read only the needed lines efficiently
	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(reader)
	currentLine := 0
	var lines []string
	for scanner.Scan() {
		currentLine++
		if currentLine >= startLine && currentLine <= endLine {
			lines = append(lines, scanner.Text())
		}
		if currentLine > endLine {
			break
		}
	}
	if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("scanner error: %w", err)
	}

	if len(lines) == 0 {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("no lines found in range %d-%d", startLine, endLine)
	}

	// Generate synthetic patch
	var patchBuilder strings.Builder
	fmt.Fprintf(&patchBuilder, "diff --git a/%s b/%s\n", treePath, treePath)
	fmt.Fprintf(&patchBuilder, "--- a/%s\n", treePath)

**#156: S3. Apply a single suggestion as a commit on the PR branch**
- State: Open. Assignee: CarsonRackley. Milestone: Sprint 3. Labels: enhancement, scope: medium.
- PR: none. The Development section says "No branches or pull requests," and no PR is referenced in the comments.
- The issue says it depends on #154, which was merged in #168.

Acceptance criteria, verbatim. The issue's markdown links are shown as issue numbers.

Preface: "Errors from the Apply POST are returned the way Gitea's other web forms return them: HTTP 400 with the message shown on the page, unless an AC says otherwise."

- AC1: "Given a suggestion on a single line, in a review comment or a reply in its thread, and a user who can push to the head branch, when they apply it, then exactly one commit is added to the head branch that replaces only that line, exactly as #154's diff shows it (AC12). The form is prefilled with the default message "Apply suggestion from @ on " and can be edited: the commit uses the submitted message, or the default if the message is submitted empty."
- AC2: "Given a viewer who can't push to the head branch (read-only, or a fork PR without "Allow edits from maintainers"), when the PR is shown, then there is no Apply button, and a direct POST returns 403 and commits nothing (#151 AC3). A signed-out viewer sees no Apply button, and a direct POST redirects to sign-in and commits nothing. Pending customer question 2 on #151; see Open Questions for the default."
- AC3: "Given the commented line's text at the current head differs from the line the suggestion was written against, or the file was deleted or renamed at head, or the line number is now past the end of the file, when someone applies it, then nothing is committed and they see "This suggestion is outdated: the code changed since it was written.""
- AC4: "Given the head branch moved between page load and Apply (someone pushed, or another suggestion was applied), when Apply is submitted with the old head SHA, then nothing is committed and they see "This branch has new commits since the page was loaded. Reload the page and try again." This holds whether or not the new commits touched the suggestion's file. The head SHA sent is the PR's head when the page loaded, even when the Files tab is showing a single earlier commit."
- AC5: "Given the PR is closed or merged, or its head branch was deleted, when the PR is shown, then there is no Apply button, and a direct POST commits nothing and returns 400 with "Suggestions can only be applied to an open pull request whose branch still exists.""
- AC6: "Given the head branch is protected against this user's push, when they apply, then nothing is committed and they see Gitea's existing message `Cannot commit to protected branch "<branch>".` (the same check and text as the web editor), not the raw pre-receive output."
- AC7: "Given a comment with zero or several suggestion blocks, or a comment on an old-side (deleted) line, which #154 AC7 renders as an ordinary code block, when shown, then there is no Apply button."
- AC8: "The commit's author and committer follow the customer's answer to question 1, and a test asserts them. Pending customer question 1 on #151; see Open Questions for the default."
- AC9: "Given an outdated review comment (its code changed in a later push), when shown, then its suggestion has no Apply button. A POST from a page loaded before the change is handled by AC3/AC4."
- AC10: "Given a suggestion identical to the current line, when someone applies it, then no commit is made and they see "This suggestion makes no changes to the code.""
- AC11: "Given a file with CRLF line endings or no final newline, when a suggestion on it is applied, then the changed line keeps the file's line ending and the file's final-newline state is unchanged; no other byte of the file changes."
- AC12: "Given the suggestion block is empty, has one blank line, or has several lines, when it is applied, then the commit deletes the line, replaces it with a blank line, or replaces it with those lines in order, matching #154 AC2's diff. No line before or after it changes."

Note: the #151 AC3 that AC2 cites is the rule "Given a user who can't push to the PR branch, when they try to apply a suggestion, then nothing is committed and they see why."

**#154: S1. Render `suggestion` blocks in review comments as a diff**
- State: Closed (closed as completed by #168 on Nov 12, 2026). Assignee: vvchopra. Milestone: Sprint 3.
- Linked PRs: #168 (merged, closed the issue) and #163 (merged, then reverted by #166, then re-landed through #168). The commits come from branch `feat/issue-154-suggestion-diff`.

Acceptance criteria, verbatim:
- AC1: "Given a code comment on a new-side line whose body has one ```suggestion block, when the comment is shown in the Conversation or Files changed tab, then the block renders as a diff headed "Suggested change": the commented line as removed (red) and each line of the block as added (green), with indentation kept."
- AC2: "Given an empty ```suggestion block, when rendered, then it shows the commented line as removed and nothing added (a "delete this line" suggestion)."
- AC3: "Given a ```suggestion block in a plain issue or PR comment (not a code comment), when rendered, then it shows as an ordinary code block, not a diff."
- AC4: "Given a code comment with two or more suggestion blocks, when rendered, then each block renders as its own diff against the same commented line. (S3 decides whether to offer Apply.)"
- AC5: "Given suggestion content containing HTML such as <script>alert(1)</script>, when rendered, then it is shown as literal text and nothing is executed."
- AC6: "Given an outdated code comment (the branch moved and the comment is Invalidated), when rendered, then the diff is still shown against the line the reviewer originally commented on, next to the existing "Outdated" label."
- AC7: "Given a code comment on an old-side (deleted) line, or one whose stored diff context is missing, when rendered, then the suggestion block shows as an ordinary code block and the page has no errors."
- AC8: "Given a code comment with a suggestion is edited, when the edit is saved, then the updated block renders as a diff without reloading the page."

# AI Logs

This folder holds every AI session for each sprint, one folder per student. The course rules are on
the [AI Log Instructions](https://csci-435-se.github.io/ai-logs/) page and the current sprint page
at <https://csci-435-se.github.io/>. This README is the team's shared convention for following them.

## What to log

Every AI session tied to this project: code, debugging, tests, reviews, drafting issues and PRs,
design discussion, the sprint report. That includes sessions that went nowhere. Purely academic
questions unrelated to the project don't need logging.

## Structure

```
ai-logs/
  sprint<N>/
    <github-username>/                          ← exact GitHub username, matching case
      .gitkeep                                  ← the folder must exist even if you used no AI
      YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md
      YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>/           ← attachments (images, etc.), optional
```

Team folders: `ab-wm`, `arjunsb26`, `CarsonRackley`, `controlled-opposition`, `Jack-Donohue`,
`vvchopra`.

## Naming

`YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`

- **Date:** the day the session started.
- **Sprint folder:** the sprint that date falls in, not the sprint the work is for.
- **Tool:** one of the course identifiers: `claude-code`, `claude-web`, `claude-desktop`, `cursor`,
  `gemini-cli`, `codex-cli`, `copilot`, `chatgpt`, `other-<name>`. Claude Code run inside VS Code is
  `claude-code`.
- **Slug:** lowercase words joined with hyphens that say what the session did. Put the issue number
  first when there is one: `issue-52-impl`, `issue-52-spec`, `pr-61-review`, `sprint1-report`.
  Replace auto-generated slugs such as `local-command-caveat...`.
- **Formats:** `.md` is preferred; `.txt` and `.json` are also accepted. No `.docx`, `.pdf`, `.html`
  or share links.

## Capturing a session

| Tool | How |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code (terminal or VS Code), other agentic CLIs | Start it with [SpecStory](https://specstory.com/): `specstory run claude`, from the repo root. Forgot? Run `specstory sync` afterwards; it back-fills from Claude Code's local history. Then copy from `.specstory/history/` (git-ignored) into your folder and rename it to the convention. |
| Web chat (claude.ai, ChatGPT, Gemini, ...) | Install a browser chat exporter and export the session as Markdown right after it ends. Include any files you pasted in as context. |
| Claude Desktop | SpecStory doesn't capture it. Copy the conversation into a `.md` file by hand. |

At the end of each sprint, run `specstory sync` once more and re-copy. A log copied mid-session is
incomplete.

## Content

- The **tool and AI model** used (SpecStory writes both).
- The **complete** prompt and response history. For agentic tools, that includes file edits and
  commands (SpecStory includes them). Logs with missing responses or truncated histories are
  **invalid**. Don't hand-write, summarise or trim a log; only rename it.
- These are **not** logs and get no full credit: a summary of a session, paraphrased prompts, a
  share link to a chat, or tool output without the prompts that produced it (Sprint 3 page).

## Question 2: What is one thing you learned about testing in your project?

I learned that a passing test only proves something once you have seen it fail. My test passed on the first run. To check it, I swapped S1's two templates back to the `main` versions and ran it again. Both the Files tab and the Conversation tab subtests failed, which shows they really depend on the feature. I also took every expected value from the input the test writes itself (the README line and the suggestion text), not from what the code printed. A test that copies the code's own output would pass even if the code were wrong. Finally, Gitea's integration tests need a built `gitea` binary, because the git hooks call it.

comment. Nothing gets posted by Claude.

**Revised issue body.** Same format as now, with these changes:

- **User Scenario:** Ana clicks line 18's number, shift-clicks line 22's, then clicks `+` and
  "Suggest change". The block holds lines 18–22, and she rewrites them as three lines. Ben sees 5
  red lines and 3 green. Applying it is S3.
- **Acceptance Criteria:**
  - AC1: Given a reviewer clicks new-side line 18's number and shift-clicks line 22's in one hunk,
    when they click `+` on line 22, then the form header reads "Lines 18–22". After posting, the
    thread sits under line 22 with the same header.
  - AC2: Given an upward selection (22, then shift-click 18), the result is the same as AC1:
    "Lines 18–22".
  - AC3: Given a one-line selection (start = end, or no shift-click), when posted, then it is an
    ordinary single-line comment with no "Lines" header.
  - AC4: Given a range form for 18–22, when "Suggest change" is clicked, then the block holds lines
    18–22 in order, with indentation kept.
  - AC5: Given a comment on 18–22 with a 3-line suggestion, when shown in Files changed or
    Conversation, then the diff shows 18–22 as 5 removed lines in order, then the 3 lines as added.
  - AC6: Given a comment on 18–22 with an empty suggestion block, when shown, then all 5 lines show
    as removed and nothing as added.
  - AC7: Given a comment on 18–22, when a push changes the text of any one line from 18 to 22 (the
    first, a middle or the last), then the comment is marked Outdated.
  - AC8: Given a comment on 18–22, when a push changes only lines after 22, then it is not marked
    Outdated.
  - AC9: Given a range ending on the file's last line, when a push deletes that line or the whole
    file, then the comment is marked Outdated.
  - AC10: Given a shift-click that would cross a hunk header, or take in expanded context lines,
    then no range is selected and the reviewer sees "A comment can only cover lines on one side of a
    single hunk."
  - AC11: Given a selection running from an old-side (deleted) line to a new-side line, then it is
    refused with the same message.
  - AC12: Given a direct POST with start > end, an old-side range, or a range outside one hunk, then
    the server returns 400 with the AC10 message and saves nothing.
  - AC13: Given single-line comments created before this change, when shown and when their line
    changes, then they render and go Outdated exactly as before.
- **Out of Scope:**
  - Ranges across files.
  - Old-side ranges.
  - Applying a range: S3 #156 and S6 #159 read the start line.
  - The API start-line field: S7 #160.
  - Drag-selecting.
  - Ranges on expanded context.
  - Following a range when lines are inserted above it. It goes Outdated, as single-line comments
    do today.
- **Open Questions:** None. The maximum range is resolved as the hunk, with no separate cap, so
  AC10 enforces it.
- **Design Decision 1 (start-line storage):**
  - Decision: store `StartLine` in `CommentMetaData`, absent meaning single-line. `Line` stays the
    range end.
  - Alternatives:
    - A `start_line` column. It needs migration 346 and goes against the repo convention, and
      nothing filters by start line in SQL.
    - One comment per line. This breaks "one comment, one suggestion".
  - Rationale: `Line`, `FetchCodeComments` keying, replies and the API all stay untouched.
  - Consequences: start line can't be queried in SQL, and S3/S6/S7 read it through a helper.
- **Design Decision 2 (range invalidation):**
  - Decision: for ranges, compare the text of lines start..end at head with the range lines stored
    in the comment's patch. Single-line comments keep blame.
  - Alternatives:
    - Blame every line. One `CommitSHA` can't hold a commit per line.
    - Store the head SHA and diff old head → new head, mapping hunks onto the range. This is
      accurate when lines shift, but needs a git diff per comment per push, and more code.
  - Rationale: same rule as S3 AC3 ("the line's text differs").
  - Consequences: one blob read per range comment per push. A line rewritten to the same text isn't
    flagged.
- **Scope:** medium. It touches the comment model helpers, the code-comment POST path (form, router,
  `services/pull/review.go` patch cutting and invalidation), the diff page JS and templates
  (selection, header, prefill) and S1's renderer. That's about 10 files plus tests, with no new
  endpoint or table. Depends on S1 #154 and S2 #155, both merged.

**Reply comment.** Lists each review point and how it was addressed, notes that apply moved to
S3/S6, and asks controlled-opposition to re-check. It ends with an authorship line, and the user
edits it before posting.

#158 (owner Jack-Donohue, Sprint 3, `scope: medium`, parent #151) got a "Changes needed" spec review
from controlled-opposition. The review asked for five things:

- Split AC3 and AC4.
- Make AC2 and AC3 stand on their own, without pointing at S1/S3.
- Add the missing cases, or list them as out of scope: upward selection, start = end, empty block,
  5→3 line count, end of file.

- S1 #154 (render suggestions as a diff) and S2 #155 (Suggest change button) are merged on `main`.

  renderer, the S2 prefill and blame-based invalidation.

afterwards based on feedback.

   Scope (S3 #156 / S6 #159).

   convention (`models-issues.md:62`, `comment.go:245`). There is no migration, and old rows stay
   single-line by construction. The issue's Design Decision gets rewritten to match.
