```markdown
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on #154 (S1) and #155 (S2), both merged

As a reviewer, I want to select a range of lines and suggest a replacement for all of them so that
I can propose changes bigger than one line.

### User Scenario

Ana opens the Files changed tab of a pull request. She clicks the number of new-side line 18,
shift-clicks the number of line 22, then clicks `+` on line 22. The comment form is headed
"Lines 18–22". She clicks "Suggest change", and the block is pre-filled with those five lines. She
rewrites them as three lines and posts. Ben opens the PR and sees a "Suggested change" diff with
five red lines and three green ones. (Applying it is S3 #156.)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a reviewer clicks the number of new-side line 18 and shift-clicks the number of
  new-side line 22 in the same hunk, when they click `+` on line 22, then the comment form's header
  reads "Lines 18–22"; after posting, the comment's thread appears under line 22 with the header
  "Lines 18–22".
- [ ] AC2: Given a reviewer selects upward (clicks line 22, then shift-clicks line 18), when they
  click `+` on line 22, then the header reads "Lines 18–22" and the comment is saved for lines
  18–22, the same as AC1.
- [ ] AC3: Given a one-line selection (shift-clicking the line already selected, or clicking `+`
  with no selection), when the comment is posted, then it is an ordinary single-line comment with no
  "Lines" header.
- [ ] AC4: Given the comment form for lines 18–22, when the reviewer clicks "Suggest change", then
  the inserted `suggestion` block contains lines 18 to 22 in order, with their indentation kept.
- [ ] AC5: Given a code comment on lines 18–22 whose body has one `suggestion` block of three lines,
  when it is shown in the Files changed or Conversation tab, then the "Suggested change" diff shows
  lines 18 to 22 as five removed (red) lines in order, followed by the three block lines as added
  (green) lines.
- [ ] AC6: Given a code comment on lines 18–22 with an empty `suggestion` block, when it is shown,
  then lines 18 to 22 show as removed and no line shows as added.
- [ ] AC7: Given a code comment on lines 18–22, when a push changes the text of any one line from 18
  to 22 (the first, one in the middle, or the last), then the comment is marked Outdated.
- [ ] AC8: Given a code comment on lines 18–22, when a push changes only lines after line 22, then
  the comment is not marked Outdated.
- [ ] AC9: Given a code comment on a range that ends on the file's last line, when a push deletes
  that last line, or deletes the file, then the comment is marked Outdated.
- [ ] AC10: Given a reviewer has selected a line, when they shift-click a line that would make the
  range cross a hunk header or include expanded context lines, then no range is selected and they
  see "A comment can only cover lines on one side of a single hunk."
- [ ] AC11: Given a reviewer has selected an old-side (deleted) line, when they shift-click a
  new-side line (or the other way round), then no range is selected and they see the same message
  as AC10.
- [ ] AC12: Given a direct POST to the code-comment endpoint whose start line is after its end line,
  is on the old side, or is not in the same hunk as the end line, when it is submitted, then the
  response is 400 with the AC10 message and no comment is saved.
- [ ] AC13: Given single-line code comments created before this change, when they are shown and when
  a push changes their line, then they render and are marked Outdated exactly as before.

### Out of Scope

- Ranges across files.
- Ranges on the old (deleted) side of the diff.
- Applying a range suggestion. S3 #156 (apply) and S6 #159 (apply several) read the stored start
  line to replace exactly the range.
- A start-line field in the REST API: S7 #160.
- Selecting by dragging; only click and shift-click on line numbers.
- Ranges that include expanded context lines (lines outside a hunk); they are refused (AC10).
- Following a range when lines are inserted above it. The comment goes Outdated, as single-line
  comments do today.

### Open Questions

- None. The maximum range length is resolved as the size of one hunk, with no separate cap; AC10
  and AC12 enforce it.

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Store a range comment's start line as `StartLine` in the comment's existing
`CommentMetaData` JSON field (absent = single-line, as today), and keep `Line` as the range end.

**Alternatives Considered:**

- _A new `start_line` column on `comment`._ Typed and queryable, but needs a migration on Gitea's
  largest table, and the repo convention (`models/issues/comment.go`, `CommentMetaData`) is that
  non-index data goes in the metadata field. Nothing needs to filter by start line in SQL.
- _One linked comment per line._ Breaks the "one comment, one suggestion" model from S4 #157.

**Rationale:** `Line` keeps its meaning, so thread placement (`FetchCodeComments` keys on `Line`),
replies, the API and every existing row are untouched; only code that cares about ranges reads the
start line. Old rows have no `StartLine`, so AC13 holds without a migration.

**Consequences:** No migration. The start line can't be filtered in SQL. S3, S6 and S7 read it
through a helper (`Comment.RangeStartLine()`).

### Decision 2

**Decision:** Mark a range comment Outdated by comparing the text of lines start..end at the new
head with the range's lines stored in the comment's diff snippet. Single-line comments keep today's
blame check.

**Alternatives Considered:**

- _Blame every line in the range._ A comment stores one `CommitSHA`, so there is nothing to compare
  each line's blame against without a new per-line store.
- _Store the head SHA and diff the old head against the new head, mapping hunks onto the range._
  Handles lines moving, but needs a git diff per comment per push and much more code.

**Rationale:** It is the same rule S3 #156 AC3 uses for apply ("the line's text at head differs"),
so a range is Outdated exactly when its suggestion could no longer be applied.

**Consequences:** One blob read per open range comment per push. A line rewritten to identical text
is not flagged.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

Touches the code-comment model helpers, the code-comment POST path (form, router, the patch snippet
and invalidation in `services/pull/review.go`), the diff page's JS and templates (range selection,
header, "Suggest change" prefill) and S1's suggestion renderer: about ten files plus unit,
integration and E2E tests, with no new endpoint, table or migration.
```

```text
package issues

import (
	"strings"

	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"
)

// SuggestionOriginalLine returns the commented line as the reviewer saw it: the last line of the
// stored patch, since CutDiffAroundLine stops right after the commented line.
// Old-side comments return None until #151 decides whether they may carry suggestions.
func (c *Comment) SuggestionOriginalLine() optional.Option[string] {
	if c.Type != CommentTypeCode || c.Line <= 0 {
		return optional.None[string]()
	}
	patch := strings.TrimRight(c.Patch, "\n")
	last := patch[strings.LastIndexByte(patch, '\n')+1:]
	if last == "" || (last[0] != '+' && last[0] != ' ') {
		return optional.None[string]() // "-" is the other side; "@", "d", "\\" mean no code line
	}
	return optional.Some(last[1:])
}

package issues_test

import (
	"testing"

	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

func TestCommentSuggestionOriginalLine(t *testing.T) {
	const header = "diff --git a/main.go b/main.go\n--- a/main.go\n+++ b/main.go\n@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@\n"
	cases := []struct {
		name     string
		typ      issues_model.CommentType
		line     int64
		patch    string
		expected optional.Option[string]
	}{
		{"added line keeps indentation", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 3, header + " package main\n-\treturn nil\n+\treturn err", optional.Some("\treturn err")},
		{"context line", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header + " package main\n func main() {}", optional.Some("func main() {}")},
		{"trailing newline in patch", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header + " package main\n+x := 1\n", optional.Some("x := 1")},
		{"blank context line", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header + " package main\n ", optional.Some("")},
		{"CRLF kept", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 1, header + "+foo\r", optional.Some("foo\r")},
		{"old side is not supported", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, -2, header + " package main\n-\treturn nil", optional.None[string]()},
		{"removed line on new side is inconsistent", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header + " package main\n-gone", optional.None[string]()},
		{"empty patch", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, "", optional.None[string]()},
		{"header only", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header, optional.None[string]()},
		{"not a code comment", issues_model.CommentTypeComment, 2, header + "+x", optional.None[string]()},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			comment := &issues_model.Comment{Type: c.typ, Line: c.line, Patch: c.patch}
			assert.Equal(t, c.expected, comment.SuggestionOriginalLine())
		})
	}
}
```

```text
// ErrSubmitReviewOnClosedPR represents an error when a user tries to submit an approve or reject review associated to a closed or merged PR.
var ErrSubmitReviewOnClosedPR = errors.New("can't submit review for a closed or merged PR")

// LineBlame returns the latest commit at the given line
func lineBlame(ctx context.Context, repo *repo_model.Repository, gitRepo *git.Repository, branch, file string, line uint) (*git.Commit, error) {
	sha, err := gitrepo.LineBlame(ctx, repo, branch, file, line)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if len(sha) < 40 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid result of blame: %s", sha)
	}

	objectFormat := git.ObjectFormatFromName(repo.ObjectFormatName)
	return gitRepo.GetCommit(sha[:objectFormat.FullLength()])
}

// checkInvalidation checks if the line of code comment got changed by another commit.
// If the line got changed the comment is going to be invalidated.
func checkInvalidation(ctx context.Context, c *issues_model.Comment, repo *repo_model.Repository, gitRepo *git.Repository, branch string) error {
	// FIXME differentiate between previous and proposed line
	commit, err := lineBlame(ctx, repo, gitRepo, branch, c.TreePath, uint(c.UnsignedLine()))
	if isErrBlameNotFoundOrNotEnoughLines(err) {
		c.Invalidated = true
		return issues_model.UpdateCommentInvalidate(ctx, c)
	}
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if c.CommitSHA != "" && c.CommitSHA != commit.ID.String() {
		c.Invalidated = true
		return issues_model.UpdateCommentInvalidate(ctx, c)
	}
	return nil
}

// InvalidateCodeComments will lookup the prs for code comments which got invalidated by change
func InvalidateCodeComments(ctx context.Context, prs issues_model.PullRequestList, doer *user_model.User, repo *repo_model.Repository, gitRepo *git.Repository, branch string) error {
	if len(prs) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	issueIDs := prs.GetIssueIDs()

	codeComments, err := db.Find[issues_model.Comment](ctx, issues_model.FindCommentsOptions{
		ListOptions: db.ListOptionsAll,
		Type:        issues_model.CommentTypeCode,
		Invalidated: optional.Some(false),
		IssueIDs:    issueIDs,
	})
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("find code comments: %v", err)
	}
	for _, comment := range codeComments {
		if err := checkInvalidation(ctx, comment, repo, gitRepo, branch); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// CreateCodeComment creates a comment on the code line
func CreateCodeComment(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, gitRepo *git.Repository, issue *issues_model.Issue, line int64, content, treePath string, pendingReview bool, replyReviewID int64, latestCommitID string, attachments []string) (*issues_model.Comment, error) {
	var (
		existsReview bool
		err          error
	)

	// CreateCodeComment() is used for:
	// - Single comments
	// - Comments that are part of a review
	// - Comments that reply to an existing review

	if !pendingReview && replyReviewID != 0 {
		// It's not part of a review; maybe a reply to a review comment or a single comment.
		// Check if there are reviews for that line already; if there are, this is a reply
		if existsReview, err = issues_model.ReviewExists(ctx, issue, treePath, line); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}

	// Comments that are replies don't require a review header to show up in the issue view
	if !pendingReview && existsReview {
		if err = issue.LoadRepo(ctx); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}

		comment, err := createCodeComment(ctx,
			doer,
			issue.Repo,
			issue,
			content,
			treePath,
			line,
			replyReviewID,
			attachments,
		)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}

		mentions, err := issues_model.FindAndUpdateIssueMentions(ctx, issue, doer, comment.Content)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}

		notify_service.CreateIssueComment(ctx, doer, issue.Repo, issue, comment, mentions)

		return comment, nil
	}

	review, err := issues_model.GetCurrentReview(ctx, doer, issue)
	if err != nil {
		if !issues_model.IsErrReviewNotExist(err) {
			return nil, err
		}

		if review, err = issues_model.CreateReview(ctx, issues_model.CreateReviewOptions{
			Type:     issues_model.ReviewTypePending,
			Reviewer: doer,
			Issue:    issue,
			Official: false,
			CommitID: latestCommitID,
		}); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}

	comment, err := createCodeComment(ctx,
		doer,
		issue.Repo,
		issue,
		content,
		treePath,
		line,
		review.ID,
		attachments,
	)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	if !pendingReview && !existsReview {
		// Submit the review we've just created so the comment shows up in the issue view
		if _, _, err = SubmitReview(ctx, doer, gitRepo, issue, issues_model.ReviewTypeComment, "", latestCommitID, nil); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}

	// NOTICE: if it's a pending review the notifications will not be fired until user submit review.

	return comment, nil
}

// createCodeComment creates a plain code comment at the specified line / path
func createCodeComment(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, repo *repo_model.Repository, issue *issues_model.Issue, content, treePath string, line, reviewID int64, attachments []string) (*issues_model.Comment, error) {
	var commitID, patch string
	if err := issue.LoadPullRequest(ctx); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("LoadPullRequest: %w", err)
	}
	pr := issue.PullRequest
	if err := pr.LoadBaseRepo(ctx); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("LoadBaseRepo: %w", err)
	}
	gitRepo, closer, err := gitrepo.RepositoryFromContextOrOpen(ctx, pr.BaseRepo)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("RepositoryFromContextOrOpen: %w", err)
	}
	defer closer.Close()

	invalidated := false
	head := pr.GetGitHeadRefName()
	if line > 0 {
		if reviewID != 0 {
			first, err := issues_model.FindComments(ctx, &issues_model.FindCommentsOptions{
				ReviewID: reviewID,
				Line:     line,
				TreePath: treePath,
				Type:     issues_model.CommentTypeCode,
				ListOptions: db.ListOptions{
					PageSize: 1,
					Page:     1,
				},
			})
			if err == nil && len(first) > 0 {
				commitID = first[0].CommitSHA
				invalidated = first[0].Invalidated
				patch = first[0].Patch
			} else if err != nil && !issues_model.IsErrCommentNotExist(err) {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("Find first comment for %d line %d path %s. Error: %w", reviewID, line, treePath, err)
			} else {
				review, err := issues_model.GetReviewByID(ctx, reviewID)
				if err == nil && len(review.CommitID) > 0 {
					head = review.CommitID
				} else if err != nil && !issues_model.IsErrReviewNotExist(err) {
					return nil, fmt.Errorf("GetReviewByID %d. Error: %w", reviewID, err)
				}
			}
		}

		if len(commitID) == 0 {
			// FIXME validate treePath
			// Get latest commit referencing the commented line
			// No need for get commit for base branch changes
			commit, err := lineBlame(ctx, pr.BaseRepo, gitRepo, head, treePath, uint(line))
			if err == nil {
				commitID = commit.ID.String()
			} else if !isErrBlameNotFoundOrNotEnoughLines(err) {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("LineBlame[%s, %s, %s, %d]: %w", pr.GetGitHeadRefName(), gitRepo.Path, treePath, line, err)
			}
		}
	}

	// Only fetch diff if comment is review comment
	if len(patch) == 0 && reviewID != 0 {
		headCommitID, err := gitRepo.GetRefCommitID(pr.GetGitHeadRefName())
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("GetRefCommitID[%s]: %w", pr.GetGitHeadRefName(), err)
		}
		if len(commitID) == 0 {
			commitID = headCommitID
		}

		patch, err = git.GetFileDiffCutAroundLine(
			gitRepo, pr.MergeBase, headCommitID, treePath,
			int64((&issues_model.Comment{Line: line}).UnsignedLine()), line < 0, setting.UI.CodeCommentLines,
		)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}

		// If patch is still empty (unchanged line), generate code context
		if patch == "" && commitID != "" {
			patch, err = gitdiff.GeneratePatchForUnchangedLine(gitRepo, commitID, treePath, line, setting.UI.CodeCommentLines)
			if err != nil {
				// Log the error but don't fail comment creation
				log.Debug("Unable to generate patch for unchanged line (file=%s, line=%d, commit=%s): %v", treePath, line, commitID, err)
			}
		}
	}
	return issues_model.CreateComment(ctx, &issues_model.CreateCommentOptions{
		Type:        issues_model.CommentTypeCode,
		Doer:        doer,
		Repo:        repo,
		Issue:       issue,
		Content:     content,
		LineNum:     line,
		TreePath:    treePath,
		CommitSHA:   commitID,
		ReviewID:    reviewID,
		Patch:       patch,
		Invalidated: invalidated,
		Attachments: attachments,
	})
}
```

```text
func GetRawDiff(repo *Repository, commitID string, diffType RawDiffType, writer io.Writer) (retErr error) {
	cmd, err := getRepoRawDiffForFileCmd(repo.Ctx, repo, "", commitID, diffType, "")
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("getRepoRawDiffForFileCmd: %w", err)
	}
	return cmd.WithStdoutCopy(writer).RunWithStderr(repo.Ctx)
}

// GetFileDiffCutAroundLine cuts the old or new part of the diff of a file around a specific line number
func GetFileDiffCutAroundLine(
	repo *Repository, startCommit, endCommit, treePath string,
	line int64, old bool, numbersOfLine int,
) (ret string, retErr error) {
	cmd, err := getRepoRawDiffForFileCmd(repo.Ctx, repo, startCommit, endCommit, RawDiffNormal, treePath)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("getRepoRawDiffForFileCmd: %w", err)
	}
	stdoutReader, stdoutClose := cmd.MakeStdoutPipe()
	defer stdoutClose()
	cmd.WithPipelineFunc(func(ctx gitcmd.Context) error {
		ret, err = CutDiffAroundLine(stdoutReader, line, old, numbersOfLine)
		return err
	})
	return ret, cmd.RunWithStderr(repo.Ctx)
}

// CutDiffAroundLine cuts a diff of a file in way that only the given line + numberOfLine above it will be shown
// it also recalculates hunks and adds the appropriate headers to the new diff.
// Warning: Only one-file diffs are allowed.
func CutDiffAroundLine(originalDiff io.Reader, line int64, old bool, numbersOfLine int) (string, error) {
	if line == 0 || numbersOfLine == 0 {
		// no line or num of lines => no diff
		return "", nil
	}

	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(originalDiff)
	hunk := make([]string, 0)

	// begin is the start of the hunk containing searched line
	// end is the end of the hunk ...
	// currentLine is the line number on the side of the searched line (differentiated by old)
	// otherLine is the line number on the opposite side of the searched line (differentiated by old)
	var begin, end, currentLine, otherLine int64
	var headerLines int

	inHunk := false

	for scanner.Scan() {
		lof := scanner.Text()
		// Add header to enable parsing

		if isHeader(lof, inHunk) {
			if strings.HasPrefix(lof, cmdDiffHead) {
				inHunk = false
			}
			hunk = append(hunk, lof)
			headerLines++
		}
		if currentLine > line {
			break
		}
		// Detect "hunk" with contains commented lof
		if strings.HasPrefix(lof, "@@") {
			inHunk = true
			// Already got our hunk. End of hunk detected!
			if len(hunk) > headerLines {
				break
			}
			// A map with named groups of our regex to recognize them later more easily
			submatches := hunkRegex.FindStringSubmatch(lof)
			groups := make(map[string]string)
			for i, name := range hunkRegex.SubexpNames() {
				if i != 0 && name != "" {
					groups[name] = submatches[i]
				}
			}
			if old {
				begin, _ = strconv.ParseInt(groups["beginOld"], 10, 64)
				end, _ = strconv.ParseInt(groups["endOld"], 10, 64)
				// init otherLine with begin of opposite side
				otherLine, _ = strconv.ParseInt(groups["beginNew"], 10, 64)
			} else {
				begin, _ = strconv.ParseInt(groups["beginNew"], 10, 64)
				if groups["endNew"] != "" {
					end, _ = strconv.ParseInt(groups["endNew"], 10, 64)
				} else {
					end = 0
				}
				// init otherLine with begin of opposite side
				otherLine, _ = strconv.ParseInt(groups["beginOld"], 10, 64)
			}
			end += begin // end is for real only the number of lines in hunk
			// lof is between begin and end
			if begin <= line && end >= line {
				hunk = append(hunk, lof)
				currentLine = begin
				continue
			}
		} else if len(hunk) > headerLines {
			hunk = append(hunk, lof)
			// Count lines in context
			switch lof[0] {
			case '+':
				if !old {
					currentLine++
				} else {
					otherLine++
				}
			case '-':
				if old {
					currentLine++
				} else {
					otherLine++
				}
			case '\\':
				// FIXME: handle `\ No newline at end of file`
			default:
				currentLine++
				otherLine++
			}
		}
	}
	if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("CutDiffAroundLine: scan: %w", err)
	}

	// No hunk found
	if currentLine == 0 {
		return "", nil
	}
	// headerLines + hunkLine (1) = totalNonCodeLines
	if len(hunk)-headerLines-1 <= numbersOfLine {
		// No need to cut the hunk => return existing hunk
		return strings.Join(hunk, "\n"), nil
	}
	var oldBegin, oldNumOfLines, newBegin, newNumOfLines int64
	if old {
		oldBegin = currentLine
		newBegin = otherLine
	} else {
		oldBegin = otherLine
		newBegin = currentLine
	}
	// headers + hunk header
	newHunk := make([]string, headerLines)
	// transfer existing headers
	copy(newHunk, hunk[:headerLines])
	// transfer last n lines
	newHunk = append(newHunk, hunk[len(hunk)-numbersOfLine-1:]...)
	// calculate newBegin, ... by counting lines
	for i := len(hunk) - 1; i >= len(hunk)-numbersOfLine; i-- {
		switch hunk[i][0] {
		case '+':
			newBegin--
			newNumOfLines++
		case '-':
			oldBegin--
			oldNumOfLines++
		default:
			oldBegin--
			newBegin--
			newNumOfLines++
			oldNumOfLines++
		}
```

```text
func (c *Commit) HasFile(filename string) (bool, error) {
	_, err := c.GetBlobByPath(filename)
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}

}

// GetFileContent reads a file content as a string or returns false if this was not possible
func (c *Commit) GetFileContent(filename string, limit int) (string, error) {
	entry, err := c.GetTreeEntryByPath(filename)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}

	r, err := entry.Blob().DataAsync()
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	defer r.Close()

	if limit > 0 {
		bs := make([]byte, limit)
		n, err := util.ReadAtMost(r, bs)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		return string(bs[:n]), nil
	}

	bytes, err := io.ReadAll(r)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return string(bytes), nil
}
```

```go
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issues

import (
	"strings"

	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"
)

// SuggestionOriginalLine returns the commented line as the reviewer saw it: the last line of the
// stored patch, since CutDiffAroundLine stops right after the commented line.
// For a multi-line comment it returns every line of the range, joined by "\n".
// Old-side comments return None until #151 decides whether they may carry suggestions.
func (c *Comment) SuggestionOriginalLine() optional.Option[string] {
	if c.Type != CommentTypeCode || c.Line <= 0 {
		return optional.None[string]()
	}
	if c.RangeStartLine() > 0 {
		lines, ok := c.RangeOriginalLines()
		if !ok {
			return optional.None[string]()
		}
		return optional.Some(strings.Join(lines, "\n"))
	}
	patch := strings.TrimRight(c.Patch, "\n")
	last := patch[strings.LastIndexByte(patch, '\n')+1:]
	if last == "" || (last[0] != '+' && last[0] != ' ') {
		return optional.None[string]() // "-" is the other side; "@", "d", "\\" mean no code line
	}
	return optional.Some(last[1:])
}

// RangeOriginalLines returns lines RangeStartLine..Line of a multi-line code comment as the
// reviewer saw them, false if the stored patch doesn't hold all of them.
func (c *Comment) RangeOriginalLines() ([]string, bool) {
	start := c.RangeStartLine()
	if start <= 0 || c.Line < start {
		return nil, false
	}
	return PatchLastNewLines(c.Patch, int(c.Line-start+1))
}

// PatchLastNewLines returns the last n new-side lines of a one-hunk patch, which end at the
// commented line, skipping removed lines. False if the hunk has fewer than n.
func PatchLastNewLines(patch string, n int) ([]string, bool) {
	rows := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(patch, "\n"), "\n")
	lines := make([]string, n)
	for i := len(rows) - 1; i >= 0 && n > 0; i-- {
		switch {
		case rows[i] == "" || rows[i][0] == '@':
			return nil, false // reached the hunk header
		case rows[i][0] == '+' || rows[i][0] == ' ':
			n--
			lines[n] = rows[i][1:]
		}
	}
	return lines, n == 0
}
```

```bash
func TestCommentSuggestionOriginalLineRange(t *testing.T) {
	const header = "diff --git a/main.go b/main.go\n--- a/main.go\n+++ b/main.go\n@@ -16,6 +16,7 @@\n"
	// new-side lines 16..22; the removed line between 19 and 20 is not part of the range
	const patch = header + " l16\n l17\n l18\n+\tl19\n-old\n l20\n+l21\n l22"
	cases := []struct {
		name     string
		start    int64
		line     int64
		patch    string
		expected optional.Option[string]
	}{
		{"lines 18-22 in order, removed line skipped", 18, 22, patch, optional.Some("l18\n\tl19\nl20\nl21\nl22")},
		{"range reaching the hunk start", 16, 22, patch, optional.Some("l16\nl17\nl18\n\tl19\nl20\nl21\nl22")},
		{"range longer than the stored hunk", 15, 22, patch, optional.None[string]()},
		{"no newline at end of file marker", 21, 22, patch + "\n\\ No newline at end of file", optional.Some("l21\nl22")},
		{"empty patch", 18, 22, "", optional.None[string]()},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			comment := &issues_model.Comment{
				Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode, Line: c.line, Patch: c.patch,
				CommentMetaData: &issues_model.CommentMetaData{StartLine: c.start},
			}
			assert.Equal(t, c.expected, comment.SuggestionOriginalLine())
		})
	}
}
```

```bash
func checkRangeInvalidation(ctx context.Context, c *issues_model.Comment, gitRepo *git.Repository, branch string) error {
	original, ok := c.RangeOriginalLines()
	if !ok {
		return nil // no snippet to compare with, as for a comment created without a review
	}
	commit, err := gitRepo.GetBranchCommit(branch)
	if err != nil {

	}
	content, err := commit.GetFileContent(c.TreePath, 0)
	if err != nil && !git.IsErrNotExist(err) {
		return err
	}
	if rangeChanged(original, content, c.RangeStartLine()) {
		c.Invalidated = true
		return issues_model.UpdateCommentInvalidate(ctx, c)
	}
	return nil
}

// rangeChanged reports whether content no longer has the original lines starting at line start.
func rangeChanged(original []string, content string, start int64) bool {
	lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(content, "\\n"), "\\n")
	if content == "" {
		lines = nil
	}
	end := int(start) - 1 + len(original)
	return end > len(lines) || !slices.Equal(lines[start-1:end], original)
}
```

```text
// CreateCodeComment will create a code comment including an pending review if required
func CreateCodeComment(ctx *context.Context) {
	form := web.GetForm(ctx).(*forms.CodeCommentForm)
	issue := GetActionIssue(ctx)
	if ctx.Written() {
		return
	}
	if !issue.IsPull {
		return
	}

	if ctx.HasError() {
		ctx.Flash.Error(ctx.GetErrMsg())
		ctx.Redirect(fmt.Sprintf("%s/pulls/%d/files", ctx.Repo.RepoLink, issue.Index))
		return
	}

	signedLine := form.Line
	if form.Side == "previous" {
		signedLine *= -1
	}

	var attachments []string
	if setting.Attachment.Enabled {
		attachments = form.Files
	}

	comment, err := pull_service.CreateCodeComment(ctx,
		ctx.Doer,
		ctx.Repo.GitRepo,
		issue,
		signedLine,
		form.Content,
		form.TreePath,
		!form.SingleReview,
		form.Reply,
		form.LatestCommitID,
		attachments,
	)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("CreateCodeComment", err)
		return
	}

	if comment == nil {
		log.Trace("Comment not created: %-v #%d[%d]", ctx.Repo.Repository, issue.Index, issue.ID)
		ctx.Redirect(fmt.Sprintf("%s/pulls/%d/files", ctx.Repo.RepoLink, issue.Index))
		return
	}

	log.Trace("Comment created: %-v #%d[%d] Comment[%d]", ctx.Repo.Repository, issue.Index, issue.ID, comment.ID)

	renderConversation(ctx, comment, form.Origin)
}
```

```text
// RenderNewCodeCommentForm will render the form for creating a new review comment
func RenderNewCodeCommentForm(ctx *context.Context) {
	issue := GetActionIssue(ctx)
	if ctx.Written() {
		return
	}
	if !issue.IsPull {
		return
	}
	currentReview, err := issues_model.GetCurrentReview(ctx, ctx.Doer, issue)
	if err != nil && !issues_model.IsErrReviewNotExist(err) {
		ctx.ServerError("GetCurrentReview", err)
		return
	}
	ctx.Data["PageIsPullFiles"] = true
	ctx.Data["Issue"] = issue
	ctx.Data["CurrentReview"] = currentReview
	pullHeadCommitID, err := ctx.Repo.GitRepo.GetRefCommitID(issue.PullRequest.GetGitHeadRefName())
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("GetRefCommitID", err)
		return
	}
	ctx.Data["AfterCommitID"] = pullHeadCommitID
	ctx.Data["IsAttachmentEnabled"] = setting.Attachment.Enabled
	upload.AddUploadContext(ctx, "comment")
	ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplNewComment)
}
```

```bash
package pull

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"

func TestRangeChanged(t *testing.T) {
	original := []string{"l3", "l4", "l5"} // a comment on lines 3-5
	cases := []struct {
		name    string
		content string
		start   int64
		changed bool
	}{
		{"unchanged", "l1\nl2\nl3\nl4\nl5\nl6\n", 3, false},
		{"first line changed", "l1\nl2\nX\nl4\nl5\nl6\n", 3, true},
		{"middle line changed", "l1\nl2\nl3\nX\nl5\nl6\n", 3, true},
		{"last line changed", "l1\nl2\nl3\nl4\nX\nl6\n", 3, true},
		{"only a line after the range changed", "l1\nl2\nl3\nl4\nl5\nX\n", 3, false},
		{"range ends on the last line, no final newline", "l1\nl2\nl3\nl4\nl5", 3, false},
		{"last line deleted", "l1\nl2\nl3\nl4\n", 3, true},
		{"file deleted", "", 3, true},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			assert.Equal(t, c.changed, rangeChanged(original, c.content, c.start))
		})
	}
}
EOF
```

====
  const afterEnd = suggestionInsertPos(value, end);
  if (afterEnd !== end) return [afterEnd, afterEnd];
  const afterStart = suggestionInsertPos(value, start);
  if (afterStart !== start) return [afterStart, afterStart];
  return [start, end];
}

/** show the "Suggest change" button of a new code comment's editor, inserting a block with the text of `codeLine` */
export function initSuggestChangeButton(editor: ComboMarkdownEditor, codeLine: HTMLElement) {
  const button = editor.container.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.markdown-button-suggest-change');
  if (!button) return;
  showElem(button.closest('.markdown-toolbar-group')!);
  button.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    const textarea = editor.textarea;
    const [start, end] = suggestionInsertRange(textarea.value, textarea.selectionStart, textarea.selectionEnd);
    textarea.setSelectionRange(start, end);
    // textContent drops the highlighting spans and keeps leading whitespace; the diff cell also holds the line's own newline
    const line = codeLine.textContent.replace(/[\r\n]+$/, '');
    const {text, cursor} = buildSuggestionInsert(textarea.value.slice(0, start), line);
    replaceTextareaSelection(textarea, text);
    textarea.setSelectionRange(start + cursor, start + cursor);
  });
}
====
import {queryElems} from '../utils/dom.ts';

function makeLine(kind: 'removed' | 'added', text: string): HTMLElement {
  const row = document.createElement('div');
  row.className = `markup-suggestion-line ${kind}`;
  const marker = document.createElement('span');
  marker.className = 'markup-suggestion-marker';
  marker.textContent = kind === 'removed' ? '-' : '+';
  const code = document.createElement('code');
  code.textContent = text; // never innerHTML: suggestion text is user input
  row.append(marker, code);
  return row;
}

// Replaces ```suggestion blocks in a PR code comment with a diff against the commented line.
// The server only sets data-suggestion-original on new-side code comments, so plain comments keep a code block.
export function initMarkupCodeSuggestion(elMarkup: HTMLElement): void {
  const original = elMarkup.getAttribute('data-suggestion-original');
  if (original === null) return;
  const label = elMarkup.getAttribute('data-suggestion-label')!;
  queryElems(elMarkup, 'code.language-suggestion', (elCode) => {
    const block = elCode.closest('.code-block-container') ?? elCode.closest('pre')!;
    // an empty fence renders "" (delete the line); otherwise every line ends with "\n", so one blank line is "\n"
    const raw = elCode.textContent;
    const diff = document.createElement('div');
    diff.className = 'markup-suggestion';
    const header = document.createElement('div');
    header.className = 'markup-suggestion-header';
    header.textContent = label;
    diff.append(header, makeLine('removed', original));
    if (raw !== '') {
      for (const line of raw.replace(/\r?\n$/, '').split(/\r?\n/)) diff.append(makeLine('added', line));
    }
    block.replaceWith(diff);
  });
}

```typescript
import {addDelegatedEventListener} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import {showErrorToast} from '../modules/toast.ts';

let anchor: {tr: HTMLElement, side: string} | null = null;
let selected: HTMLElement[] = [];

function newLineNum(tr: Element): number {
  return Number(tr.querySelector('td.lines-num-new')?.getAttribute('data-line-num') || 0);
}

/** the new-side rows from `a` to `b` in either order, or null when they aren't in one hunk */
export function collectRangeRows(a: HTMLElement, b: HTMLElement): HTMLElement[] | null {
  const [first, last] = a.compareDocumentPosition(b) & Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_PRECEDING ? [b, a] : [a, b];
  const rows: HTMLElement[] = [];
  for (let tr: Element | null = first; tr; tr = tr.nextElementSibling) {
    // a hunk header, or expanded context which belongs to no hunk
    if (tr.classList.contains('tag-code') || tr.classList.contains('line-expanded')) return null;
    if (newLineNum(tr)) rows.push(tr as HTMLElement); // skips removed lines and comment rows
    if (tr === last) return rows;
  }
  return null; // `last` isn't after `first` in this file
}

function setSelected(rows: HTMLElement[]) {
  for (const tr of selected) tr.classList.remove('range-selected');
  selected = rows;
  for (const tr of selected) tr.classList.add('range-selected');
}

/** the selected range, when `tr` is its last row and it has more than one line */
export function getSelectedRange(tr: Element): {rows: HTMLElement[], start: number, end: number} | null {
  if (selected.length < 2 || selected.at(-1) !== tr) return null;
  return {rows: selected, start: newLineNum(selected[0]), end: newLineNum(tr)};
}

// click a line number to start a range, shift-click another to end it
export function initDiffRangeSelect() {
  addDelegatedEventListener(document, 'click', '.code-diff td.lines-num[data-line-num]:not([data-line-num=""])', (td, e: MouseEvent) => {
    const tr = td.closest('tr')!;
    const side = td.classList.contains('lines-num-new') ? 'right' : 'left';
    if (!e.shiftKey || !anchor) {
      anchor = {tr, side};
      setSelected(side === 'right' ? [tr] : []);
      return;
    }
    window.getSelection()?.removeAllRanges();
    const rows = anchor.side === 'right' && side === 'right' ? collectRangeRows(anchor.tr, tr) : null;
    if (!rows) {
      anchor = null;
      setSelected([]);
      showErrorToast(td.closest('[data-range-invalid]')!.getAttribute('data-range-invalid')!);
      return;
    }
    setSelected(rows);
  });
}
```

import {initMarkupCodeSuggestion} from './suggestion.ts';

function makeMarkup(attrs: Record<string, string>, body: string): HTMLElement {
  const el = document.createElement('div');
  el.className = 'render-content markup';
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(attrs)) el.setAttribute(k, v);
  el.innerHTML = body;
  return el;
}

function codeBlock(text: string, lang = 'suggestion'): string {
  return `<div class="code-block-container code-overflow-scroll"><pre class="code-block"><code class="chroma language-${lang} display">${text}</code></pre></div>`;
}

const attrs = {'data-suggestion-original': '\treturn err', 'data-suggestion-label': 'Suggested change'};

function rows(el: Element) {
  return Array.from(el.querySelectorAll('.markup-suggestion-line'), (row) => ({
    kind: row.classList.contains('removed') ? 'removed' : 'added',
    text: row.querySelector('code')!.textContent,
  }));
}

test('renders the original line as removed and each block line as added', () => {
  const el = makeMarkup(attrs, `<p>try this</p>${codeBlock('\treturn fmt.Errorf("x: %w", err)\n\treturn nil\n')}`);
  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);
  expect(el.querySelector('.code-block-container')).toBeNull();
  const diff = el.querySelector('.markup-suggestion')!;
  expect(diff.querySelector('.markup-suggestion-header')!.textContent).toEqual('Suggested change');
  expect(rows(diff)).toEqual([
    {kind: 'removed', text: '\treturn err'},
    {kind: 'added', text: '\treturn fmt.Errorf("x: %w", err)'},
    {kind: 'added', text: '\treturn nil'},
  ]);
  expect(el.querySelector('p')!.textContent).toEqual('try this');
});

test('empty block only removes the line', () => {
  const el = makeMarkup(attrs, codeBlock(''));
  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);

````bash
import {collectRangeRows} from './repo-diff-range.ts';

// a unified diff: new-side lines carry data-line-num on td.lines-num-new, removed lines have it empty
function row(cls: string, newLine = '') {
  return `<tr class="${cls}"><td class="lines-num lines-num-new" data-line-num="${newLine}"></td></tr>`;
}

function rowsOf(html: string) {
  document.body.innerHTML = `<table><tbody>${html}</tbody></table>`;
  return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('tr'));
}

const lineNums = (rows: HTMLElement[] | null) => rows?.map((tr) => tr.querySelector('td')!.getAttribute('data-line-num'));

test('collectRangeRows', () => {
  const trs = rowsOf(row('same-code', '18') + row('del-code') + row('add-code', '19') + row('add-comment') + row('same-code', '20'));

  // #158 AC3: one line

});
````

````text
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"fmt"
	"maps"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
	"gitea.dev/modules/git"
	repo_service "gitea.dev/services/repository"
	files_service "gitea.dev/services/repository/files"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestPullReviewSuggestionAttribute(t *testing.T) {
	onGiteaRun(t, func(t *testing.T, u *url.URL) {
		user2 := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
		repo, err := repo_service.CreateRepositoryDirectly(t.Context(), user2, user2, repo_service.CreateRepoOptions{
			Name:             "test_suggestion",
			Readme:           "Default",
			AutoInit:         true,
			ObjectFormatName: git.Sha1ObjectFormat.Name(),
			DefaultBranch:    "master",
		}, true)
		require.NoError(t, err)

		_, err = files_service.ChangeRepoFiles(t.Context(), repo, user2, &files_service.ChangeRepoFilesOptions{
			NewBranch: "suggestion-branch",
			Files: []*files_service.ChangeRepoFile{{
				Operation:     "update",
				TreePath:      "README.md",
				ContentReader: strings.NewReader("# Title\n\treturn err\n"),
			}},
		})
		require.NoError(t, err)

		session := loginUser(t, "user2")
		testPullCreate(t, session, "user2", "test_suggestion", false, "master", "suggestion-branch", "Suggestion PR")
		pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{BaseRepoID: repo.ID, HeadBranch: "suggestion-branch"})
		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))
		commentURL := fmt.Sprintf("/user2/test_suggestion/pulls/%d/files/reviews/comments", pr.Issue.Index)

		postComment := func(t *testing.T, origin, side, line string, extra map[string]string) *HTMLDoc {
			values := map[string]string{
				"origin":        origin,
				"content":       "```suggestion\n\treturn nil\n```",
				"side":          side,
				"line":          line,
				"path":          "README.md",
				"single_review": "true",
			}
			maps.Copy(values, extra)
			req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", commentURL, values)
			return NewHTMLParser(t, session.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK).Body)
		}

		for _, origin := range []string{"diff", "timeline"} { // repo/diff/comments.tmpl and view_content/conversation.tmpl
			t.Run(origin, func(t *testing.T) {
				markup := postComment(t, origin, "proposed", "2", nil).Find(".render-content.markup[data-suggestion-original]").First()
				require.Equal(t, 1, markup.Length())
				assert.Equal(t, "\treturn err", markup.AttrOr("data-suggestion-original", ""))
				assert.Equal(t, "Suggested change", markup.AttrOr("data-suggestion-label", ""))
			})
		}

		t.Run("reply in the thread gets the attribute", func(t *testing.T) {
			first := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{IssueID: pr.IssueID, Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode, Line: 2, TreePath: "README.md"}, unittest.OrderBy("id ASC"))
			doc := postComment(t, "diff", "proposed", "2", map[string]string{"reply": strconv.FormatInt(first.ReviewID, 10)})
			markups := doc.Find(".render-content.markup[data-suggestion-original]")
			assert.Equal(t, doc.Find(".render-content.markup").Length(), markups.Length()) // every comment in the thread, reply included
			assert.Equal(t, "\treturn err", markups.Last().AttrOr("data-suggestion-original", ""))
		})

		t.Run("old side gets no attribute", func(t *testing.T) {
			doc := postComment(t, "diff", "previous", "1", nil)
			require.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(".render-content.markup code.language-suggestion").Length()) // the comment did render
			assert.Equal(t, 0, doc.Find("[data-suggestion-original]").Length())
		})
	})
}
````

````go
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
	"gitea.dev/modules/git"
	"gitea.dev/modules/gitrepo"
	pull_service "gitea.dev/services/pull"
	repo_service "gitea.dev/services/repository"
	files_service "gitea.dev/services/repository/files"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// fileLines returns "l1\n".."lN\n" with the given lines replaced
func fileLines(n int, replace map[int]string) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	for i := 1; i <= n; i++ {
		if s, ok := replace[i]; ok {
			sb.WriteString(s + "\n")
		} else {
			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "l%d\n", i)
		}
	}
	return sb.String()
}

func TestPullReviewRangeComment(t *testing.T) {
	onGiteaRun(t, func(t *testing.T, u *url.URL) {
		user2 := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
		repo, err := repo_service.CreateRepositoryDirectly(t.Context(), user2, user2, repo_service.CreateRepoOptions{
			Name:             "test_range",
			AutoInit:         true,
			Readme:           "Default",
			ObjectFormatName: git.Sha1ObjectFormat.Name(),
			DefaultBranch:    "master",
		}, true)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		writeFile := func(branch, newBranch, content string) {
			_, err := files_service.ChangeRepoFiles(t.Context(), repo, user2, &files_service.ChangeRepoFilesOptions{
				OldBranch: branch,
				NewBranch: newBranch,
				Files:     []*files_service.ChangeRepoFile{{Operation: "update", TreePath: "README.md", ContentReader: strings.NewReader(content)}},
			})
			require.NoError(t, err)
		}
		// lines 2 and 13 of 14 change, so the diff has two hunks: new lines 1-5 and 10-14
		writeFile("master", "", fileLines(14, nil))
		writeFile("master", "range-branch", fileLines(14, map[int]string{2: "X2", 13: "X13"}))

		session := loginUser(t, "user2")
		testPullCreate(t, session, "user2", "test_range", false, "master", "range-branch", "Range PR")
		pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{BaseRepoID: repo.ID, HeadBranch: "range-branch"})
		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))
		commentURL := fmt.Sprintf("/user2/test_range/pulls/%d/files/reviews/comments", pr.Issue.Index)

		post := func(t *testing.T, origin, side, startLine, line string, status int) *HTMLDoc {
			req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", commentURL, map[string]string{
				"origin":        origin,
				"content":       "```suggestion\nnew\n```",
				"side":          side,
				"start_line":    startLine,
				"line":          line,
				"path":          "README.md",
				"single_review": "true",
			})
			resp := session.MakeRequest(t, req, status)
			if status != http.StatusOK {
				return nil
			}
			return NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		}

		for _, origin := range []string{"diff", "timeline"} {
			t.Run("AC1 AC5 range on lines 1-3 from "+origin, func(t *testing.T) {
				doc := post(t, origin, "proposed", "1", "3", http.StatusOK)
				assert.Equal(t, "Lines 1–3", strings.TrimSpace(doc.Find(".code-comment-range").First().Text()))
				markup := doc.Find(".render-content.markup[data-suggestion-original]").Last()
				assert.Equal(t, "l1\nX2\nl3", markup.AttrOr("data-suggestion-original", ""))
			})
		}

		t.Run("AC3 one-line range is a single-line comment", func(t *testing.T) {
			doc := post(t, "diff", "proposed", "11", "11", http.StatusOK)
			assert.Equal(t, 0, doc.Find(".code-comment-range").Length())
			comment := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{IssueID: pr.IssueID, Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode, Line: 11})
			assert.EqualValues(t, 0, comment.RangeStartLine())
		})

		t.Run("AC12 invalid ranges are refused", func(t *testing.T) {
			before := unittest.GetCount(t, &issues_model.Comment{IssueID: pr.IssueID, Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode})
			post(t, "diff", "proposed", "4", "3", http.StatusBadRequest)   // start after end
			post(t, "diff", "previous", "1", "3", http.StatusBadRequest)   // old side
			post(t, "diff", "proposed", "4", "11", http.StatusBadRequest)  // two hunks
			post(t, "diff", "proposed", "7", "8", http.StatusBadRequest)   // between hunks, no hunk at all
			assert.Equal(t, before, unittest.GetCount(t, &issues_model.Comment{IssueID: pr.IssueID, Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode}))
		})

		gitRepo, err := gitrepo.OpenRepository(t.Context(), repo)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		defer gitRepo.Close()
		invalidate := func(t *testing.T) {
			require.NoError(t, pull_service.InvalidateCodeComments(t.Context(), issues_model.PullRequestList{pr}, user2, repo, gitRepo, "range-branch"))
		}
		post(t, "diff", "proposed", "", "2", http.StatusOK) // AC13: a single-line comment on line 2
		ranged := func() []*issues_model.Comment {
			var cs []*issues_model.Comment
			for _, c := range unittest.LoadBeansAndAssert[issues_model.Comment](t, &issues_model.Comment{IssueID: pr.IssueID, Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode}) {
				if c.RangeStartLine() > 0 || c.Line == 2 {
					cs = append(cs, c)
				}
			}
			return cs
		}

		t.Run("AC8 a change after the range keeps it current", func(t *testing.T) {
			writeFile("range-branch", "", fileLines(14, map[int]string{2: "X2", 13: "Y13"}))
			invalidate(t)
			for _, c := range ranged() {
				assert.False(t, c.Invalidated, "comment on line %d", c.Line)
			}
		})

		t.Run("AC7 AC13 a change inside the range makes it outdated", func(t *testing.T) {
			writeFile("range-branch", "", fileLines(14, map[int]string{2: "Y2", 13: "Y13"}))
			invalidate(t)
			cs := ranged()
			require.Len(t, cs, 3) // two range comments and the single-line one
			for _, c := range cs {
				assert.True(t, c.Invalidated, "comment on line %d", c.Line)
			}
		})
	})
}
````

````text
| `docs/testing.md` | authoritative test documentation; this doc summarises it |

## Conventions & invariants

- A Go package whose tests touch the database needs a `main_test.go` containing
  `func TestMain(m *testing.M) { unittest.MainTest(m) }`. Without it the test DB is never
  initialised.
- Every DB-backed test calls `unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()` first, which reloads the fixtures, so
  tests do not depend on each other's writes.
- Adding a row to `models/fixtures/*.yml` means keeping denormalised counter columns
  (`num_issues`, `num_closed_issues`, ...) consistent, or `CheckConsistencyFor` fails.
- Handler tests use `contexttest.MockContext` rather than constructing a `context.Context`
  by hand — see `services/context` for what the real one carries.
- Integration tests need Git LFS installed. The database comes from `GITEA_TEST_DATABASE`; empty
  defaults to SQLite, which is what you want locally.
- Frontend tests are Vitest, not Jest. Playwright is only for the e2e tier.

## Recipes

**Run one test.**

```sh
go test -run '^TestName$' ./modulepath/   # or: make test-backend#TestName
pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>
GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='<filepath>' make test-e2e
```

**Add a DB-backed unit test.** Put `*_test.go` beside the code; add `main_test.go` with
`unittest.MainTest(m)` if the package has none; call `unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()`; load rows
with `unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean`; add fixture rows only if no existing row fits.
````
</details></tool-use>

```text
## The guide layer (rules 16-22)

`guide/` holds a plain-English page for each reference page in `docs/`, same filename. It exists so
a person new to Go and to this codebase can get oriented. It is **derived**, not independent.

16. Every guide carries `source:`, `source-hash:` and `verified-at:` in its frontmatter **[checked]**.
17. A guide's `source:` names a real `docs/*.md` with the **same filename** **[checked]**.
18. `source-hash:` is the first 16 characters of `sha256sum docs/<name>.md`. If the reference page
    changes and the guide is not regenerated, `check.sh` reports **drift** **[checked]**. Regenerating
    means: reread the reference page, rewrite the guide, update the hash and `verified-at`.
19. Guide headings match `guide/_TEMPLATE.md` exactly and in order **[checked]**.
20. Guides are capped at **200 lines**, code fences at **30** **[checked]** — teaching needs more room
    than reference does.
21. **A guide adds explanation, vocabulary and worked steps. It adds no new facts.** Every repo path
    a guide cites must also be cited by its source page **[checked]**. If you need a fact the
    reference page lacks, add it *there* first, which bumps the hash and forces the guide to be
    regenerated in the same commit — exactly the intended order.
22. `guide/START-HERE.md` has no source page. It is exempt from rules 17, 18 and 21, and is where
    cross-cutting material lives that no single reference page owns.

**Never fix a fact in `guide/`.** If the two layers disagree, the reference page is the truth and
the guide is stale: fix `docs/`, regenerate the guide, ship both in one PR. A disagreement is a bug
report against `docs/`, not an editing job in `guide/`.
  Closing (`SetIssueAsClosed`, `models/issues/issue_update.go`) skips dependencies the same way and
  otherwise uses `IssueNoDependenciesLeft`, where a closed pull request counts as done. Changing one
  rule does not change the other.
- **Review comments are anchored to a commit, not to a line of the current head.** `CreateCodeComment`
  takes `latestCommitID` and a `treePath`; when the branch moves, `InvalidateCodeComments` marks
  the ones that no longer apply. A comment feature that stores only a line number will drift.
- `GetDiffForRender` and `GetDiffForAPI` are deliberately separate — the render path carries
  highlighting, escaping and a repo link for building URLs. Do not use the API one to build HTML.
- `notify_service.*` is called after the transaction, exactly as in `services-issue.md`.

## Recipes
AI-ASSISTANCE.md
COURSE-WORKFLOW.md
INDEX.md
MAINTENANCE.md
README.md
_TEMPLATE.md
check.sh
docs
guide
```

```markdown
Closes #158

## What changed

A reviewer can now comment on a range of new-side lines in Files changed. Click a line number, shift-click another in the same hunk, then click `+` on the last line of the range. The comment form and the posted thread are headed "Lines 18–22". "Suggest change" pre-fills every line of the range, and a suggestion renders with all the range's lines removed.

- **Storage:** the range start is `StartLine` in the comment's existing `CommentMetaData` JSON field. `Line` stays the range end, so thread placement, replies, the API and old rows are unchanged. No migration. `Comment.RangeStartLine()` and `Comment.RangeOriginalLines()` are the helpers S3/S6/S7 can use.
- **Server (`services/pull/review.go`):**
  - `CreateCodeComment` takes a `startLine`.
  - For a range it stores the hunk up to the range end and refuses (`ErrCodeCommentRangeInvalid` → 400) a range that isn't on the new side of one hunk.
  - A reply inherits its thread's range.
- **Invalidation:** a range comment goes Outdated when the text of any line in its range changed at the new head (`checkRangeInvalidation`). Single-line comments keep the existing blame check.
- **Frontend:**
  - `repo-diff-range.ts` handles click / shift-click on new-side line numbers and refuses selections across hunks, expanded context or sides, with a toast.
  - The `+` handler fetches the form with `start_line`/`line`, and the template renders the header.
  - S2's `initSuggestChangeButton` takes the range's lines.
  - S1's renderer splits the original on `\n`.

## Why

Reviewers could only suggest single-line changes. This covers #158 AC1–AC13. Apply-a-range was moved out of scope to S3 #156 / S6 #159 (see the spec discussion on the issue).

## Test Evidence

See the Design Decision and Decision 2 in #158. The start line is stored in `CommentMetaData` instead of a new column, and range invalidation compares text.
```

# Ponytail

You are a lazy senior developer. The best code is the code never written. You solve the whole problem with the least new code. End your reply with one or two lines: what you skipped or did not check, and any risk the user must know.

Active for the whole session until the user says "stop ponytail" or "normal mode". Switch level: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.

## Before you write

Read the task and the code it touches. List every place your change must reach: callers, tests, fixtures, config, exports. Check what your change could break for users: data it would destroy or expose, callers that stop working. That is scope. Extra features are not.

## The smallest complete change

Take the first option that fully works:

1. Does it need to exist? Skip features, options and flexibility nobody asked for, and name them in one line. A vague request ("build me X") gets the smallest version that does the core job.
2. Already in this codebase (a helper, component, service, pattern)? Use it the way the surrounding code does.
3. Standard library or a platform feature? Use it, unless the project has its own. A house component beats a native widget.
4. An installed dependency? Use it. Never add a dependency for a few lines.
5. Can it be one line a reader gets at a glance? One line.
6. Otherwise: the minimum code that works.

- Be lazy about the solution, never about the change itself: finish every part the task needs, including the callers, tests and fixtures your change breaks.
- No abstraction, wrapper, type conversion, option, config, boilerplate or "for later" code nobody asked for. Keep values in the form the platform already gives you. Deletion beats addition. Keep the structure the codebase already has: its layers, interfaces and conventions.
- The shortest working diff wins, once you know everything it must touch. A one-liner that needs decoding is not short.
- Comment only the why the code cannot show, in one line.
- Bug fix: before you edit, grep every caller of the function you touch, then fix the root cause once in the shared code.
- Code you move or merge keeps its error handling and validation.
- Between options of equal size, take the one that is correct on edge cases.
- Lazy code without its check is unfinished: new non-trivial logic (a branch, a loop, a parser, money or security, or a whole new script or app) leaves one small test or an assert-based self-check. Trivial changes need none.
- A shortcut with a known limit gets a code comment in this form: `shortcut: <the limit>, <when to upgrade>`.

Never cut: validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs, anything the user asked for.

## Levels

| Level | Behavior |
|-------|----------|
| **lite** | Build what was asked. Name the smaller option in one line and let the user pick. |
| **full** | The rules above. Default. |
| **ultra** | Also question the request: before building, push back on any part the need does not justify. |

Review a change like the senior developer who will be paged when it breaks.
Order of importance: correct, safe, holds under load, tested, fast, lean.
Lean still matters: every extra line must be read, tested and fixed later.
This is a report the user asked for, so give it in full.

## 1. Understand first

- Review what the user names: uncommitted or staged changes, a branch, a PR
  link, or files. Nothing named: the uncommitted changes, or the last commit
  if there are none.
- Read the diff, then the code it touches: callers of every changed function,
  the functions it calls, the tests, the README.
- Trace the real flow: where data comes in, what is stored, what goes out.
- A change can break code it does not touch. When a signature, return value
  or behavior changes, grep every caller.
- Find the expected load in the repo (README, deploy config): one person
  running a script, or many users and processes at once. Judge scale against
  that, and say which load you assumed.

## 2. Look for

1. **Bug:** wrong result, crash, missed edge case (empty, zero, last item,
   rounding, time zones), a caller broken by the change, a fix applied in one
   caller while the shared function stays broken.
2. **Risk:** security holes (injection, weak randomness, secrets, missing
   checks on input from users), data loss (errors swallowed, writes in the
   wrong order, no transaction).
3. **Scale:** fine for one user, wrong for many: check-then-write races, the
   same work done by every process, memory or lists that only grow, a query
   per item, O(n^2) on big input, per-process state that must be shared.
4. **Missing test:** risky new logic (a branch, a parser, money, security,
   data writes, a bug fix) with no test that fails when it breaks. One good
   test, not coverage.
5. **Speed:** big slowdowns are problems. Small wins (work repeated in a hot
   loop) are suggestions; some software counts every millisecond.
6. **Lean:** code that should not exist or should be smaller.
   - delete: dead code, unused options, speculative features
   - reuse: the repo already has this helper (name the path)
   - stdlib / native: the standard library or platform already does it; a
     new dependency for a few lines
   - yagni: abstraction with one implementation, config nobody sets
   - merge: near-copies that must change together
   - split: one function doing several unrelated jobs, so it is hard to read
     or test. Split by job, never by line count, and never into helpers that
     exist only to make a function shorter.

## 3. Check before you report

- Every finding needs a concrete case: "this input or situation leads to this
  wrong result". No case, no finding.
- Re-read the lines and confirm: the caller exists, the value can really be
  empty, the code really is unused.
- A shortcut marked with a `shortcut:` (or older `ponytail:`) comment that names its limit is a
  decision, not a finding, unless the expected load already crosses it.
- Propose the smallest fix that works. Prefer fixes that delete code. Never
  add layers, frameworks or config the problem does not need.
- No style taste, no "consider", no vague worries.

## 4. Output

Very simple English: short sentences, everyday words. Explain a technical
term the first time you use it. The reader may never have seen this code.

Start with `What this change does:` in two or three sentences.

Then the findings in three groups, skip empty groups:
- **Must fix:** bug, security, data loss, breaks at the expected load.
- **Should fix:** risky code without a test, real slowness, duplication, a
  function that mixes jobs, code that should not exist.
- **Nice to have:** small speed-ups, shorter forms.

Number findings across all groups, so the user can say "fix 2 and 5".
Every finding has all four parts, each one or two short sentences:

2. **Orders land on the wrong day** (`billing/close_day.py:L40-52`)
   - **What this is:** At midnight this job closes the day and bills all orders of that day.
   - **Problem:** It takes "today" from the server clock, which runs in UTC. An order placed
     at 00:30 in Berlin is billed on the day before.
   - **Fix:** Compute the day once in the shop's time zone:
     `datetime.now(ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin")).date()`. One line, nothing else changes.
   - **If we skip it:** Late orders show the wrong date, and accounting fixes them by hand.

End with:
- `Verdict: Ship.` or `Verdict: fix 1 and 3 first.`
- `Lean: -<N> lines possible.` when lean findings exist.
- `Not checked:` one line, if something mattered and you could not check it.

Nothing found: `What this change does:`, then `Looks good. Ship.` and one line
on what you checked.

Lists findings, changes no code.

```text
 // SuggestionOriginalLine returns the commented line as the reviewer saw it: the last line of the
 // stored patch, since CutDiffAroundLine stops right after the commented line.
+// For a multi-line comment it returns every line of the range, joined by "\n".
 // Old-side comments return None until #151 decides whether they may carry suggestions.
 func (c *Comment) SuggestionOriginalLine() optional.Option[string] {
 	if c.Type != CommentTypeCode || c.Line <= 0 {
 		return optional.None[string]()
 	}
+	if c.RangeStartLine() > 0 {
+		lines, ok := c.RangeOriginalLines()
+		if !ok {
+			return optional.None[string]()
+		}
+		return optional.Some(strings.Join(lines, "\n"))
+	}
 	patch := strings.TrimRight(c.Patch, "\n")
 	last := patch[strings.LastIndexByte(patch, '\n')+1:]
 	if last == "" || (last[0] != '+' && last[0] != ' ') {
@@ -23,3 +31,30 @@ func (c *Comment) SuggestionOriginalLine() optional.Option[string] {
 	}
 	return optional.Some(last[1:])
 }
+
+// RangeOriginalLines returns lines RangeStartLine..Line of a multi-line code comment as the
+// reviewer saw them, false if the stored patch doesn't hold all of them.
+func (c *Comment) RangeOriginalLines() ([]string, bool) {
+	start := c.RangeStartLine()
+	if start <= 0 || c.Line < start {
+		return nil, false
+	}
+	return PatchLastNewLines(c.Patch, int(c.Line-start+1))
+}
+
+// PatchLastNewLines returns the last n new-side lines of a one-hunk patch, which end at the
+// commented line, skipping removed lines. False if the hunk has fewer than n.
+func PatchLastNewLines(patch string, n int) ([]string, bool) {
+	rows := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(patch, "\n"), "\n")
+	lines := make([]string, n)
+	for i := len(rows) - 1; i >= 0 && n > 0; i-- {
+		switch {
+		case rows[i] == "" || rows[i][0] == '@':
+			return nil, false // reached the hunk header
+		case rows[i][0] == '+' || rows[i][0] == ' ':
+			n--
+			lines[n] = rows[i][1:]
+		}
+	}
+	return lines, n == 0
+}

+func TestCommentSuggestionOriginalLineRange(t *testing.T) {
+	const header = "diff --git a/main.go b/main.go\n--- a/main.go\n+++ b/main.go\n@@ -16,6 +16,7 @@\n"
+	// new-side lines 16..22; the removed line between 19 and 20 is not part of the range
+	const patch = header + " l16\n l17\n l18\n+\tl19\n-old\n l20\n+l21\n l22"
+	cases := []struct {
+		name     string
+		start    int64
+		line     int64
+		patch    string
+		expected optional.Option[string]
+	}{
+		{"lines 18-22 in order, removed line skipped", 18, 22, patch, optional.Some("l18\n\tl19\nl20\nl21\nl22")},
+		{"range reaching the hunk start", 16, 22, patch, optional.Some("l16\nl17\nl18\n\tl19\nl20\nl21\nl22")},
+		{"range longer than the stored hunk", 15, 22, patch, optional.None[string]()},
+		{"no newline at end of file marker", 21, 22, patch + "\n\\ No newline at end of file", optional.Some("l21\nl22")},
+		{"empty patch", 18, 22, "", optional.None[string]()},
+	}
+	for _, c := range cases {
+		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			comment := &issues_model.Comment{
+				Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode, Line: c.line, Patch: c.patch,
+				CommentMetaData: &issues_model.CommentMetaData{StartLine: c.start},
+			}
+			assert.Equal(t, c.expected, comment.SuggestionOriginalLine())
+		})
+	}
+}

+// checkRangeInvalidation invalidates a multi-line comment when any line of its range changed text at the branch head.
+// One CommitSHA can't hold a blame per line, so ranges compare text instead.
+func checkRangeInvalidation(ctx context.Context, c *issues_model.Comment, gitRepo *git.Repository, branch string) error {
+	original, ok := c.RangeOriginalLines()
+	if !ok {
+		return nil // no snippet to compare with, as for a comment created without a review
+	}
+	commit, err := gitRepo.GetBranchCommit(branch)
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	content, err := commit.GetFileContent(c.TreePath, 0)
+	if err != nil && !git.IsErrNotExist(err) {
+		return err
+	}
+	if rangeChanged(original, content, c.RangeStartLine()) {
+		c.Invalidated = true
+		return issues_model.UpdateCommentInvalidate(ctx, c)
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// rangeChanged reports whether content no longer has the original lines starting at line start.
+func rangeChanged(original []string, content string, start int64) bool {
+	lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(content, "\n"), "\n")
+	if content == "" {
+		lines = nil
+	}
+	end := int(start) - 1 + len(original)
+	return end > len(lines) || !slices.Equal(lines[start-1:end], original)
+}

import {addDelegatedEventListener} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import {showErrorToast} from '../modules/toast.ts';

let anchor: {tr: HTMLElement, side: string} | null = null;
let selected: HTMLElement[] = [];

function newLineNum(tr: Element): number {
  return Number(tr.querySelector('td.lines-num-new')?.getAttribute('data-line-num') || 0);
}

/** the new-side rows from `a` to `b` in either order, or null when they aren't in one hunk */
export function collectRangeRows(a: HTMLElement, b: HTMLElement): HTMLElement[] | null {
  const [first, last] = a.compareDocumentPosition(b) & Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_PRECEDING ? [b, a] : [a, b];
  const rows: HTMLElement[] = [];
  for (let tr: Element | null = first; tr; tr = tr.nextElementSibling) {
    // a hunk header, or expanded context which belongs to no hunk
    if (tr.classList.contains('tag-code') || tr.classList.contains('line-expanded')) return null;
    if (newLineNum(tr)) rows.push(tr as HTMLElement); // skips removed lines and comment rows
    if (tr === last) return rows;
  }
  return null; // `last` isn't after `first` in this file
}

function setSelected(rows: HTMLElement[]) {
  for (const tr of selected) tr.classList.remove('range-selected');
  selected = rows;
  for (const tr of selected) tr.classList.add('range-selected');
}

/** the selected range, when `tr` is its last row and it has more than one line */
export function getSelectedRange(tr: Element): {rows: HTMLElement[], start: number, end: number} | null {
  if (selected.length < 2 || selected.at(-1) !== tr) return null;
  return {rows: selected, start: newLineNum(selected[0]), end: newLineNum(tr)};
}

// click a line number to start a range, shift-click another to end it
export function initDiffRangeSelect() {
  addDelegatedEventListener(document, 'click', '[data-range-invalid] td.lines-num[data-line-num]:not([data-line-num=""])', (td, e: MouseEvent) => {
    const tr = td.closest('tr')!;
    const side = td.classList.contains('lines-num-new') ? 'right' : 'left';
    if (!e.shiftKey || !anchor) {
      anchor = {tr, side};
      setSelected(side === 'right' ? [tr] : []);
      return;
    }
    window.getSelection()?.removeAllRanges();
    const rows = anchor.side === 'right' && side === 'right' ? collectRangeRows(anchor.tr, tr) : null;
    if (!rows) {
      anchor = null;
      setSelected([]);
      showErrorToast(td.closest('[data-range-invalid]')!.getAttribute('data-range-invalid')!);
      return;
    }
    setSelected(rows);
  });
}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-13 01:14:54Z)**_

**What this change does:** Reviewers can pick a range of new-side lines in a PR's Files changed tab: click one line number, then shift-click another. The comment then covers the whole range. The first line of the range is saved in the comment's existing JSON metadata field. The server checks that the range sits on the new side of one hunk, "Suggest change" pre-fills every line, and suggestions render with all the range's lines removed. A range comment goes Outdated when the text of any line in it changes.

I assumed the expected load is a small course team.

**Should fix**

1. **A refused range fails silently in the browser** (`web_src/js/features/repo-diff.ts:54-56`)
   - **What this is:** When you submit a comment, the page posts the form and swaps the response HTML in where the form was.
   - **Problem:** A range refusal from the server is a 400 with a JSON body, not HTML. The JS never checks the response status and tries to read the JSON as HTML. That throws an error and the form just stays there with no message. It can really happen:
     - The diff is shown with "ignore whitespace" from the whitespace dropdown, or for a single commit. Its hunks then differ from the full PR diff the server checks against.
     - Someone pushed to the branch since the page was loaded.
   - **Fix:** Before parsing the response, add `if (!response.ok) { showErrorToast((await response.json()).errorMessage); return; }`. That's about three lines, the same idea as `repo-issue.ts:379`.
   - **If we skip it:** The reviewer clicks "Add single comment", nothing happens, and they never see the AC10 message.

**Nice to have**

2. **Invalidation re-reads the branch and the whole file for every range comment** (`services/pull/review.go` `checkRangeInvalidation`)
   - **What this is:** After each push, every open range comment on the PR is checked against the new head.
   - **Problem:** Each comment looks up the branch commit again and reads the entire file with no size limit. For example, 50 range comments on a 5 MB file means about 250 MB read per push.
   - **Fix:** Look up the branch commit once in `InvalidateCodeComments` and pass it in. Reading only up to the range end would cut the rest.
   - **If we skip it:** It's fine for a class project. Very large files with many range comments would make pushes slower.

3. **Range selection is mouse-only** (`web_src/js/features/repo-diff-range.ts`)
   - **What this is:** A range is started and ended by clicking line-number cells, which keyboard focus can't reach.
   - **Problem:** A keyboard-only reviewer can't make a range comment. Single-line comments through the `+` button still work. The existing file-view line selection in `repo-code.ts` has the same limit.
   - **Fix:** Give the new-side line-number cells `tabindex="0"` and treat Enter / Shift+Enter like a click.
   - **If we skip it:** Range comments stay mouse-only, the same as the file view today.

Verdict: fix 1 first.

Not checked: whether a reviewer can add a comment at all while viewing a single commit or with whitespace ignored, which is the main way to hit finding 1. I inferred it from the whitespace dropdown and single-commit view in `box.tmpl` but didn't try it.

Review a change like the senior developer who will be paged when it breaks.
Order of importance: correct, safe, holds under load, tested, fast, lean.
Lean still matters: every extra line must be read, tested and fixed later.
This is a report the user asked for, so give it in full.

## 1. Understand first

- Review what the user names: uncommitted or staged changes, a branch, a PR
  link, or files. Nothing named: the uncommitted changes, or the last commit
  if there are none.
- Read the diff, then the code it touches: callers of every changed function,
  the functions it calls, the tests, the README.
- Trace the real flow: where data comes in, what is stored, what goes out.
- A change can break code it does not touch. When a signature, return value
  or behavior changes, grep every caller.
- Find the expected load in the repo (README, deploy config): one person
  running a script, or many users and processes at once. Judge scale against
  that, and say which load you assumed.

## 2. Look for

1. **Bug:** wrong result, crash, missed edge case (empty, zero, last item,
   rounding, time zones), a caller broken by the change, a fix applied in one
   caller while the shared function stays broken.
2. **Risk:** security holes (injection, weak randomness, secrets, missing
   checks on input from users), data loss (errors swallowed, writes in the
   wrong order, no transaction).
3. **Scale:** fine for one user, wrong for many: check-then-write races, the
   same work done by every process, memory or lists that only grow, a query
   per item, O(n^2) on big input, per-process state that must be shared.
4. **Missing test:** risky new logic (a branch, a parser, money, security,
   data writes, a bug fix) with no test that fails when it breaks. One good
   test, not coverage.
5. **Speed:** big slowdowns are problems. Small wins (work repeated in a hot
   loop) are suggestions; some software counts every millisecond.
6. **Lean:** code that should not exist or should be smaller.
   - delete: dead code, unused options, speculative features
   - reuse: the repo already has this helper (name the path)
   - stdlib / native: the standard library or platform already does it; a
     new dependency for a few lines
   - yagni: abstraction with one implementation, config nobody sets
   - merge: near-copies that must change together
   - split: one function doing several unrelated jobs, so it is hard to read
     or test. Split by job, never by line count, and never into helpers that
     exist only to make a function shorter.

## 3. Check before you report

- Every finding needs a concrete case: "this input or situation leads to this
  wrong result". No case, no finding.
- Re-read the lines and confirm: the caller exists, the value can really be
  empty, the code really is unused.
- A shortcut marked with a `shortcut:` (or older `ponytail:`) comment that names its limit is a
  decision, not a finding, unless the expected load already crosses it.
- Propose the smallest fix that works. Prefer fixes that delete code. Never
  add layers, frameworks or config the problem does not need.
- No style taste, no "consider", no vague worries.

## 4. Output

Very simple English: short sentences, everyday words. Explain a technical
term the first time you use it. The reader may never have seen this code.

Start with `What this change does:` in two or three sentences.

Then the findings in three groups, skip empty groups:
- **Must fix:** bug, security, data loss, breaks at the expected load.
- **Should fix:** risky code without a test, real slowness, duplication, a
  function that mixes jobs, code that should not exist.
- **Nice to have:** small speed-ups, shorter forms.

Number findings across all groups, so the user can say "fix 2 and 5".
Every finding has all four parts, each one or two short sentences:

2. **Orders land on the wrong day** (`billing/close_day.py:L40-52`)
   - **What this is:** At midnight this job closes the day and bills all orders of that day.
   - **Problem:** It takes "today" from the server clock, which runs in UTC. An order placed
     at 00:30 in Berlin is billed on the day before.
   - **Fix:** Compute the day once in the shop's time zone:
     `datetime.now(ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin")).date()`. One line, nothing else changes.
   - **If we skip it:** Late orders show the wrong date, and accounting fixes them by hand.

End with:
- `Verdict: Ship.` or `Verdict: fix 1 and 3 first.`
- `Lean: -<N> lines possible.` when lean findings exist.
- `Not checked:` one line, if something mattered and you could not check it.

Nothing found: `What this change does:`, then `Looks good. Ship.` and one line
on what you checked.

Lists findings, changes no code.

```text
function initRepoDiffConversationForm() {

  addDelegatedEventListener<HTMLFormElement, SubmitEvent>(document, 'submit', '.conversation-holder form', async (form, e) => {

    if (!validateTextareaNonEmpty(textArea)) return;

      // if the form is submitted by a button, append the button's name and value to the form data
      const submitter = e.submitter;
      const isSubmittedByButton = submitter instanceof HTMLButtonElement || (submitter instanceof HTMLInputElement && submitter.type === 'submit');

      const response = await POST(form.getAttribute('action')!, {data: formData});
      const newConversationHolder = createElementFromHTML(await response.text());

    const params = new URLSearchParams();
    params.append('title', title?.startsWith(wipPrefix) ? title.slice(wipPrefix.length).trim() : `${wipPrefix.trim()} ${title}`);
    const response = await POST(updateUrl, {data: params});
    if (!response.ok) {
      showErrorToast(`Failed to toggle 'work in progress' status`);
      return;
    }
    window.location.reload();
```
